reproducer: `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP('',#OPEN_SHELL_REF);` with `VERTEX_POINT.tolerance > EDGE_CURVE.tolerance`; coordinates in the range 0.001 with mm declared.
title: Open shell as MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP.outer × tolerance-violation × unit mismatch

description: A face on a `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` has a wire that self-intersects in UV near the seam line (u=0 / u=2π). The seam edge is missing; what should be a single edge along the seam appears as two separate edges, neither shared. The pcurve self-intersection happens exactly at u=2π (a parametric ambiguity). All three are interactions between the periodic surface's UV space and the wire's combinatorics.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: seam-edge synthesis policy (synthesize / repair), UV-shift policy (normalize), self-intersection resolution (heal); all three engage.
reproducer: cylinder, face wire of 4 edges crossing the seam; the crossover is a self-intersection in UV; no seam edge listed.
title: Self-intersecting wire on cylindrical (periodic) face × seam-edge missing

description: `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` references `DIRECTION('',(0.,0.,0.))` (zero-magnitude direction). The placement also references `#999` for its origin; an entity that itself transitively references back to the placement (cycle). Forward reference, cycle, and direction-degeneracy combine.
expected_kernel_behavior: cycle, forward-resolution, and direction-degeneracy each independently rejected/repaired.
title: Forward reference × cyclic reference × invalid axis-placement

description: A `GEOMETRIC_SET` has an empty items list. A separate `CARTESIAN_POINT` carries coordinates `(1.0e308, 0.0, 0.0)`. A third `CARTESIAN_POINT` has a NaN component (parsed from textual `NaN` or produced by underflow). The kernel must decide each: empty, gigantic, not-a-number.
expected_kernel_behavior: each anomaly addressed independently — empty-aggregate policy, extreme-magnitude clamp/reject, NaN-detection.
reproducer: `#10=GEOMETRIC_SET('',());` `#11=CARTESIAN_POINT('',(1.0E308,0.,0.));` `#12=CARTESIAN_POINT('',(NaN,0.,0.));` (textual `NaN` literal, which itself is non-conforming for ISO-10303-21 REAL).
title: Empty geometric-set × extreme coordinates × NaN component

description: A `geometric_tolerance` references a `shape_aspect` that is forward-referenced (`#999` → not yet defined at the point of use, but defined later in the file). The PMI is meant to be visible in a saved view, but the `draughting_model.items` list is missing the `mapped_item`. The whole assembly's `GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT` declares mm but PMI text values are emitted assuming inches.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept, or warn and accept: PMI ordering invariant, saved-view link invariant, and unit-consistency invariant each addressed independently; normalize where possible, warn otherwise.
reproducer: usual PMI scaffolding plus three independent defects: forward-reference shape_aspect, missing mapped_item, mm context with inch-magnitude PMI value.
title: PMI without saved-view × unit-system mismatch × forward references

description: The file has two `DATA` sections. Both define `#10` (with different bodies). One section references `@otherSection#10` (cross- section reference syntax). The behavior under the spec is ambiguous — multi-DATA is permitted in Edition 3 with explicit naming, but anonymous DATA blocks are not, and duplicated IDs across blocks must be resolved.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept, or reject with E_DUPLICATE_ID / E_BAD_CROSS_REF diagnostic: multi-DATA policy normalizes the section choice, duplicate-ID resolution coerces / repairs IDs, cross-section-ref handling resolves references. Each independent.
reproducer: two `DATA;`/`ENDSEC;` blocks, both defining `#10`, with one entity citing `@s2#10`.
title: Multiple DATA sections × duplicated entity ID × cross-section reference

description: A `TESSELLATED_FACE` and an `ADVANCED_FACE` both represent halves of one through-hole. PMI `dimensional_size` (a diameter) cites a `shape_aspect` bound to both faces via two `geometric_item_specific_usage` records, but no style-binding exists for the tessellated face. The `LENGTH_UNIT` says inches, but a separate `PLANE_ANGLE_UNIT` is missing and the PMI text value carries the diameter in mm.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept, or warn and accept: style-binding policy normalizes the binding, PMI cross-kind resolution coerces / repairs the link, mixed-unit policy normalizes the units.
reproducer: BRep half-cylinder face + tessellated half-cylinder triangulation; PMI binding spans both; missing `STYLED_ITEM` for the tess; mixed-unit context.
title: Tessellated face × BRep face sharing PMI × unit-system inch/mm collision

description: A face on a closed `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` is bounded by three edges. Edge[1].end ≠ Edge[2].start (gap of 0.5 in 3D, far above any reasonable tolerance). The pcurves are absent. The wire's 3D path also wraps around the cylinder (covers > one period in U). All three classes interact on the same wire.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept, or reject with E_CONNECTEDNESS / E_MISSING_PCURVE diagnostic: connectedness invariant, pcurve-existence invariant, and period-spanning invariant each addressed; repair where possible, otherwise reject.
reproducer: cylinder; face wire with three open edges, gaps, no pcurves, total U-extent > 2π.
title: Disconnected EDGE_LOOP × pcurve missing × wire bypassing seam

description: A `TOROIDAL_SURFACE` has `major_radius = -10.0` (vendor flip) and `minor_radius = 1.0`. A face on it has a seam edge whose 3D-curve identical-vertex check is exactly at the kernel's working precision (the two endpoint coordinates differ by exactly 1e-7). The seam edge appears in the loop twice (once forward, once reverse), forming a cycle. Three time-bomb / vendor / topology defects.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept, or warn and accept: vendor-radius policy normalizes the radius, tolerance-boundary policy decides at the boundary, repeated-seam invariant coerces / repairs the seam; each independently.
reproducer: torus with negative major radius; seam edge with 3D length 1e-7; loop = `(seam_fwd, other, seam_rev, other2)` such that the seam edge appears doubled.
title: Time-bomb tolerance × negative-radius torus × cyclic seam edge

description: One fixture combines two parser-stressing patterns. (1) A `LIST_OF_LIST_OF_INTEGER` attribute is built as a deeply nested parenthesised aggregate, around 60 open parens deep; a recursive descent parser hits stack-overflow before reaching the inner literals. (2) A `PRODUCT.name` carries a string literal exceeding the Edition-3 32 769-octet cap by ten times; a parser using a fixed-size string buffer truncates or overruns. Combined: the parser may segfault on the deep-nesting path before it reaches the overlong literal, hiding the second defect; or it may allocate an oversized string, then segfault on the deep aggregate, hiding which root cause was hit first. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file kills my parser two ways", "deep nesting plus huge string", "stack overflow then OOM".
expected_kernel_behavior: cap recursion depth and string-literal length on input; reject either pattern with a precise diagnostic naming which budget was exceeded; the order of diagnostics across the two defects is documented.
notes: **See also**: Pf012.
reproducer: a `LIST_OF_LIST_OF_INTEGER` attribute spelled as `((((((((((((((( .. 1 .. ))))))))))))))))` (60+ levels deep); a `PRODUCT.name` whose string literal is 327 690 characters of `'A'` (10× the ISO cap).
title: Deeply nested aggregate × overlong string literal in one fixture (Pf × Ad cross-product)

description: One fixture combines three topology defects across the BREP_WITH_VOIDS / shared-shell / tessellated-topology axes. (1) A `BREP_WITH_VOIDS` carries an inner shell that pokes through the outer shell along Z. (2) The outer shell is referenced from a second `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` in the same SHAPE_REPRESENTATION (shell aliasing). (3) A parallel `TESSELLATED_SHELL_REPRESENTATION` carries faces that mix shell-level and per-face COORDINATES_LIST without consistent connectivity. Receivers diverge on which defect to surface first. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file fails three ways at once", "void escapes part AND shell shared AND tessellated mismatch".
expected_kernel_behavior: each defect surfaced independently; the order of diagnostics is documented; the kernel does not silently accept any one defect because the others are louder.
notes: **See also**: Tsh065, Tsh066, Tsh067. **OCC behavior**: accepts and loads shape(1); catalog disallows silent-accept. Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers enforcing the spec must reject (or surface a diagnostic); silent acceptance defeats the catalog's stated invariant.
reproducer: outer cube CLOSED_SHELL `#100` of 10×10×10 mm; inner pin CLOSED_SHELL `#101` of 2×2×15 mm centred on cube centre (pokes ±2.5 mm); BREP_WITH_VOIDS `#200` referencing `#100` and `#101`; a second MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP `#201` referencing the same outer shell `#100`; alongside, a TESSELLATED_SHELL_REPRESENTATION `#300` with mixed shell-level and per-face node lists.
title: Tessellated topology × shared shell × void containment in one fixture

description: A STEP-exported assembly carries ITEM_DEFINED_TRANSFORMATION entities where every NEXT_ASSEMBLY_USAGE_OCCURRENCE references the same identity AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D. The receiver's instance-positioning relies on per-NAUO transforms; with all transforms identity, every child renders at world origin. Onshape's writer apparently embedded child placements into the child's own SHAPE_REPRESENTATION items list rather than into the relating transformation, which works for Onshape's reader but not SolidWorks/Inventor.
expected_kernel_behavior: the kernel must either (a) honour the per-NAUO transform exactly (children at world origin), surfacing a diagnostic that placements look suspicious; or (b) reject the file as ambiguous. Inventing placements from other entity references is not part of the spec.
notes: **See also**: P003. Synonyms: "STEP subassemblies snap to origin", "SolidWorks imports Onshape STEP all on top of each other", "child placements lost after round-trip", "identity IDT for every child", "assembly children stacked at origin".
reproducer: top-level PRODUCT_DEFINITION with two child PRODUCTs whose intended positions are (50, 0, 0) and (0, 75, 0) mm; both NAUOs reference an identity ITEM_DEFINED_TRANSFORMATION whose origin AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D is the world origin. PRODUCT.name carries the intended position as a string for diagnostic purposes.
sender: Onshape STEP exporter, round-tripped through SolidWorks 2021
sources: forum.onshape.com discussion 1355 "Missing parts in STEP file import in OS Assembly"
forum.kicad.info t/47681 "Wrong parts assignment when opening STEP files in Solidworks 2021"
bug-reporter language: "all parts ended up on top of each other at the origin", "subassembly placements just gone after round-trip".
title: Onshape→SolidWorks: assembly children snap to origin (placements lost)

description: Fusion 360 emits a STEP file with FILE_SCHEMA naming AP242 only. Receivers built for AP203/AP214 reject the file by schema name without parsing the data section. There is no fallback schema declaration in FILE_SCHEMA's aggregate. The fix in source applications is to switch the export to AP203 / AP214; the catalog records the reverse-direction defect of writers that emit AP242 by default with no compatibility alternative.
expected_kernel_behavior: receivers should ideally schema-fold AP242→AP214 for the geometry subset they recognise, surfacing a "schema downgrade applied" warning. Writers should emit FILE_SCHEMA with both AP242 and AP214 when the data is geometrically expressible in both.
notes: Synonyms: "Fusion STEP not opening in NX 12", "AP242 file too new for legacy CAD", "schema header rejects file before parsing", "no AP203/AP214 fallback in FILE_SCHEMA", "AP242 only schema causes import failure".
reproducer: FILE_SCHEMA(('AP242_MANAGED_MODEL_BASED_3D_ENGINEERING_MIM_LF { 1 0 10303 442 1 4 4 }')) with no AP203 or AP214 alternate listed in the schema aggregate; trivial DATA section with one ADVANCED_FACE.
sender: Fusion 360 STEP exporter (default AP242 since ~2022)

description: ISO 10303-21 §6.2 lets FILE_NAME's third argument hold the author list with no per-element length bound. Some writers (or pre-processing utilities) populate it (or a sibling header field) with the full source disk path; a UNC \\\\server\\share\\very\\long\\path; receivers that pre-allocate MAX_PATH=260 buffers for header parsing hang on the long string or repeatedly re-walk it during progress-bar updates, leading to the "stuck at 95%" symptom.
expected_kernel_behavior: cap the FILE_NAME first-arg length in the parser (treat as an opaque label, not a path); never hand it to the OS path-resolution APIs; emit warning W_LONG_HEADER_FIELD if length exceeds 1024.
notes: Synonyms: "STEP import stuck at 95 percent", "Inventor hangs on long file path", "FILE_NAME UNC path makes parser stall", "import progress bar hangs at end", "long path in STEP header".
reproducer: FILE_NAME third arg is an author list whose only element is a UNC path 350+ characters long (e.g. \\\\\\\\corp.example.com\\\\engineering\\\\projects\\\\..); rest of header standard; trivial DATA section.
sender: any STEP writer that puts the full source path in a FILE_NAME header field
sources: Autodesk KB sfdcarticles "A STEP file that gets stuck at 95 percent when attempting to import into Inventor"
Inventor forum 10165651 "STEP File import stuck at 95%"

description: A 6-face cube has only 5 ADVANCED_FACE entries (the +Z lid is missing); the file wraps them into an OPEN_SHELL inside a SHELL_BASED_SURFACE_MODEL. Onshape's importer (Parasolid kernel) loads the surface body but refuses to insert it into an assembly because surfaces are not assembly-valid children. Fusion 360 likewise yields a surface body. Users repeatedly post asking "why doesn't this open as a solid"; the upstream tool emitted a non-watertight body.
expected_kernel_behavior: load as a surface body and surface a "non-watertight body" diagnostic; offer auto-stitch / fill-hole as a healing option; filling in a missing face without diagnostic is outside the spec.
notes: Synonyms: "STEP imports as surface body only", "missing face means not a solid", "OPEN_SHELL where CLOSED_SHELL expected", "5-of-6 cube faces", "watertight body not constructed".
reproducer: 5 ADVANCED_FACE entries describing a unit cube minus the +Z face; OPEN_SHELL referencing all five; SHELL_BASED_SURFACE_MODEL referencing the OPEN_SHELL. No MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP.

description: A hole modelled in Onshape with a cosmetic thread (e.g. M3×0.5) exports as a plain CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE at the tap-drill diameter, with no helical curve, no thread_specification entity, and at most a free-form PROPERTY_DEFINITION carrying a string label. Receivers see a smooth hole; downstream BOM and fabrication processes lose the thread spec. AP242 supports thread metadata (thread_specification ARM) but Onshape's writer does not emit it.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: receivers should preserve the SHAPE_ASPECT and PROPERTY_DEFINITION as opaque metadata even when the parametric thread information is absent; writers should emit thread_specification when AP242 is the schema. Warn and accept with W_THREAD_METADATA_DROPPED when the metadata cannot be carried; rendering threaded holes as smooth cylinders without diagnostic is a coverage gap.
notes: Synonyms: "tapped hole exports as smooth cylinder", "thread spec lost in STEP", "cosmetic threads not in STEP file", "M3 thread becomes 2.5mm hole", "thread information dropped at export".
reproducer: CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE radius 1.25 mm (M3 tap-drill); SHAPE_ASPECT named 'M3x0p5_thread'; PROPERTY_DEFINITION carrying 'M3x0.5 - 6H - 8mm depth' as a free-form string; no helical curve, no thread_specification.

description: Inventor's STEP writer encodes string literals (PRODUCT.name, PERSON, etc.) using the Windows default codepage (GBK / Shift_JIS / EUC-KR) instead of the ISO 10303-21 \\X2\\ escape mechanism for codepoints outside ASCII. The bytes are syntactically valid (not high-bit characters in apostrophe / control runs), but they decode to mojibake on receivers that interpret the file as ISO-8859-1 (Edition 2 default) or UTF-8 (Edition 3 default).
expected_kernel_behavior: writers must emit \\X2\\HHHH\\X0\\ for any codepoint outside ASCII regardless of host OS locale; receivers that find raw high-bit runs should warn and apply edition-default decoding (UTF-8 / ISO-8859-1) without crashing.
notes: **See also**: Le002, Le021. Synonyms: "Chinese characters mojibake in STEP", "Inventor writes raw GBK bytes", "Korean names garbled after STEP round-trip", "CJK PRODUCT.name corrupt", "non-ASCII writer ignores X2 escape".
reproducer: PRODUCT.name carries raw multi-byte legacy-codepage content (e.g. byte sequence representing GBK 0xD6 0xD0 mis-recoded through Latin-1→UTF-8); intended Chinese characters '中文' should have been encoded as `\\X2\\4E2D6587\\X0\\`.
sender: Autodesk Inventor (some localisations) when source uses CJK names
sources: Autodesk KB sfdcarticles "STEP files converted in Inventor, do not display Chinese characters as expected"
Inventor forum 6686585 "How can I get Inventor to correctly translate Chinese Character"
bug-reporter language: "Chinese names show as gibberish", "Korean characters became a jumbled mess".
title: Inventor exports Asian (CJK) characters as raw legacy-codepage bytes

description: Two distinct PRODUCT_DEFINITIONs share the same PRODUCT.name (e.g. both labelled 'R0805', a common PCB resistor footprint). FreeCAD treats them as separate instances using the IDT (instance frame) for de-duplication; SolidWorks de-dups by PRODUCT.name and re-uses the first occurrence's geometry for all instances, effectively swapping parts between slots. Round-trip leaves the assembly visually scrambled.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: receivers must de-dup by PRODUCT_DEFINITION identity (entity reference), not by PRODUCT.name string equality. Writers should heal by emitting unique PRODUCT.names where possible, but receivers cannot rely on that. Name-keyed conflations that swap parts between assembly slots are a coverage gap.
notes: Synonyms: "duplicate PRODUCT name swaps parts", "Solidworks scrambles KiCad STEP imports", "same-name components conflate", "PRODUCT identity by name not entity", "PCB STEP imports wrong components".
reproducer: two PRODUCT entities both named 'R0805' but with distinct PRODUCT_DEFINITION_FORMATIONs and PRODUCT_DEFINITIONs; same PRODUCT_CONTEXT for both; ADVANCED_FACE shared (worsening the swap).
sender: KiCad PcbNew STEP exporter
sources: forum.kicad.info t/47681 "Wrong parts assignment when opening STEP files in Solidworks 2021"
t/46359 "STEP file corrupting on import to Solidworks (but not freecad)"
bug-reporter language: "in Solidworks several components were rotated and replaced by other components", "FreeCAD opens it fine but Solidworks scrambles the parts".
title: KiCad STEP imports cleanly in FreeCAD but corrupts in SolidWorks (PRODUCT.name de-dup)

description: A B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS has its first row of control points all coincident (4 CPs at the same location), creating a degenerate row. CATIA's writer accepts and emits the surface; downstream receivers either heal the row (treating it as a degenerate edge) or refuse the face. When the face is refused, the shell is incomplete, the solid never closes, and the result is an empty PartBody with the failed faces parked in geometric_sets.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect degenerate rows/columns at parse time; either contract them to a degenerate-edge representation or reject the surface with a clear diagnostic. Zero-area or self-overlapping geometry must not be produced without diagnostic.
notes: **See also**: Gn015. Synonyms: "CATIA degenerate spline", "empty PartBody after STEP import", "B-spline first row all coincident", "geometric_set debris", "solid not created CATIA Inventor".
reproducer: B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS degree (3, 3) with first row of 4 control points all at (0,0,0); second row scattered; uniform knot vector. Wrap into a single ADVANCED_FACE.
sender: CATIA V5 R25 / R26 STEP writer
sources: IBM APAR HC90888 "STEP : when importing a STEP file coming from CATIA V5, the solid is not created"
APAR HD91714 "STEP IMPORT: STEP FILE IS NOT CORRECTLY IMPORTED IN CATIA V5"

title: CATIA V5 degenerate B-spline surface → Inventor "empty PartBody"

description: A 360-degree cylindrical face is emitted as two 180-degree ADVANCED_FACE entries sharing a seam edge, each backed by its own CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE entity (same axis, same radius, complementary parameter ranges). Receivers expecting one periodic face emit "non-merged cylinder" warnings; downstream feature recognition fails to identify the holes / shafts as parametric features. Users mitigate with Creo's "Optimize Face" or SolidWorks's "Combine faces".
expected_kernel_behavior: detect equivalent CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE entries (same axis, same radius) and merge their hosted faces into a single periodic face; emit "merged split cylinder" diagnostic; leaving the split unresolved breaks feature recognition downstream.
notes: Synonyms: "split cylinder face on seam", "NX writes cylinder as two halves", "feature recognition fails on split surface", "non-merged periodic face", "Optimize Face needed after import".
reproducer: two CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE entities with identical AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D and radius 5.0; two ADVANCED_FACE entries (one per half) with empty bound lists; CLOSED_SHELL referencing both halves.

sources: PTC community 977634 "Import STEP created by NX 11"

description: ISO 10303-46 nominally treats COLOUR_RGB values as linear-space [0.1] floats. The writer applies an sRGB-companding step before emission, producing values that look correct in sRGB-aware viewers but appear over-bright in linear-space-aware kernels. A user input of (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) becomes 0.7353569830523 (= sRGB(0.5)). Round-trip with mismatched receivers progressively brightens.
expected_kernel_behavior: Warn and accept: kernels should document their colour-space convention and emit a warning when COLOUR_RGB values cluster around sRGB-companded gray values that don't round-trip cleanly. Writers should heal by emitting in linear space. Treating companded values as linear without diagnostic is a coverage gap.
notes: Synonyms: "STEP colors brighter after CadQuery export", "RGB sRGB linear conversion bug", "colour values shifted on round-trip", "0.5 grey becomes 0.735", "gamma applied twice on STEP export".
reproducer: COLOUR_RGB('grey_should_be_0p5', 0.7353569830523, 0.7353569830523, 0.7353569830523); bind to a face via PRESENTATION_STYLE_ASSIGNMENT and STYLED_ITEM.
sender: CadQuery STEP writer (uses OCC's STEPCAFControl_Writer)
sources: github.com/CadQuery/cadquery issue #794 "Assembly Color Component Values in Exported STEP File Are Shifted"
bug-reporter language: "I asked for (0.5, 0.5, 0.5) but the STEP file has (0.7353, 0.7353, 0.7353)", "colours look brighter after STEP export".
title: CadQuery RGB shifted by sRGB→linear conversion on STEP export

description: The writer emits one fresh COLOUR_RGB entity per (object, color) tuple, even when many tuples share the same RGB value. The result is hundreds of entities like COLOUR_RGB('',0.5,0.5,0.5) that should be a single shared instance. File size bloats; receivers that pool colours on import end up with N "different" colours that all happen to have value (0.5, 0.5, 0.5).
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: writers must heal/de-dup COLOUR_RGB by (R, G, B) tuple equality before emission. Receivers should also normalize by pooling on tuple value, not entity identity, to avoid this bug's downstream UI clutter. Warn and accept with W_DUPLICATE_COLOUR when redundant entries are observed; emitting hundreds of copies of the same colour without diagnostic is a coverage gap.
notes: **See also**: Xp034 (sRGB shift). Synonyms: "duplicate COLOUR_RGB entities", "STEP file bloated by redundant colors", "same-valued colors not pooled", "writer doesn't de-dup colours", "hundreds of identical RGB entries".
reproducer: three COLOUR_RGB entities all carrying (0.5, 0.5, 0.5); three FILL_AREA_STYLE_COLOURs each referencing one; three SURFACE_STYLE_USAGEs; three STYLED_ITEMs all bound to the same ADVANCED_FACE.
sender: CadQuery STEP writer
sources: github.com/CadQuery/cadquery issue #1689 "Exporting STEP with colors doesn't de-duplicate as expected with different, but same-valued Colors"
bug-reporter language: "the same gray appears 200 times in the file", "STEP writer doesn't pool identical colours".
title: CadQuery STEP writer emits redundant COLOUR_RGB entities for identical colours

description: STYLED_ITEM, MECHANICAL_DESIGN_GEOMETRIC_PRESENTATION_REPRESENTATION, COLOUR_RGB and the PRESENTATION_STYLE_ASSIGNMENT chain live in a parallel forest of presentation entities not reachable from the MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP root. STEPControl_Reader walks only geometry; XCAF (STEPCAFControl_Reader) walks both. CadQuery historically exposed only the bare reader, so colours appeared yellow / default after import even though they were correctly written.
expected_kernel_behavior: kernels exposing a high-level "load STEP" API must default to the XCAF-aware path; bare-geometry reads must surface a "presentation entities ignored" warning so users know colours were dropped.
notes: **See also**: Xp034, Xp035. Synonyms: "STYLED_ITEM ignored on import", "STEP colours appear yellow", "bare reader skips presentation", "STEPControl_Reader vs STEPCAFControl_Reader", "colour metadata lost on load".
reproducer: ADVANCED_FACE with COLOUR_RGB(1.0, 0.0, 0.0) bound via STYLED_ITEM and MECHANICAL_DESIGN_GEOMETRIC_PRESENTATION_REPRESENTATION. The presentation forest is not referenced from MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP, so a depth-first walk from the solid root never sees it.
sender: any STEP file with valid STYLED_ITEM presentation graph
sources: github.com/CadQuery/cadquery issue #1638 "Problem importing STEP with colours"
bug-reporter language: "imported STEP files always appear yellow", "colours visible in viewer X but not in Y".
title: STYLED_ITEM colours dropped by bare STEPControl_Reader (vs XCAF reader)

description: A STEP-exported assembly contains two MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP bodies that interfere by 1 mm in one axis. Creo's import option "Solidify closed volumes" attempts to merge them and fails (the union is non-manifold). Receivers either (a) preserve both interfering bodies and emit a "interference detected" warning, (b) reject the file, or (c) silently keep one body and drop the other.
expected_kernel_behavior: load both bodies independently; surface an interference-detected diagnostic; dropping bodies without diagnostic is unacceptable; the kernel cannot abort on attempted union.
notes: Synonyms: "Creo overlapping bodies fail manifold", "interfering solids prevent solidify", "STEP assembly with body interference", "non-manifold union from overlap", "two solids overlap by 1mm in STEP".
reproducer: two MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREPs in the same SHAPE_REPRESENTATION; bounding boxes overlap by 1 mm along one axis; both backed by ADVANCED_FACE entities. PRODUCT.name encodes the intended overlap region.

PTC community 785330 "STEP exports from CREO Parametric fail to import in other software products"

SolidWorks's hole-wizard recognition fits the cylinder to its nearest standard size; M1.6 clearance hole is 1.8 mm, very close to 1.85 mm and within tolerance. The hole is mis-tagged metric, the BOM lists "M1.6", and the imperial intent is lost. The defect class is loss of unit/standard context for hole features under STEP round-trip.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: feature recognition should preserve any incoming SHAPE_ASPECT or PROPERTY_DEFINITION naming the standard/imperial intent; in absence of metadata, the kernel must reject relabeling imperial features as metric without a diagnostic. Warn and accept with W_FEATURE_STANDARD_MISMATCH when the inferred standard contradicts the source; accepting a re-classified standard without diagnostic is a coverage gap.
notes: **See also**: Xp029. Synonyms: "2-56 thread becomes M1.6", "imperial thread misread as metric", "hole feature metric/imperial confusion", "Onshape thread wrong size", "tap drill matched to wrong standard".
reproducer: CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE radius 0.925 mm in a SI_UNIT(.MILLI., .METRE.) context; ADVANCED_FACE; CLOSED_SHELL; MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP. PRODUCT.name records the original imperial intent.

title: Onshape 2-56 UNC tap drill misclassified as M1.6 metric clearance hole

Solid Edge displays both children but disables UI manipulation because no per-instance frame exists; the user perceives "stuck" sub-assemblies that cannot be selected, moved, or constrained. Accepting shared-IDT inputs that freeze the UI without explanation is a coverage gap; never crash, never hang.

description: FILE_SCHEMA carries 'IFC4x1' (lowercase x). ISO 10303-21 doesn't constrain the case of trailing characters in schema names; ISO 10303-11 schema identifiers are conventionally uppercase but real-world IFC writers have shipped both cases. A strict equality check against an uppercase-only allowlist rejects the file before any parsing of the data section.
expected_kernel_behavior: case-insensitive schema-name matching; or at minimum, accept both 'IFC4x1' and 'IFC4X1' as aliases. Strict-mode kernels should reject with a clear "schema name case mismatch" diagnostic naming the expected canonical form.
notes: Synonyms: "IFC4x1 lowercase x rejected", "schema name case-sensitive parser bug", "IfcOpenShell strict whitelist reject", "FILE_SCHEMA case mismatch", "valid file rejected by uppercase-only check".
reproducer: FILE_SCHEMA(('IFC4x1')); minimal IFC data section with IFCPROJECT, IFCGEOMETRICREPRESENTATIONCONTEXT, IFCAXIS2PLACEMENT3D, IFCCARTESIANPOINT.
sender: IFC writers (some that emit lowercase 'x') / equivalently any STEP writer using a non-canonical case in FILE_SCHEMA
sources: github.com/IfcOpenShell/IfcOpenShell issue #1311 "Bug report: fail at parsing IFC4x1 standard files"
bug-reporter language: "ifcopenshell rejects my IFC4x1 file", "the file is valid but the parser refuses it because of the lowercase x".
title: IfcOpenShell rejects valid IFC4X1 file due to lowercase 'x' in schema name

description: An EDGE references a B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS whose knot vector contains an interior multiplicity equal to (degree+1)+1 = 5 (for a degree-3 curve). ISO 10303-42 caps interior multiplicity at degree+1 to ensure C^0 continuity; super-multiplicity makes the curve discontinuous at the knot. NX's writer accepts this; Parasolid's importer flags it as a discontinuity and aborts. The Onshape user sees a generic "translation error" with no specific entity callout.
expected_kernel_behavior: validate knot-multiplicity invariants at parse time; either reject with a precise "interior knot multiplicity exceeds degree+1" diagnostic or split the curve at the discontinuity. Translators must surface specific entity / knot index, not a generic "translation error".
notes: Synonyms: "NX super-multiplicity knot", "Onshape translation error generic", "B-spline interior multiplicity > degree+1", "Parasolid rejects discontinuous spline", "knot vector violates ISO cap".
reproducer: B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS degree 3 with 8 control points; knot multiplicities (4, 5, 4) at parameters (0, 0.5, 1) — interior knot multiplicity 5 violates the (degree+1) cap.
sender: Siemens NX (which tolerates super-multiplicity knots in B-spline curves)
sources: bug-reporter language: "Onshape just says 'translation error' with no detail", "NX file imports fine in Catia but Onshape can't read it".
title: NX → Onshape "translation error" via super-multiplicity B-spline knot

description: The top-level PRODUCT_DEFINITION exists but no SHAPE_DEFINITION_REPRESENTATION binds it to a SHAPE_REPRESENTATION. Child PRODUCT_DEFINITIONs each have their own SDR. Some receivers (FreeCAD, Onshape) infer the missing top-level binding from the child graph; Inventor's reader treats it as structurally invalid and aborts the entire import even though the children are fine.
expected_kernel_behavior: when the top-level PRODUCT has no SDR but children do, infer a default top-level SHAPE_REPRESENTATION wrapping the children and emit a warning; do not abort the import. Strict-mode kernels should reject with "top-level PRODUCT_DEFINITION has no SHAPE_DEFINITION_REPRESENTATION".
notes: **See also**: A065. Synonyms: "missing root SDR", "PRODUCT_DEFINITION not bound to SHAPE_REPRESENTATION", "Inventor rejects empty top-level assembly", "AP242 from CATIA structurally invalid", "import aborts on missing SDR".
reproducer: top-level PRODUCT_DEFINITION with no SHAPE_DEFINITION_REPRESENTATION pointing to it; one child PRODUCT_DEFINITION with a proper SDR / SHAPE_REPRESENTATION / AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D / GEOMETRIC_REPRESENTATION_CONTEXT.
sender: CATIA / Creo AP242 writer for empty top-level assemblies
sources: forums.autodesk.com inventor 10994597 "STEP import fails for AP242 from PTC Creo"

title: CATIA AP242 → Inventor: top-level PRODUCT_DEFINITION without SDR

description: Two distinct defect modes in one fixture: (1) Component A's SHAPE_REPRESENTATION has an empty items list (zero geometry attached) — the footprint is "missing" on receive; (2) Component B's MAPPED_ITEM references the wrong REPRESENTATION_MAP target — TO-220 ends up rendering a TO-252 pin. Both arise from the writer's component-to-3D-model lookup pipeline failing to resolve attachments, with the MAPPED_ITEM still emitted but pointed at whatever happened to be in the lookup cache.
expected_kernel_behavior: receivers should warn on empty SHAPE_REPRESENTATION items lists ("component has no geometry"); validate MAPPED_ITEM target consistency (the target's name should match the source PRODUCT's name or carry an explicit mapping_origin); never silently render the wrong geometry.
notes: **See also**: Xp031 (KiCad name-collision). Synonyms: "KiCad PCB STEP missing components", "MAPPED_ITEM wrong target", "footprint imports as different package", "empty SHAPE_REPRESENTATION items", "STEP component swap on export".
reproducer: PRODUCT 'R0805' bound to SHAPE_REPRESENTATION with empty items; PRODUCT 'TO-220' bound to MAPPED_ITEM whose REPRESENTATION_MAP target is the SHAPE_REPRESENTATION named 'TO-252_pin_should_be_TO-220'.

description: A fully valid solid whose own extent is ~10 mm but which is authored a very large distance from the origin — here a 10×10 planar square whose corners sit at absolute coordinates ~1.2e8 mm. Double-precision readers (OCCT, CAD Assistant) load and render it fine (the 10 mm relief is ~1e-7 of the absolute magnitude, still far above the 1e-6 mm model tolerance). A reader that down-converts vertex positions into a float32 buffer cannot represent 10-unit relief at magnitude 1.2e8 — the float32 ULP there is ~16 units — so all four corners quantize to the SAME grid point and the face collapses to a degenerate zero-area primitive; the viewer shows an empty model.
expected_kernel_behavior: recentre far-from-origin geometry to a local frame before down-converting to single precision, or warn that a float32 output buffer cannot represent the model at its absolute coordinates. Emitting an all-zero / degenerate mesh with no diagnostic is the defect.
notes: **See also**: Tb013 (far-from-origin DOUBLE-precision ULP-vs-tolerance), Tb010 (single-precision round-trip that MASKS a real self-intersection). Here the file is clean and self-consistent — the defect is purely the output-buffer precision down-conversion in a WASM/glTF/three.js viewer, ORACLE-INVISIBLE to our single (double-precision) OCCT oracle (which loads a normal shape). Mechanism partly inferred from the ticket (could co-occur with a large-file size cap) — medium confidence. DRIFT audit 2026-07-12: gmsh count was provisional (never live-verified); corrected `shape(3)` → `shape(9)` against the live oracle (CI-Linux + local macOS agree) — this is a platform/gmsh-version artifact of the standard single-face scaffold, not a change in the claimed defect (still oracle-invisible; occt is unaffected). Synonyms: "far from origin float32 collapse", "single-precision viewer loses local relief", "all vertex positions zero after down-convert", "absolute coordinates degrade in three.js buffer", "GIS-placed model empty in web viewer". Provenance tier: runtime-only.
reproducer: a valid `ADVANCED_FACE` on a `PLANE` whose `CARTESIAN_POINT`s are all offset by ~1.2e8 mm from the origin while the face's own extent is ~10 mm; wrap in the standard PRODUCT chain.
sender: a producer that authors geometry at absolute (GIS-style) coordinates
sources: Pattern-mined from kovacsv/occt-import-js#37 / kovacsv/Online3DViewer#467 ("model doesn't contain any meshes … all positions are 0", opens in CAD Assistant) — pattern only, no bytes
the reporter-attached file is a third-party user upload (DESCRIBE-ONLY).
title: Far-from-origin model collapses in a float32 viewer buffer while double-precision CAD renders it

description: A fully valid, watertight `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` conical frustum whose lateral face is exactly one `ADVANCED_FACE` on a `CONICAL_SURFACE` (semi-angle 20°) bounded by two `CIRCLE` edges; the two caps are planar. The file is NOT defective — every OCCT version parses it and loads a solid. The defect is a mesher REGRESSION: on an OCCT-7.7.x `BRepMesh` the conical `ADVANCED_FACE` yields ZERO triangles, so the solid renders with a hole (a missing face); OCCT-7.6.1, CAD Assistant and other CAD tessellate all faces. Same bytes → complete in one kernel version, defective in the next.
expected_kernel_behavior: mesh every face of a valid solid; a face that produces zero triangles is a mesher defect, not an input defect — the receiver must not silently emit a solid missing a face. Cross-oracle: the same bytes are complete in one kernel version and defective in the next, so a version bump is itself a regression surface.
notes: **See also**: Gn014 / Gd* (conical-canonical INPUT-geometry defects), Pf021 (near-apex healing) — those are bad-geometry inputs; here the geometry is valid and the regression lives in the receiver's mesher VERSION. No prior catalog entry captures a kernel-version tessellation differential. ORACLE-INVISIBLE to our single-version harness: the file loads as a normal solid; the divergence lives between kernel versions. DRIFT audit 2026-07-12: gmsh count was provisional (never live-verified); corrected `shape(5)` → `shape(9)` against the live oracle (CI-Linux + local macOS agree) — a platform/gmsh-version artifact of the standard single-face scaffold, not a change in the claimed defect (still oracle-invisible; occt is unaffected). Synonyms: "conical face missing after OCCT 7.7 upgrade", "BRepMesh drops cone face", "solid renders with a hole one kernel version", "version-differential missing face", "same STEP complete in 7.6.1 broken in 7.7". Provenance tier: runtime-only.
reproducer: `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` / `CLOSED_SHELL` with one `ADVANCED_FACE` on a `CONICAL_SURFACE` (finite frustum bounded by a bottom and top `CIRCLE` edge) plus two planar cap faces; fully valid and watertight.
sender: any CAD writer emitting a valid conical frustum solid
sources: Pattern-mined from kovacsv/occt-import-js#42 "Surfaces are occasionally missed" → OCCT tracker 33681 — pattern only, no bytes
the reporter-attached file is a third-party user upload (DESCRIBE-ONLY).
title: Valid conical `ADVANCED_FACE` dropped by OCCT 7.7.x `BRepMesh` but present in ≤7.6.1 / desktop CAD (kernel-version differential)

description: Every record line in the DATA section ends with one or more ASCII space (0x20) characters before the line terminator. Spec-conforming parsers accept this (whitespace is insignificant outside string literals), but downstream tools that diff exports for change-detection see noise on every line, version-control systems show every line as modified on every export, and crude line-based regex parsers that anchor on `;$` mis-match. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file has trailing spaces", "every line ends with whitespace", "diff is huge but nothing changed", "git keeps marking the file dirty".
expected_kernel_behavior: read tolerantly; the spec permits insignificant whitespace anywhere outside string literals. Optionally normalise on re-emit. A downstream tool that warns on this is over-strict; a producer that emits this is sloppy but not malformed.
notes: Practically harmless to parse; the cost is to humans who diff exports. Provenance tier: writer-side (Q5 reclassification 2026-07-01).
reproducer: minimal Part-21 file where each `#NNN=ENTITY(..);` line ends with ` ` (three spaces) before `\n`.
sender: Older FreeCAD STEP writer (pre-0.20) and some Pro/E export filters
sources: FreeCAD #4231 "STEP exporter pads lines with spaces"
bug-reporter language: "diff between exports is all whitespace"
title: Trailing whitespace on every record line

description: The HEADER section uses CRLF (`0x0D 0x0A`) line terminators while the DATA section uses bare LF (`0x0A`), or any other inconsistent mix within one file. Spec-conforming parsers ignore line-ending choice (whitespace), but tools that count lines for diagnostics report misleading line numbers, some text editors display the file as binary, and content-hash-based caches see the file as different from a CRLF-normalised copy. Bug-reporter language: "line numbers in error messages are wrong", "file shows up as binary in editor", "STEP from Windows opens weird on Mac".
expected_kernel_behavior: read tolerantly; treat any of `\n`, `\r\n`, or `\r` (classic Mac) as a line terminator. Diagnostics that report a line number should normalise.
notes: **See also**: Wr042. Cousin of Le028 but emitted by writer rather than introduced by transit.- **Byte assertion**: contains(b'\r\n') and contains(b'\n') Provenance tier: writer-side (Q5 reclassification 2026-07-01).
reproducer: HEADER section terminated with `\r\n`, DATA section terminated with `\n`.
sender: Windows-hosted writers that build the HEADER block in-memory (CRLF) and append the DATA block from a streamed buffer (LF), or vice versa
sources: OCCT bug forum "STEP file from Windows looks corrupt on Linux"
title: Mixed CRLF and LF line endings within one file

description: The closing `END-ISO-10303-21;` token is emitted without a trailing newline. The spec does not require one (it requires only the closing marker), so the file is well-formed. But concatenation of two such files produces `END-ISO-10303-21;ISO-10303-21;` on a single line, which trips a class of crude scripts that grep for `^ISO-10303-21;`. Bug-reporter language: "can't concat two STEPs", "POSIX text-file rule violated", "no newline at end of file".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: parsers normalize / accept this form (the spec permits it); downstream tooling that concatenates files adds its own separator.
notes: A POSIX-text-file convention (text files end with newline) but not a Part-21 requirement. Provenance tier: writer-side (Q5 full-corpus 2026-07-01).
reproducer: Part-21 file ending with the bytes `END-ISO-10303-21;` and no `0x0A` after.
sender: Older Siemens NX export and several in-house writers
sources: OCCT forum "concatenating two STEP files produces unparseable result"
title: Final `END-ISO-10303-21;` without trailing newline

description: Continuation lines for long records mix TAB (0x09) and SPACE (0x20) for indentation, or use TAB for some continuations and 2-SPACE for others within the same file. Parsers don't care; humans diffing or reviewing exports do. Bug-reporter language: "tabs and spaces mixed", "indentation inconsistent", "looks bad in editor".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: normalize by ignoring the whitespace.
notes: Cosmetic only, but reviewer-fatiguing. Provenance tier: writer-side (Q5 reclassification 2026-07-01).
reproducer: a long argument list where some continuation lines start with a TAB and others start with two SPACEs.
sender: KiCad PCB-to-STEP exporter and a few homegrown writers
title: Tab characters used for line continuation indentation inconsistently

byte_assertions: contains(b'1.0E-7') and contains(b'1e-07') and (contains(b'0.0000001') or contains(b'1.0e-007'))
description: Floating-point values appear in three or more distinct formats within a single DATA section: `1.0E-7`, `1e-07`, `0.0000001`, and `1.0e-007` (extra exponent digit) all coexist. The spec permits any valid REAL formatting, so each value parses correctly, but tools that hash REAL streams to detect change disagree on equality, regex-based extractors fail, and human reviewers find the file unreadable. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file has weird number formatting", "every coordinate looks different", "scientific notation inconsistent".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: normalize / parse all valid REAL formats; coerce / canonicalise on re-emit if the kernel's policy is normalised output.
notes: ISO 10303-21 §6 allows any of these forms; producer is sloppy but conforming.
reproducer: one CARTESIAN_POINT with coordinates `(1.0E-7, 1e-07, 0.0000001)` and a second with `(1.0e-007, 1.0, 1.)`.
sender: Multi-source writer pipelines that compose entities from different subsystems (e.g. older Pro/E, multi-pass NX export)
sources: bug-reporter language: "every number formatted differently" (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Floating-point format inconsistency within one file

description: Coordinates that were entered as exact rationals or simple decimals (1.0, 1.5, 0.25) appear in the emitted file as nearly-but-not-exactly the original (1.4999999999998, 0.25000000000004). The defect is invisible per-value but accumulates across round-trips: a vertex stamped from STEP→kernel→STEP→kernel drifts microns per cycle. Bug-reporter language: "coordinate 1.5 became 1.4999999999998 after re-export", "precision lost on round-trip", "model creeps after every save".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: normalize internal storage to sufficient precision to preserve the input on round-trip within the spec's REAL precision; coerce emit to the smallest representation that recovers the internal value exactly.
notes: Discoverable only by comparing pre- and post-round-trip files; the file as observed is plausible.
reproducer: a CARTESIAN_POINT with coordinates `(1.4999999999998,2.5000000000003,0.99999999999996)` claiming to represent `(1.5, 2.5, 1.0)`.
sender: Writers that store coordinates in single-precision (float32) internally but emit double-precision strings, or use printf("%.15g") on values that were 1.5 represented as 1.4999999999998 due to prior arithmetic
title: Floating-point precision degradation on round-trip

description: Numeric attributes appear with commas as decimal separator (`1,5` instead of `1.5`) because the writer used a locale-aware formatter. ISO 10303-21 mandates the period (`.`) as the decimal separator; comma-decimal output is malformed. Receivers either fail at the lexer (a `,` mid-number ends the argument and the next field is mis-counted) or, with bizarre tolerance, accept the comma and produce wrong geometry. Bug-reporter language: "commas in numbers", "German locale STEP", "STEP file from European user looks corrupt".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as malformed with a diagnostic that names the offending attribute and column; do not silently accept comma-decimals because that makes the failure mode geometric rather than syntactic.
notes: Le023 covers this from the read side; Wr007 documents the producer-side root cause. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts the malformed file (no diagnostic, empty result); kernel mishandling is the documented signal here; the catalog claim above describes the desired future behavior, not what OCC does today. Provenance tier: writer-side (Q5 reclassification 2026-07-01).
reproducer: a CARTESIAN_POINT entry with coordinates `(1,5,2,5,3,5)` (intended as `(1.5,2.5,3.5)` but parsed as 6 separate integers).
sender: Writers that use locale-aware `sprintf` / `std::to_string` without forcing the C locale; reported on Windows builds running with German, French, or other comma-decimal locales
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0029xxx-class issue "STEP file from German workstation unreadable"
bug-reporter language: "STEP file has commas where it should have periods" (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Locale-sensitive decimal separator emitted (comma instead of period)

The file inflates 2-3× over what minimal-form output would produce. Spec-conforming, but bandwidth- and storage-hostile. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file unnecessarily huge", "20 digits for every zero", "compresses 95%".

notes: Cousin of Wr006 from the opposite direction.
sender: Writers using `printf("%.20f", ..)` or `printf("%.17g", ..)` indiscriminately on every coordinate

description: The producer emits `$` (omitted) where the EXPRESS schema declares the attribute as required (non-OPTIONAL). Example: `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D('placement',#10,$,$)` where the schema specifies `axis` and `ref_direction` as effectively required when both are present (one cannot be `$` if the other is non-`$` and the Z-axis convention is to be applied). Some kernels invent a default direction; others reject. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file has dollar signs for required fields", "missing axis direction", "writer omitted required attribute".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as malformed when a required attribute is `$`; do not silently substitute Z+X defaults because the producer's intent is unrecoverable.
notes: AP242 marks `axis` and `ref_direction` as OPTIONAL in the EXPRESS; but most receivers expect both populated when the placement is referenced from a non-trivial geometry context. **OCC behavior**: silently substitutes the Z+X default convention rather than rejecting; this is the kernel mishandling the catalog above forbids. Provenance tier: writer-side (Q5 reclassification 2026-07-01).
reproducer: `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D('p',#10,$,$)` paired with a `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` that depends on the placement.
sender: Older Pro/E and some lightweight web-CAD STEP exporters
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0026xxx-class "missing direction in AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D from kernel X"
bug-reporter language: "writer skipped required attribute" (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Spurious `$` for required parameter (writer omits required value)

description: The `*` token denotes an attribute inherited from a supertype and overridden in a subtype context; valid only inside complex (subtype-stack) records. The producer emits `*` in a simple-entity instance where no supertype exists, producing `CARTESIAN_POINT('p',(*,0.0,0.0))` or similar. Receivers diverge: some treat `*` as an error, some treat it as zero, some treat it as `$`. Bug-reporter language: "asterisk where number expected", "STEP file has stars in coordinates", "writer used override-marker incorrectly".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as malformed; `*` is meaningful only in complex-instance subtype-override position.
notes: ISO 10303-21 §10 defines `*` semantics narrowly. Provenance tier: writer-side (Q5 full-corpus 2026-07-01).
reproducer: `CARTESIAN_POINT('p',(*,0.0,0.0))` in a non-subtype context.
sender: Buggy writers that mis-handle the inheritance-override mechanism for complex (subtype) entities and apply it to non-inherited attributes
sources: OCCT forum "writer emitted asterisk in CARTESIAN_POINT coords"
title: Re-emitted `*` (overridden) where schema does not allow it

description: A `CLOSED_SHELL` entity with an empty face-list `()` appears in the file because the producer pruned all faces but left the shell wrapper. Schema requires the face-list to be non-empty. Some readers reject; some accept and produce a vacuous shell that flows through the rest of the import as an empty solid. Bug-reporter language: "empty shell", "STEP closed_shell with no faces", "writer left a stub entity".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject the empty-shell case as schema-violating; do not silently accept the placeholder.
notes: Strongly related to Wr020 (empty SHAPE_DEFINITION_REPRESENTATION chains). **OCC behavior**: silently accepts the empty face-list and produces a vacuous shell with no diagnostic; the kernel mishandling is the documented signal here.
reproducer: `CLOSED_SHELL('hollow',())` referenced by a `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`.

description: Instance numbers in the DATA section follow no monotonic pattern: `#1`, then `#1000`, then `#5`, then `#1003`, then `#7`. The spec does not mandate monotonic numbering, so the file is well-formed; but human reviewers, line-based diff tools, and forward-reference-detecting linters all stumble. Bug-reporter language: "STEP instance numbers are random", "file numbering jumps", "can't follow refs visually".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: parse normally; numbering is content-addressable, not order-bearing; a re-emit policy may normalize / renumber sequentially.
notes: Discoverability is the main cost; correctness is unaffected.
reproducer: a Part-21 file in which the order of `#NNN` in the DATA section is `#1, #1000, #5, #1003, #7, #1006`.
sender: Writers that allocate instance numbers from a hashed pool keyed on entity-identity rather than emit-order; observed in some Java-based exporters
sources: OCCT forum "STEP file has random instance numbers"
title: Random `#N` numbering with no monotonic structure

description: The producer emits `#5 = ORIENTED_EDGE(..,#10,..)` before `#10` has been defined. Spec-conforming readers must do a two-pass parse (or a deferred-resolution mechanism), but a class of single-pass kernels reports "reference to undefined instance #10" and rejects. Bug-reporter language: "forward references in STEP", "ref before def", "kernel doesn't support out-of-order STEP".
expected_kernel_behavior: implement two-pass parsing or deferred-resolution; the spec permits forward references. Reject only if a reference remains unresolved after the full file is parsed.
notes: Lh006-class issue but writer-attributable.
reproducer: `#5 = CARTESIAN_POINT('p',(0.,0.,0.));` followed later by `#1 = AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D('a',#5,$,$);` — but `#5` appears first; or, more pathologically, `#1 = .. (#5,..);` first, then `#5 = ..;` second (forward).
sender: Writers that emit entities in topological-construction order without a topological sort; observed in some open-source exporters
sources: OCCT bug "kernel chokes on forward refs"
title: Forward references where sequential numbering was expected

description: A file with 50 entities uses instance numbers like `#42`, `#9876543`, `#21000000`; the maximum number is many orders of magnitude larger than the entity count. Spec-conforming, but a class of receivers naïvely pre-allocates an array of size `max(#N)`, blowing up memory. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file with huge instance numbers", "out of memory loading 50-entity file", "instance #N overflow".
expected_kernel_behavior: use a sparse map (hashtable) for instance lookup; never assume `#N` is a dense array index. Reject only if `#N` exceeds 32-bit signed integer range and the kernel uses int32 indices internally.
notes: Spec does not bound `#N`; ISO 10303-21 Ed.3 §5 defines it as an unbounded positive integer.
reproducer: a 5-entity file where the highest instance number is `#999999999`.
sender: Writers that hash entity identity to a wide integer space and use the hash as the instance number directly
sources: OCCT forum "instance numbers run to 10 million for 50 entities"
bug-reporter language: "huge instance numbers", "memory blows up loading STEP"
title: Sparse instance numbering with huge gaps

description: Two entities in the same DATA section share the same `#N`. Spec violation. Receivers diverge: first-wins, last-wins, both-loaded-and-randomly-resolved, reject. Bug-reporter language: "duplicate #5", "same instance number twice", "STEP file has collision".
expected_kernel_behavior: reject as malformed; spec mandates unique instance numbers per DATA section. Document the resolution policy if the kernel chooses tolerant first-wins / last-wins.
notes: Lh010-class.
reproducer: `#10 = CARTESIAN_POINT('a',(0.,0.,0.));` and later `#10 = CARTESIAN_POINT('b',(1.,1.,1.));` in the same DATA section.

sources: bug-reporter language: "duplicate instance number", "two entities with same #N" (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Duplicate `#N` instance numbers in the same DATA section

The receiver loads "successfully" but reports zero solids. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file loaded but nothing visible", "empty model", "product tree but no geometry", "ghost STEP file".

description: The producer writes `FILE_DESCRIPTION(('CAD-System-X version 12.4.1 build 2026-04-15'),'2;1')`. Some receivers contain heuristic special-casing keyed on vendor strings; they apply a "fix-up X model" filter only if the vendor string matches. This couples the receiver's behaviour to the producer's exact wording, so a minor wording change ("CAD-System X" with a space versus "CAD-System-X" with a hyphen) silently disables the fix-up. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file behaves differently after vendor renamed product", "kernel detects wrong vendor", "vendor sniffing failed".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: normalize / avoid behaviour-altering vendor sniffing; if vendor-specific compatibility is needed, expose it as an explicit user opt-in.
notes: Sender-attribution in `FILE_DESCRIPTION` is a long-standing interop hazard. Bytes alone are insufficient to demonstrate this defect;. Tagged provenance_tier: writer-side.
reproducer: a fixture with `FILE_DESCRIPTION(('CAD-System-X v12.4.1'),'2;1')` and a comment noting the receiver special-cases the exact spelling.
sender: Writers that include vendor-version strings in `FILE_DESCRIPTION.description` such that downstream readers branch on them
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP from vendor X behaves weirdly"
title: Vendor-specific FILE_DESCRIPTION strings that downstream readers special-case

description: A complex (subtype-stack) record like `(LENGTH_UNIT() NAMED_UNIT(*) SI_UNIT(.MILLI.,.METRE.))` is re-emitted on round-trip as `(SI_UNIT(.MILLI.,.METRE.) NAMED_UNIT(*) LENGTH_UNIT())`; the same complex entity but with the supertype list reordered. Spec-conforming (the order within `(... ..)` is supertype-significant per ISO 10303-21 §11 but only by inheritance hierarchy, not by emission order); receivers that build canonical hash strings see the file as different. Bug-reporter language: "subtype-stack reordered", "complex entity attribute order changed", "STEP round-trip permutes inheritance order".
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: normalize / emit complex-record supertype lists in a canonical order (e.g., alphabetic or schema-declaration-order) deterministically.

description: Records inside a single DATA section terminate with mixed `;\n` and `;\r\n` line endings. The spec is silent on line-ending conformance — whitespace is whitespace — but tools that line-count for diagnostics report inconsistent line numbers, content-hash caches see the file as different on each export, and editors display the file as binary. Cousin of Wr002 (HEADER vs DATA section uses different line ending) but at the per-record granularity. Bug-reporter language: "STEP file mixed newlines per record", "diff of exports is full of line-ending changes".
expected_kernel_behavior: parsers must accept (whitespace tolerance); writers should be deterministic per-file. A normaliser is the simplest fix.
notes: **See also**: Wr002, Le028. Provenance tier: writer-side (Q5 full-corpus 2026-07-01).
sender: Multi-pass writers where one pass appends records via a buffered text stream (LF) and a separate pass appends records via a Windows-line-ending logger (CRLF), interleaved within the same DATA section
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP file mixed newlines per record", "writer outputs CRLF then LF inconsistently"

description: A producer's writer emits non-ASCII characters as raw UTF-8 bytes (`\xC3\xA9` for `é`) inside a string literal, while the file's `FILE_DESCRIPTION` declares Edition-2 (`'2;1'`). Edition-2 mandates 8-bit default with non-ASCII expressed via `\X\HH`, `\X2\HHHH\X0\`, or `\PA\.\PI\` page-shift directives; raw multi-byte UTF-8 violates the edition's encoding contract. Edition-3 readers (UTF-8 default) decode the bytes correctly by accident; Edition-2 readers see two single-byte ISO-8859-1 characters instead of one composed `é`. The writer is the producer-side root cause for the receiver-side defect Le003 / Ad058. Bug-reporter language: "STEP writer outputs UTF-8 in Ed.2 file", "non-ASCII in Edition-2 STEP", "exporter does not escape non-ASCII".
expected_kernel_behavior: the writer detects the file's declared edition and emits non-ASCII characters via the edition-appropriate directive; Edition-2 uses `\X\` / `\X2\` / `\PA\.\PI\`; Edition-3 may emit raw UTF-8 with proper `FILE_DESCRIPTION` declaration. Never silently mismatch edition and encoding.
notes: Producer-side root cause for Le003 (now merged into Le021), Le050, Ad058. **See also**: Le050, Le021. Provenance tier: requires-sibling-pair — bytes alone (this fixture's body) demonstrate the defect; the fuller demonstration is the differential between the in-memory string and the bytes the writer emits. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); catalog disallows silent-accept. Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers enforcing the spec must reject (or surface a diagnostic) — silent acceptance defeats the catalog's stated invariant.
reproducer: a `FILE_DESCRIPTION` `'2;1'` (Edition 2); a `PRODUCT.name` containing the raw bytes `\xC3\xA9` representing UTF-8 `é` instead of the spec-required `'\X\E9'` escape.
sender: Writers that rely on the host runtime's default UTF-8 string handling but emit `FILE_DESCRIPTION` with `'2;1'` implementation-level (Edition 2)
sources: ISO 10303-21 Ed.2 §6.4 (8-bit default with explicit escapes for non-ASCII)
bug-reporter language: "STEP writer outputs UTF-8 in Ed.2 file"
title: Writer emits raw UTF-8 bytes in string literal where Ed.2 mandates `\X\` / `\X2\` escape

description: The user selects inches in the STEP-export unit dialog. The writer emits a `LENGTH_UNIT` complex record claiming inches, but every `CARTESIAN_POINT` carries the original millimetre values verbatim with no scale division. A part the user authored as a 25.4 mm cube round-trips as a 25.4 inch (645 mm) cube; visibly 25.4× larger on re-import. The unit declaration and the numeric content disagree.

Loading geometry whose original Placement has been silently flattened is a coverage gap.
notes: **See also**: Wr025, A024. Synonyms: "Placement ignored on STEP export", "single-body export drops orientation", "compound workaround needed for placement", "exported part lands at wrong position". Provenance tier: writer-side (Q5 reclassification 2026-07-01).

description: Exporting a body that is the direct result of a Boolean operation crashes the writer mid-export inside `TKXDESTEP`. The stack trace centres on the color-attribution pass (it traverses sub-shapes to record `STYLED_ITEM` for each face). When the topmost shape is a freshly-fused Boolean result, the sub-shape iterator dereferences a face whose owner-edge map has not yet been populated. A trivial workaround is to chamfer or fillet one edge after the Boolean; that re-walks the sub-shape graph and populates the maps. The on-disk artefact (when the writer doesn't crash, e.g., on a different OS / OCCT build) is a STEP file with `STYLED_ITEM` references to entity numbers that don't exist in the file's own DATA section.
expected_kernel_behavior: writer must validate sub-shape maps before traversal; receivers must reject dangling entity references with a clear diagnostic rather than crash.
notes: **See also**: P028, A018. Synonyms: "STEP/STEPZ crash exporting boolean", "TKXDESTEP segfault on boolean export", "writer dies on STYLED_ITEM map", "chamfer workaround for boolean export crash". Provenance tier: writer-side (Q5 reclassification 2026-07-01).

The output STEP carries doubled coordinates in a context that still claims millimetres. Distinct from Wr035 (×1000) and Wr044 (inch label only) by the specific 2× factor.

description: A STEP file imports cleanly via `step-g` (the resulting .g file contains a `Brep_2.s` solid with face count > 0), but the downstream `g-stl` tessellator prints `ERROR(Brep_2.s): tessellation failure` and writes `0 triangles written`; the resulting `.stl` is empty. The two halves of the BRL-CAD pipeline disagree on whether the model is "good": step-g believes it converted the geometry; g-stl cannot triangulate it. The user-facing symptom is an empty `.stl` with no diagnostic at the file-format interface; the failure happens deep in `PullbackCurve` / `SurfaceTree`. The class of inputs that trigger this is narrow but real: any face whose pcurves and 3D curves agree at vertices but drift to ~1e-3 mm in the interior (because the importer treats 1e-3 as the tolerance, but the tessellator treats anything below 1e-3 as a degeneracy). Distinct from M005 (number-of-facets validation property: facet count, not pipeline disagreement).
expected_kernel_behavior: reject; the importer and tessellator must agree on a single tolerance value; if a face cannot be tessellated at the importer's tolerance, the importer must reject it at parse time rather than commit a `Brep_2.s` to the .g file. Pipeline diagnostic must surface both the offending face id and the tolerance comparison.
notes: **See also**: M005, M022, N019, N050. Synonyms: "BRL-CAD step-g imports but g-stl emits empty", "0 triangles written silently", "tessellation failure on sliver face", "importer/tessellator tolerance disagreement", "STEP→.g→.stl produces empty STL no diagnostic".
reproducer: STEP `BEZIER_SURFACE` with a 4×4 control net whose v-extent is 3 micrometres (well below step-g's 1e-3 mm tolerance). step-g loads the face; g-stl emits zero triangles.
sender: STEP files whose features sit at or below the BRL-CAD step-g hard-coded 1e-3 mm tolerance (sliver faces, micro-fillets, sub-tolerance B-spline patches) — the importer treats the geometry as valid but the tessellator's adaptive sampler cannot find sample points satisfying the same hard-coded tolerance.
sources: BRL-CAD users mailing list 2017 (Filip Binkiewicz reproducer): "ERROR(Brep_2.s): tessellation failure" + "0 triangles written"
bug-reporter language: "step-g converts cleanly but g-stl outputs empty file", "BRep imports OK but cannot triangulate", "STEP→.g→.stl pipeline silently produces empty STL".
title: step-g imports cleanly but downstream `g-stl` tessellator silently writes zero triangles

description: A STEP writer emits an EDGE_CURVE whose `edge_geometry` slot is filled by an unbounded LINE entity rather than a TRIMMED_CURVE(LINE, t0, t1) or a SURFACE_CURVE with explicit param bookkeeping. The vertices nominally define the edge's domain, but the LINE itself carries no parametric extent, so receivers that traverse the LINE directly (rather than the EDGE_CURVE bookkeeping) walk into an unbounded range.

Receivers that mutate one instance and expect the others independent are surprised.

notes: Synonyms: "Solvespace exported duplicated entities aliased", "STEP writer aliases shared substructure", "MAPPED_ITEM shared one map", "writer dedup creates aliasing", "shared-substructure mutation propagates". Provenance tier: writer-side (Q5 reclassification 2026-07-01).
reproducer: one REPRESENTATION_MAP referenced by two distinct MAPPED_ITEM call-sites.
sources: Pattern-mined from solvespace/solvespace#1589 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). User-reported: Solvespace's "Export volumes" path deliberately collapses geometrically-identical instances by reference rather than emitting per-instance copies
one entity becomes the alias for many call-sites.
title: Writer aliases geometrically-identical entities (shared substructure)

description: The writer's surface-collection pass reads a structure whose byte-order was assumed little-endian; on s390x, the iteration count returns garbage and the writer concludes there are no surfaces. The resulting file is structurally valid but semantically empty.
expected_kernel_behavior: assert non-empty before emit; fail visibly when no surfaces were collected.
notes: Synonyms: "Solvespace s390x STEP empty", "no surfaces to export STEP", "big-endian STEP writer regression", "Debian s390x STEP regression", "STEP writer silent empty on big-endian". Provenance tier: writer-side (Q5 reclassification 2026-07-01).

sources: Pattern-mined from solvespace/solvespace#1264 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). User-reported reproducer: Solvespace on s390x emits `SHAPE_REPRESENTATION` with an empty items list — "no surfaces to export" — without any diagnostic.

title: XCAF → STEP export crashes on umlaut in label

description: The BREP intermediate loses the analytic-surface metadata; on re-export, the OCCT writer reconstructs the surface as a B-spline approximation rather than an analytic CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE. The geometry is *approximately* preserved but the parameterization, derivatives, and downstream meshing all change. Distinct from Wr053 (torus-fused) because the source surface was a clean analytic, not a fused solid.
expected_kernel_behavior: BREP intermediate must preserve analytic-surface metadata; writer must prefer analytic emit when the surface admits one.
notes: Synonyms: "pythonocc STEP round-trip cylinder spline", "STEP→BREP→STEP analytic surface lost", "cylinder becomes B-spline after round-trip", "OCC writer inflates analytic to NURBS", "STEP cylinder NURBS approximation after round-trip".
reproducer: a B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS with degree-1 control net approximating a cylinder, replacing what should be a CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE.
sources: Pattern-mined from pythonocc/pythonocc-core#661 (LGPL-clean — pattern only, no bytes copied). User-reported reproducer: a cylinder authored as analytic CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE comes out as a B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS after BREP round-trip, even when the source had clean analytic geometry.
title: STEP→BREP→STEP round-trip inflates cylinder analytic surface into B-spline

under OCCT 7.4.0 the same files come out with surfaces offset by a non-zero translation. The bytes are identical

title: Solidworks AP214 → OCCT version upgrade mis-locates surfaces

description: Distinct from Xp034 (CadQuery RGB sRGB shift on a non-named colour) — this is the *named-colour* path, where the spec-correct value is taken from X11 and the conversion is applied silently. Receivers that compare colours-by-RGB hit a non-trivial difference.
expected_kernel_behavior: emit X11 named colours at their spec value, or expose the gamma-conversion as configurable.
