title: Model marked Loaded without entities; load skipped silently

description: Two different sources of warnings (parser warnings about file syntax vs. semantic warnings about data content) are mapped onto the same severity bucket. A consumer who suppresses load warnings ends up suppressing data warnings too. Typical fixture: a stray comment between HEADER's ENDSEC and the DATA section (parser-level warning) plus a B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS at the upper-boundary degree (e.g., degree 25, a data-level warning). Bug-reporter language: "warnings hidden", "parser warnings vs data warnings confused".
expected_kernel_behavior: Distinguish severity classes; separate warning channels.
notes: Bug-reporter synonyms: "diagnostic channel confusion". Provenance tier: runtime-only; bytes alone cannot demonstrate this defect; the symptom is the conflation of two diagnostic severity channels emitted by the kernel during parse + transfer. A behavioral test that captures the kernel's diagnostic stream is the appropriate venue. Synonyms: "STEP load warning vs data warning conflated", "diagnostic severity confused", "syntax warning suppresses semantic warning", "warning channel mixed for STEP load", "STEP warning bucket conflated".
reproducer: A file with both a parser-level warning (a stray comment between ENDSEC and DATA, or in another unusual place) and a data-level warning (e.g., a B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS at the spec-boundary degree).

title: Load-time warning vs data-content warning: severity confusion

description: A reader's `Mend()` step takes a Fail-class diagnostic and downgrades it to a Warning if the kernel "fixed" the underlying problem. A consumer relying on the original Fail to gate further processing now misses it. Typical fixture: a B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS whose knot multiplicities don't match the required count (e.g., degree 2 with 3 control points needs 6 knots, but the multiplicities sum to 7); a Fail-class condition that gets auto-mended and silently demoted. Bug-reporter language: "kernel hid an error", "fail downgraded to warning silently", "wrong knot count not reported".
expected_kernel_behavior: Warn and accept: always preserve the original severity; record the Mend as a separate "auto-corrected" event. Must not silently downgrade Fail to Warning.
notes: Synonyms: "silent error fix", "fail demoted". Provenance tier: runtime-only; bytes alone cannot demonstrate this defect; the symptom is a runtime mutation of the diagnostic-severity record (Fail demoted to Warning) inside the kernel's check object. The static fixture only encodes the input precondition; observing the demotion requires a kernel runtime trace. Synonyms: "STEP Mend demotes Fail to Warning", "auto-fix hides original failure", "kernel mend hides bad knot count", "B_SPLINE knot defect silently fixed", "Fail downgraded to Warning by kernel".
reproducer: An entity that triggers a Fail-class check (e.g., a `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` whose knot count is off-by-one — degree 2 with 3 control points but knot_multiplicities sum to 7 instead of the expected 6) but is then auto-fixed by the reader.
sender: deduced — OCCT uncovered-class sweep
title: A "Mend" demotes a Fail to a Warning, hiding the original failure (e.g., B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS with wrong knot count auto-fixed)

Downstream consumers see "Done" status with no shape attached. Bug-reporter language: "kernel says done but produced nothing", "transfer succeeded with empty result", "extreme-magnitude coordinates overflow".
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject and emit the underlying exception text: mark the transfer as Error, not Done; must not silently swallow exceptions.

Provenance tier: runtime-only; bytes alone cannot demonstrate this defect; the symptom is a transfer-time C++ exception silently swallowed and replaced with a null binding plus a "Done" status. The static fixture only carries the trigger geometry; demonstrating the swallowed exception requires a kernel runtime trace. Synonyms: "STEP entity bound to null after exception", "B-spline with extreme coords gives null", "1.0E+308 control point swallows exception", "STEP transfer Done but shape null", "exception swallowed during STEP transfer".

category: §12.1c (sub-class: virtual-dispatch fall-through, umbrella over stub manifestations)
description: BRL-CAD step-g virtual-dispatches every subtype through `LoadONBrep`; the base implementation prints to stderr and returns false. Any subtype the importer does not specifically override (e.g. `SeamCurve`, `CompositeCurve`, `BoundedPCurve`, `CompositeCurveOnSurface`, `CurveBoundedSurface`, `RectangularCompositeSurface`, `SurfacePatch`, `CartesianTransformationOperator`, `Polyline`) falls through and gets dropped without caller-side knowledge that geometry was lost. The diagnostic prints to stderr only and never propagates as an error code; callers cannot distinguish full success from partial drop. Fixture demonstrates the pattern with `SEAM_CURVE` since cylinders almost always carry one.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject; every stubbed dispatch must escalate to a `STEP_LOAD_ERROR` that propagates to the top-level converter; the converter must exit non-zero when any subgraph reachable from a referenced `ADVANCED_BREP_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION` returned false. Distinct from In013 (the kernel-actor "no actor" case): here the actor exists but is a stub.
notes: **See also**: Gn038, Twi100, Twi101, Gs057, Gs058, U045, In013, Pf037. Synonyms: "step-g LoadONBrep not implemented umbrella", "virtual-dispatch fall-through silently drops geometry", "stderr-only diagnostic for missing subtype", "BRL-CAD step-g cannot escalate stub-misses to error".

description: ISO 10303-21 grammar requires every REAL to carry a decimal point (`1.`, `1.0`, `0.5`). Generators that print integer values into REAL slots emit `1` where `1.` is required (e.g. `IFCDIRECTION((1,0,0))`). stepcode warns and salvages via `istringstream >> double`; strict readers reject. Implementors Issue 003 records the original disagreement: integers must not be followed by a dot, REALs must be.
expected_kernel_behavior: Strict reject by default; lenient mode auto-promote INTEGER → REAL with a warning. Never silently coerce.
notes: A primary cause of integer-vs-real type-coercion bugs. **See also**: Ad049, Ls002, Ls003, Ls004, Ls005, Ls006, Ls009. **OCC behavior**: silently coerces the integer to a REAL with no diagnostic; kernel mishandling; the catalog above forbids silent coercion. Synonyms: "REAL with no decimal point", "integer where REAL required", "1 written instead of 1.", "DIRECTION coords missing dots", "STEP REAL missing trailing period". Provenance tier: bytes-only (Q5 full-corpus 2026-07-01).
title: REAL literal missing mandatory decimal point

description: Grammar requires at least one digit before the dot. `.5` is not legal; `0.5` is. C/Python `%g` formatters frequently emit bare `.5`.
expected_kernel_behavior: Strict reject; lenient readers commonly accept implicit zero.
notes: **See also**: Ls001. Synonyms: "REAL with no digit before decimal", ".5 instead of 0.5 in STEP", "leading-dot REAL literal", "%g formatter emits .5", "missing zero before decimal".
title: REAL literal with no digit before the decimal point

description: ISO 10303-21 specifies upper-case `E` for the REAL exponent; lower-case `e`, embedded whitespace (`1.5 E+3`), or `+` sign in the exponent (`1e+18`) are non-conforming. Locale-aware printers also produce these.
expected_kernel_behavior: Lex `[+-]?\d+(\.\d*)?([eE][+-]?\d+)?` permissively; emit warning for non-canonical subsets.
notes: **See also**: Ls001. Synonyms: "lowercase e in REAL exponent", "1e+18 instead of 1E+18", "whitespace in REAL exponent", "STEP exponent has plus sign", "non-standard exponent in STEP".
title: Lower-case `e` exponent or whitespace around exponent

description: Some legacy Fortran-fronted exporters (older I-DEAS, CADAM converters) emit `1.0D5` instead of `1.0E5`. ISO 10303-21 only allows `E`/`e`.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject with diagnostic "exponent must be 'E', got 'D'".
notes: **See also**: Ls001. Synonyms: "Fortran D exponent in STEP", "1.0D5 instead of 1.0E5", "legacy Fortran writer emits D exponent", "I-DEAS D-exponent REAL", "CADAM D-style exponent".
title: Fortran-style `D` exponent (`1.0D5`)

description: Some generators write `+1.0` for positive REAL. The Part-21 BNF arguably disallows leading `+` for INTEGER but admits it for REAL; uniform handling preferred.
expected_kernel_behavior: Accept signed reals and integers uniformly; never silently strip the sign.
notes: **See also**: Ls001. **OCC behavior**: silently strips the leading `+` sign with no diagnostic on the surrounding context; kernel mishandling; the catalog above expects uniform handling without sign-stripping. Synonyms: "plus sign on positive REAL", "+1.0 in STEP literal", "explicit positive sign on numeric", "STEP rejects leading plus", "INTEGER with explicit plus".
title: Explicit positive sign on numeric literal (`+1.0`)

description: Modern languages tolerate `1_000_000`. Some in-house exporters borrow this and emit `IFCREAL(1_000.0)`. ISO 10303-21 disallows underscores in numerics.
expected_kernel_behavior: Strict reject with clear "underscore not permitted in numeric literal".
notes: **See also**: Ls001. Synonyms: "underscore in numeric literal", "1_000_000 in STEP REAL", "digit grouping in STEP number", "Python-style underscore in STEP", "thousands separator inside number".
title: Numeric literal with embedded underscore digit-grouping

description: `1.0E+999999` parsed via `strtod` yields `inf`; `NaN` results from malformed inputs. Geometry pipelines that compare via `<`/`>` then violate sort invariants in STL containers.
expected_kernel_behavior: Clamp magnitude or reject non-finite where geometry expects finite.
notes: **See also**: Ad014. Synonyms: "1.0E+999999 overflows to infinity", "STEP REAL becomes inf", "NaN from STEP", "infinity in geometry pipeline", "non-finite REAL breaks sort". Provenance tier: bytes-only (Q5 full-corpus 2026-07-01).

description: Spec permits leading zeros and a leading sign on INTEGER but no `0x` hex or interpretation of leading zero as octal. Some tools emit `0x10` or interpret `010` as octal-8.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject hex/octal; accept leading `+` and zeros per spec.
notes: **See also**: Ls001. Synonyms: "hex literal in STEP integer", "0x10 in STEP", "octal interpretation of 010", "STEP integer with 0x prefix", "non-decimal integer literal".

description: ISO 10303-21 §5.2 says LF, CR, TAB, FF are ignored characters; §5.6 says only SPACE, comments, and print directives separate tokens. Strict reading: `#1\t=\tCARTESIAN_POINT(..)` after tab-removal becomes `#1=CARTESIAN_POINT(..)`, but `#1<TAB>2` would become `#12`. Real-world parsers tolerate any ASCII whitespace as a separator. Defects: split keyword `FILE _SCHEMA`, internal whitespace inside `#NNN` references, files with `\r`-only line endings, `\f` between attributes, long-line wrapping inside an instance.
expected_kernel_behavior: Treat any of `\t \f\r\n` as whitespace separator (matches user expectation); preserve line/column counting across line-ending conventions; warn on TAB inside an identifier; accept print-control directives `\F\` and `\N\` as zero-width separators where token separator is allowed; reject embedded whitespace inside `#N` (between `#` and digits).
notes: **See also**: Le028. Synonyms: "tab as STEP token separator", "FF as token separator", "tab between # and =", "ignored char inside STEP token", "whitespace handling in STEP scanner".
reproducer: `FILE _SCHEMA(('AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN'));`, `# 12 = IFCPERSON(..);`, file with CR-only line endings, `#1=IFCPOINT(\F\(0.,0.,0.));`
title: Whitespace handling: tab/CR/LF/FF as token separators or ignored chars

description: A STEP reader parses a malformed file, accumulates syntax errors internally, then reports a generic "parsing failed" status to the caller. Detailed line / column / entity information is logged to stderr but not returned via API. Tools that wrap the reader (via Python / command-line) cannot present diagnostics to users. Typical fixture: two entities with distinct lexical syntax errors; e.g., one with an unclosed parenthesis and another with a missing string-literal quote.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject with structured diagnostics: reader returns a structured diagnostic list with file location, entity ID, and error text per error. Must not silently swallow syntax errors.
notes: **See also**: Ad088. Synonyms: "STEP parser error message inaccessible", "syntax error not surfaced to caller", "unclosed paren error swallowed", "parser warnings don't reach API", "STEP error log not exposed".

description: The Part-21 grammar requires the leaves of a complex entity record (`#1=( A() B() C() )`) to be separated by whitespace, not commas. A writer that emits commas (carrying habit from argument lists) produces a token that a strict reader must reject.

notes: **See also**: Ls010, Ls048. Synonyms: "complex entity leaves separated by commas", "multiple-inheritance leaves with comma separators", "STEP complex record uses commas not whitespace", "comma in complex entity rejected", "complex entity grammar violation".

description: The external mapping of a multiple-inheritance entity must list ALL ancestor leaves, not only the most-specific subtypes. A writer that elides an ancestor (e.g. `NAMED_UNIT` between `CONVERSION_BASED_UNIT` and `PLANE_ANGLE_UNIT`) produces a record that resolves ambiguously on dispatch.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject the record (or accept-with-warning and synthesise the missing ancestor); never silently bind to an arbitrary subset of the type lattice.
notes: **See also**: Ls010, Ls047. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); catalog disallows silent-accept. Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers enforcing the spec must reject (or surface a diagnostic); silent acceptance defeats the catalog's stated invariant. description: ISO 10303-21 distinguishes INTEGER and REAL literals; a REAL carries a mandatory decimal point. A count/degree/dimension attribute typed INTEGER in the EXPRESS schema must not receive a REAL literal. The fixture writes the REAL literal `3.0` in the `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` degree slot, where the integer `3` is required. This is the inverse of Ls001 (integer written where a REAL is required). A real-first tokenizer (`untyped_parameter` tries `real` before `integer`) mis-types `3.0` as a REAL parameter and may silently truncate it.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject or warn on a non-integral value in an INTEGER slot; never silently truncate `3.0` to `3`.
notes: **See also**: Ls001. **OCC behavior**: silently accepts (no diagnostic, empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject, warn-and-proceed}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers enforcing the spec must reject or emit a diagnostic. Synonyms: "REAL where INTEGER expected", "degree given 3.0", "count field carries a decimal point", "fractional value in integer slot", "float literal in STEP integer attribute". Provenance tier: bytes-only. Expected validation is provisional (best-guess) pending oracle rebaseline — the live occt/gmsh oracle is not run here (platform divergence); nightly CI reconciles.

description: A complex (subsuper / combined-entity) instance is written as a parenthesized list of simple records, e.g. `#1=(A(...)B(...))`. A `many0`-style parser accepts an EMPTY list `()`, i.e. a complex instance with ZERO constituent records. A complex instance must combine at least one (really at least two) simple records; the empty form is meaningless. Distinct from Ls013 (`PRODUCT()` — keyword present, no attributes): here there is no keyword at all, just `()`. The empty complex `#1` is reachable (referenced as a GEOMETRIC_SET item), so a parser must process it rather than skip dead code.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject the empty complex instance; the lexer may accept `()` as a zero-record list, but the semantic layer must reject "0 constituent records, expected >=1".
notes: **See also**: Ls013. **OCC behavior**: OCC loads the file and produces no shape (empty). Re-audit (2026-07-18, empty-claim re-audit): the only model-root geometry is a `GEOMETRIC_SET` referencing a `CARTESIAN_POINT`, which has no shape-representation root and OCC transfers to no shape even when well-formed (confirmed by a matching well-formed control — loads empty); the declared Part-21 syntax defect cannot manifest as lost geometry (base and clean both empty). Toy/placeholder topology, not a defect-driven data-loss; not a proven kernel bug. Synonyms: "empty subsuper instance", "complex entity with no records", "keyword-less empty parens instance", "zero-record combined entity", "STEP empty complex #1=()". Provenance tier: bytes-only. Expected validation is provisional (best-guess) pending oracle rebaseline — the live occt/gmsh oracle is not run here (platform divergence); nightly CI reconciles.
reproducer: `#1=(); #2=CARTESIAN_POINT('p',(0.,0.,0.)); #3=GEOMETRIC_SET('gs',(#1,#2));` — `#1` is an empty complex instance referenced by `#3`.

description: ISO 10303-21 §6.3 block comments are delimited by an opening `/*` and a closing `*/`. A parser that requires the closer fails if it is missing; an unterminated comment consumes every byte to end-of-file, silently swallowing the section terminators (`ENDSEC` / `END-ISO-10303-21;`). The fixture opens a comment in the DATA section after a valid CARTESIAN_POINT and never closes it, so the remainder of the file — including the close bookend — is eaten. A conformant reader must reject with an unterminated-comment diagnostic; it must not hang or silently drop the tail.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject with an unterminated-comment diagnostic; never hang, and never silently drop the swallowed file tail.
notes: **See also**: Ls056. **OCC behavior**: rejects with a parse diagnostic (`Undefined Parsing: ... Incorrect...`) on both `occt_heal_on`/`occt_heal_off` and `gmsh_autofix_on`/`gmsh_autofix_off` — matches this entry's own "Expected kernel behavior" (reject with an unterminated-comment diagnostic; never hang, never silently drop the tail). Synonyms: "unterminated comment", "missing */ closer", "comment runs to EOF", "STEP comment never closed", "dangling /* opener". Provenance tier: bytes-only. DRIFT audit 2026-07-12: live-verified (macOS OCP/OCCT 7.8.1, matching CI-Linux) — corrected the placeholder `empty/empty` guess to the observed `reject/reject`, which is the spec-conformant behavior this entry asks for.
reproducer: `#1=CARTESIAN_POINT('origin',(0.,0.,0.));` followed by `/* note ...` with no closing `*/` before EOF.
sources: Pattern-mined from ricosjp/ruststep combinator.rs::comment (`tag("/*") ... tag("*/")` fails if the closer is missing) (Apache-2.0/MIT — pattern only, no bytes copied)
title: Unterminated block comment (no closing `*/`) swallows the file tail

description: ISO 10303-21 §6.3 block comments do NOT nest. In `/* a /* b */ tail */` the comment closes at the FIRST `*/`, so the inner `/*` is not an opener — it is comment text. Whatever follows the first closer is live token stream, and the final `*/` is a stray, unmatched closer (a lexical error). An author who tries to comment out an entity but nests a second opener inside will have that entity LEAK back into the parse: here `#2=CARTESIAN_POINT('leaked',...)` re-enters the token stream and a stray `*/` trails it.
expected_kernel_behavior: Treat comments as non-nesting per the spec and reject the stray `*/`; document the non-nesting rule clearly so authors do not rely on nested-comment behavior.
notes: **See also**: Ls055. **OCC behavior**: OCC loads the file and produces no shape (empty). Re-audit (2026-07-18, empty-claim re-audit): the only model-root geometry is loose `DIRECTION`s and a leaked `CARTESIAN_POINT`, which has no shape-representation root and OCC transfers to no shape even when well-formed (confirmed by a matching well-formed control — loads empty); the declared Part-21 syntax defect cannot manifest as lost geometry (base and clean both empty). Toy/placeholder topology, not a defect-driven data-loss; not a proven kernel bug. Synonyms: "nested comment illusion", "comments do not nest", "stray */", "leaked entity from comment", "unmatched comment closer", "double */ after entity". Provenance tier: bytes-only. Expected validation is provisional (best-guess) pending oracle rebaseline — the live occt/gmsh oracle is not run here (platform divergence); nightly CI reconciles.
reproducer: `/* a /* b */ #2=CARTESIAN_POINT('leaked',(0.,0.,0.)); */` — comment = `/* a /* b */`; the CARTESIAN_POINT leaks; the trailing `*/` is stray.
sources: Pattern-mined from ricosjp/ruststep combinator.rs::comment (non-nesting) (Apache-2.0/MIT — pattern only, no bytes copied)
title: Non-nesting comment illusion; inner opener leaves a stray closer

description: An `EDGE_CURVE` bounding a face has only its 3D curve populated; no parametric (pcurve) representation accompanies the edge on its host surface. Many writers strip pcurves entirely or fail to compute them per-face. Receivers that assume every edge-on-face has a pcurve dereference null and crash; receivers that tolerate the absence must reconstruct the pcurve by projecting the 3D curve onto the surface.
expected_kernel_behavior: synthesise the missing pcurve by projecting the 3D curve onto the host surface, or reject the input as malformed. Never dereference a null pcurve handle.
notes: Cross-oracle: pure-Python Part-21 validator accepts (`accept`); OCCT crashes (`signal(11)`). The crash is on the kernel side; the file is spec-conformant Part-21.
reproducer: `EDGE_CURVE` references a 3D `LINE`/`B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` and bounds an `ADVANCED_FACE`; the corresponding `SURFACE_CURVE.associated_geometry` lacks any `PCURVE` entry. With STEP writer flag "Write out curves in parametric space of surface" enabled but no cached pcurve.
sender: STEP exporters in 3D-only mode; IGES BRep round-trips; Multiboard parts library

description: An `EDGE_CURVE` carries a `PCURVE` whose evaluation at its parameter endpoints does not match the edge's `VERTEX_POINT` 3D positions. Lifting the pcurve through the host surface (`CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE`, `PLANE`, etc.) lands at a different point than the edge's vertex coordinates. Typical pattern: 3D edge endpoints are at (10,0,0)–(10,0,5) on a cylinder of radius 10 (so the pcurve start should be at u=0,v=0), but the pcurve runs from (u=0,v=0) to (u=π/2,v=5); pcurve endpoints disagree with vertex 3D positions. Often produced when a foreign translator regenerated pcurves without coordinating with vertices, so the pcurve and the vertex disagree about where the edge starts.
expected_kernel_behavior: drop the bad pcurve and recompute it from the 3D curve, or reject as malformed. Keeping the pcurve without verification produces silent geometric corruption.
notes: **OCC behavior**: accepts and loads shape(1); OCC's STEP reader recomputes the pcurve from the 3D curve on transfer (per Gp193), so the declared 2D/pcurve defect does not survive into the built shape. Perturbing the declared defect from clean to grossly exaggerated leaves the built shape unchanged in both shape-counts and BRepCheck validity (heal_on and heal_off), so the shape-count oracle cannot distinguish it from a clean input; shape(1) does not witness a kernel bug. Synonyms: "pcurve endpoints don't match vertex coordinates", "2D parameter curve start/end disagrees with vertex 3D position", "lifted pcurve lands at wrong point", "edge vertices and pcurve disagree about endpoint location", "pcurve evaluation at endpoint differs from vertex_point".
reproducer: `EDGE_CURVE` whose `PCURVE` start/end points (lifted via the host surface) differ from `VERTEX_POINT` coordinates by more than vertex tolerance.
sender: IGES re-import (pcurves recomputed independently of 3D curves)
title: Pcurve endpoints disagree with edge vertex 3D positions

description: Projecting a 3D curve through the singular pole of a sphere or apex of a cone produces an indeterminate UV path; the parametric domain has a degenerate row where the surface map becomes non-injective. Surface-surface intersection and face translation routines misbehave near these singularities, and any wire that touches the singular point lacks a definitive UV image.

description: After a period-shift pass on a revolved face's wire, the wire endpoints land in an inconsistent parameter band — some pcurve endpoints in `[0,2π]`, others in `[2π,4π]` — even though all should sit in a single period band. The inconsistency blocks subsequent triangulation, which expects a single coherent parameter window.
expected_kernel_behavior: a period-shift pass must produce a self-consistent UV band for all wire endpoints, or refuse the shift when no consistent band exists. A post-condition check on the band coverage catches the inconsistency.
notes: **See also**: Gs019. **OCC behavior**: accepts and loads shape(1); OCC's STEP reader recomputes the pcurve from the 3D curve on transfer (per Gp193), so the declared 2D/pcurve defect does not survive into the built shape. Perturbing the declared defect from clean to grossly exaggerated leaves the built shape unchanged in both shape-counts and BRepCheck validity (heal_on and heal_off), so the shape-count oracle cannot distinguish it from a clean input; shape(1) does not witness a kernel bug. Synonyms: "period-shift fix leaves wire across multiple bands", "wire endpoints in inconsistent UV bands after period adjust", "triangulation blocked by mixed-band pcurves", "revolved face period shift fails to converge", "pcurve endpoints scattered across periods after healing".
reproducer: Face on a `SURFACE_OF_REVOLUTION` whose pcurves require shifting by 2π; run the period-shift pass; attempt to mesh.
title: Period-shift fix on revolved face leaves wire in inconsistent UV band, blocks meshing

description: PRO/E exports (identifiable by `originating_system` 'PRO/Engineer …' in `FILE_NAME`) contain pcurves with sharp bends, typically authored as degree-1 `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` in `.POLYLINE_FORM.` with vendor-specific interior knot multiplicities. These vendor-shaped B-spline pcurves must be protected from generic intersection-fix routines that would otherwise corrupt them. A specialized "bend-pcurve" pass holds the pcurve fixed while neighbors are adjusted.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; recognize PRO/E sender and route bent pcurves through the protective branch.
notes: **OCC behavior**: accepts and loads shape(1); OCC's STEP reader recomputes the pcurve from the 3D curve on transfer (per Gp193), so the declared 2D/pcurve defect does not survive into the built shape. Perturbing the declared defect from clean to grossly exaggerated leaves the built shape unchanged in both shape-counts and BRepCheck validity (heal_on and heal_off), so the shape-count oracle cannot distinguish it from a clean input; shape(1) does not witness a kernel bug. Synonyms: "PRO/E polyline-form pcurve gets corrupted by intersection healer", "bent B-spline pcurve from PRO/Engineer", "pcurve sharp bend killed by generic ShapeFix", "polyline pcurve degree-1 with vendor multiplicities", "wire intersection fix damages PRO/E pcurve".
reproducer: PRO/E STEP file with a face whose pcurve has a sharp bend; run generic ShapeFix wire intersection healing; observe pcurve corruption.
sender: PRO/E (`PRO7978.igs`, `PRO10107.stp`)
title: Bent / polyline-form `B_SPLINE` pcurve from PRO/E IGES requires protective handling

description: After an IGES BRep round-trip (or other translator path), a cylindrical face appears with two distinct but identically-defined `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` instances (e.g. `#20` and `#21`) where each `ADVANCED_FACE` uses one copy; analytic identity is lost. A single 3D edge then has two pcurves on these supposedly-same surfaces; duplicate surface definitions and aliased pcurves create confusion, and pcurves stored against the second copy disagree with those against the first even though geometrically identical.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; canonicalize duplicate analytic surfaces post-IGES; re-bind pcurves to the canonical surface.
notes: **See also**: Gn023, Gp016. **OCC behavior**: accepts and loads shape(1); OCC's STEP reader recomputes the pcurve from the 3D curve on transfer (per Gp193), so the declared 2D/pcurve defect does not survive into the built shape. Perturbing the declared defect from clean to grossly exaggerated leaves the built shape unchanged in both shape-counts and BRepCheck validity (heal_on and heal_off), so the shape-count oracle cannot distinguish it from a clean input; shape(1) does not witness a kernel bug. Synonyms: "duplicate CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE instances after IGES BRep round-trip", "cylinder analytic identity lost", "two copies of same cylindrical surface", "duplicate analytic surfaces after IGES round-trip", "pcurves on supposedly-same cylinder disagree".
reproducer: Cylindrical face → IGES BRep → re-import; check that all faces of the cylinder share the same `Geom_CylindricalSurface` handle.
title: Cylinder represented twice as duplicate `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` instances loses analytic identity

description: A B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS has an internal knot whose multiplicity equals the degree, producing only C0 continuity at that parameter. Downstream meshers, fillet/chamfer engines, and IGES exporters that assume at least C1 mis-handle the discontinuity and emit kinks where the source intended a smooth join.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect the C0 break and either split the curve into two C∞-internal pieces, raise the knot multiplicity to enforce a true G1+ join, or report the discontinuity as a quality metric so downstream tools can handle it explicitly.
notes: Same defect applies to pcurve splitting on host surfaces. **OCC behavior**: accepts with ERR diagnostic (empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({heal}). Kernel-bug witnessed: catalog asks for healing; OCC neither heals nor rejects; the input is dropped on the floor without diagnostic. Synonyms: "B-spline curve has C0 internal break", "interior knot multiplicity equals degree creates kink", "downstream tools cannot ingest C0 spline", "knot multiplicity=degree produces visible cusp", "B-spline kink at interior knot".
reproducer: Degree-2 B-spline whose knot vector is `(0,0,0, 0.5,0.5,0.5, 1,1,1)` — multiplicity 3 at u=0.5 forces C0; control polygon does not have collinear neighbors at the breakpoint.
title: B-spline curve has C0 internal break that downstream tools cannot ingest

description: A `COMPOSITE_CURVE` lists multiple segments that are intended to form a single continuous curve. Segment N's last 3D point sits at a distance of several millimetres from segment N+1's first 3D point; far beyond any reasonable connectivity tolerance. The composite curve is not actually connected; treating it as one curve produces invalid downstream geometry.
expected_kernel_behavior: report the connectivity defect with the offending segment indices and 3D gap; either bridge the segments by inserting a connecting curve, snap endpoints, or refuse to treat the aggregate as a single curve.
notes: Similar defect class to `Twi-` wire connectivity but at the curve-aggregate level. **OCC behavior**: accepts and loads shape(1); OCC does not transfer the COMPOSITE_CURVE into the face wire at all (the face loads with no edges), so the declared 3D inter-segment gap never reaches the built shape. Dialing the gap from 0 to 0.5 mm leaves shape-counts and BRepCheck validity unchanged, so the shape-count oracle cannot distinguish it from a gap-free input; shape(1) does not witness a kernel bug. Synonyms: "composite curve segments don't meet", "gap between consecutive composite curve segments", "composite_curve has disconnected segments", "segment N+1 starts far from segment N's end", "composite curve connectivity check fails".
reproducer: Two LINE-based EDGE_CURVEs whose vertices are at `(5,0,0)` and `(5.005,0,0)` respectively. Both edges share a wire but the kernel must report a 5e-3 disconnect.
title: Composite curve segments do not meet within connectivity tolerance

description: An edge on an analytic surface (cylinder, cone, sphere, torus, plane) carries a 3D space curve but no 2D pcurve. To trim the surface, the kernel must project the 3D curve into UV. Some senders never emit pcurves, expecting the consumer to compute them; the projection must remain same-parameter and may resolve to an analytic 2D primitive (line in UV) where the geometry permits.
expected_kernel_behavior: synthesize the missing pcurve via projection, validate same-parameter consistency afterwards, and emit an analytic 2D line where the underlying surface admits one (e.g., on cylinders, spheres). Alternatively, refuse the edge and require a sender that supplies pcurves.
notes: Distinct from a *bad* pcurve (Twi-class). Also see Gp019 (edge without pcurve). **OCC behavior**: accepts and loads shape(1); the edge carrying only a bare 3D curve (no pcurve) is transferred by synthesizing its pcurve via projection (the documented heal), building a complete, BRepCheck-valid 4-edge face. The declared missing-pcurve defect thus does not survive into the built shape; the shape-count oracle cannot distinguish it from a pcurve-supplied input, so shape(1) does not witness a kernel bug. Synonyms: "edge has no parametric curve", "pcurve absent on face edge", "tessellator fails on edge with no UV curve", "kernel must project 3D curve onto surface", "edge without 2D representation needs synthesis".
reproducer: A vertical EDGE_CURVE on a CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE running from `(R,0,0)` to `(R,0,h)` with only a 3D LINE representation, no SURFACE_CURVE pcurve.
title: Edge has 3D curve but no pcurve, requiring projection onto host surface

description: A 2D-curve-shift routine intended for periodic surfaces is invoked on a planar (non-periodic) surface. The routine shifts the pcurve by the surface's "period"; but on a non-periodic surface the period is undefined, returning zero or NaN. The pcurve becomes invalid.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject as precondition error: pcurve-shifting only runs on surfaces flagged periodic; non-periodic surface invocation is a precondition error.
notes: **See also**: Twi084, Gp008. Synonyms: "pcurve shift on non-periodic surface", "period shift applied to planar surface returns NaN", "pcurve shift routine misfires on plane", "shift-by-period on non-periodic surface degenerates", "shifting pcurves on flat surface gives invalid result".
reproducer: Planar face with a wire whose pcurves were emitted with U values outside the face's parametric range. Healer applies a shift; on planar surface the shift is degenerate.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0028595 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Pcurve shifting on non-periodic surface produces wrong result

description: A projection of a 3D curve onto a surface produces a 2D curve that extends infinitely in the parametric domain instead of being bounded to the input curve's parameter range. Downstream consumers (face-bound check, mesher) read the unbounded curve and either crash or produce infinite tessellation.
expected_kernel_behavior: projection range matches input range exactly; never produce unbounded pcurves from bounded inputs.
notes: **See also**: Gp035. Synonyms: "pcurve projection produces unbounded line", "projection emits infinite parameter range", "bounded 3D curve becomes infinite pcurve after projection", "unbounded pcurve crashes mesher", "projection range doesn't match input curve range".
reproducer: 3D curve segment with parameter range `[0,1]`; project onto plane. Resulting pcurve has parameter range `[-∞, +∞]`.
sources: OCCT MANTIS#0026198 (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Pcurve projection produces infinite line instead of bounded

description: An edge's vertex point in 3D and the pcurve evaluated at the corresponding parameter disagree beyond vertex tolerance. The edge passes 3D-curve-vs-vertex check (because 3D curve does match vertex) but fails 2D-pcurve check.
expected_kernel_behavior: Reject if either fails: vertex-pcurve consistency check separate from vertex-3D-curve check; both must pass independently.
notes: **See also**: Twi060, Twi088, Twi059. Synonyms: "vertex 3D point and pcurve disagree at endpoint", "pcurve evaluation at edge endpoint differs from vertex", "vertex-pcurve consistency check fails", "edge passes 3D check but fails 2D check", "UV at parameter doesn't lift to vertex 3D position".
reproducer: Edge with vertex V at `(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)`; 3D curve is a line from `(1.0, 0.0, 0.0)` to `(2.0, 0.0, 0.0)`. Pcurve on the hosting face evaluates at parameter 0 to UV `(0.5, 0.0)` whose 3D image is `(1.05, 0.0, 0.0)` — beyond vertex tolerance.

description: A 3D B-spline curve, closed (first control point == last), is projected onto a surface to compute a pcurve. The projection algorithm walks the curve with discontinuity at the closing seam; the resulting pcurve has a wild excursion near the seam, parameter range no longer matches the input curve's range.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: closed-curve projection treats the seam as a continuity constraint; pcurve range matches input range; no spike. Must not silently produce spike.
notes: **See also**: Gp037, Twi088. Synonyms: "pcurve projection unstable on closed B-spline", "spike in pcurve at closure seam", "closed-curve projection has wild excursion at seam", "projection of closed B-spline produces wrong parameter range", "pcurve bumps near closing seam of periodic curve".
reproducer: Closed B-spline curve (degree 3, 8 control points with first == last); project onto plane. Pcurve has spike at seam parameter.
title: Pcurve projection unstable on closed B-spline curve

category: §12.2a pcurve defects (sub-class: writer-emitted pcurves disagree with 3D)
description: When pcurves are emitted alongside 3D curves on `EDGE_CURVE`, every receiver re-projects them to verify consistency. The writer's pcurve, computed by a separate pass after the 3D curve is fixed, often disagrees with the 3D curve at the edge tolerance; a re-import yields edges that drift off the surface, faces with `BRepCheck_InvalidEdgeOnSurface` errors, or sewing failures. The community workaround is to disable pcurve emission entirely; the kernel-side bug is that the two representations are not co-fitted.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; pcurves must be co-fitted with the 3D curve so that surface-evaluated pcurve and 3D curve agree within the edge tolerance; if they cannot be fitted, omit the pcurve and let the receiver re-project.
notes: **See also**: Gp028, Tfa023. Synonyms: "STEP writer pcurves disagree with 3D curves", "disable writing pcurves to STEP and IGES by default", "edge tolerance violated by writer pcurve", "pcurve drift after STEP round-trip".
reproducer: STEP file with `SURFACE_CURVE` carrying both a 3D curve and a `PCURVE` whose 2D parametric curve evaluates ~ε off the 3D curve when projected onto the surface. Receiver reports edge-on-surface tolerance violation.
sender: OCCT's STEP writer when configured to emit pcurves (`write.surfacecurve.mode = 1`).
sources: bug-reporter language: "disable writing pcurves to STEP and IGES by default", "pcurves and 3D curves disagree on round-trip", "writer-emitted pcurves cause downstream failures". (OCCT MANTIS tracker 502 as of 2026-05-02)
title: Pcurves emitted by default duplicate / contradict the surface 3D curve

description: STEP file with a planar face (`PLANE`, z=0, normal +Z) bounded by a single `FACE_OUTER_BOUND` containing one `ORIENTED_EDGE` whose basis is a `CIRCLE` (radius=5.0, axis=+Z, center at origin). `edge_start` and `edge_end` are two **distinct** `VERTEX_POINT` entities — V1 at (5.0, 0.0, 0.0) and V2 at (5.0, −1e-8, 0.0) — separated by ~1e-8 m, which is within the declared `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT = 1e-7`. The circle's parametric extent runs from θ=0 to θ≈2π−2×10⁻⁹ rad (not exactly 2π). Some readers collapse the two vertices into one (treating the loop as closed); others preserve both vertices and produce a wire with a near-zero-length free edge at the closure point.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect near-coincident `edge_start`/`edge_end` on a closed-curve `EDGE_CURVE` when vertex gap < declared tolerance; collapse to a single vertex and treat as a true closed loop; emit `W_NEAR_COINCIDENT_CLOSURE_VERTICES`.
notes: OCCT MANTIS 0027634. B4 wave-6 DEF-DD. Synonyms: "full-circle edge with two vertices at closure", "CIRCLE EDGE_CURVE edge_start edge_end near-coincident", "near-degenerate circle closure vertex", "two distinct vertices on full-revolution CIRCLE", "zero-length free edge at closure point".
reproducer: `CIRCLE(radius=5)` on z=0 `PLANE`; `EDGE_CURVE` with `edge_start=VERTEX_POINT((5,0,0))` and `edge_end=VERTEX_POINT((5,-1e-8,0))`; `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT=1e-7`; single `ORIENTED_EDGE` in the `FACE_OUTER_BOUND`. OCCT loads the face (shape(1)) with 2 vertex entries both resolving to (5,0,0) and 1 edge.
sender: STEP exporters that emit a full-circle `EDGE_CURVE` with `edge_start` ≠ `edge_end` but at distance < `UNCERTAINTY_MEASURE_WITH_UNIT`; common in CATIA/SolidWorks exports of near-degenerate revolution features.

description: STEP file with two adjacent `ADVANCED_FACE` entities: F1 on surface S1 (`PLANE`, y=0, normal +Y, the XZ plane) and F2 on surface S2 (`CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE`, radius=3, axis +Z). They share edge E: a `LINE` from (3,0,0) to (3,0,5) (lies on both y=0 and x²+y²=9). The `SURFACE_CURVE` for edge E carries two `PCURVE` entries. The pcurve for F2 correctly references S2 (cylinder). **THE DEFECT**: the pcurve for F1 (the plane) has its `basis_surface` attribute pointing to S2 (the cylindrical surface) instead of S1 (the plane). The 3D curve of E is correct. OCCT loads the shape but `brepcheck` flags it as invalid; gmsh rejects ("Could not fix wire in surface 1"); the wrong surface UV domain is used to evaluate the planar face boundary.
expected_kernel_behavior: validate `PCURVE.basis_surface` against the `ADVANCED_FACE.face_geometry` for each face that uses the edge; emit `E_PCURVE_WRONG_BASIS_SURFACE` when the surface IDs do not match; reject or warn before propagating incorrect UV bounds to downstream operations.
notes: OCCT MANTIS 0030124. B4 wave-6 DEF-EE. Synonyms: "PCURVE basis_surface wrong surface reference", "PCURVE points at adjacent face surface", "wrong basis surface in PCURVE", "PCURVE.basis_surface mismatch", "adjacent face surface UV error pcurve".
reproducer: Two `ADVANCED_FACE`s sharing an `EDGE_CURVE` via a `SURFACE_CURVE`; the `SURFACE_CURVE` lists two `PCURVE`s; the pcurve for the `PLANE` face encodes `PCURVE('...',#CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE,...)` (wrong `basis_surface`). OCCT: `shape(1)`, `brepcheck=False`; gmsh: reject.
sender: STEP exporters that copy a `PCURVE` from one face to an adjacent face without updating the `basis_surface` reference; common in translation pipelines that share `SURFACE_CURVE` entities between adjacent faces but emit separate `PCURVE` slots with the wrong surface ID.

category: §12-2a pcurves (sub-class: sampled projection fallback + endpoint extremity correction)
description: An `EDGE_CURVE` (`#24`) has a 3D geometry that is a general, non-iso, cubic `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` (`#11`, control points near but not on a radius-5 `SPHERICAL_SURFACE` `#5`) tracing a diagonal path from `(5,0,0)` toward the north pole. There is no closed-form analytic projection of a general B-spline onto a sphere, so `ShapeConstruct_ProjectCurveOnSurface` cannot use its analytic path and falls back to the **sampled** branch: it evaluates the 3D curve at a fixed grid of sample points (~23), projects each onto the sphere, and approximates a B-spline pcurve through the projected 2D points. The approximated pcurve's endpoints do not land exactly on the vertex UV parameters, so `correctExtremity` must nudge the projected 2D endpoints back onto the vertices. Two additional stressors are baked in: the supplied pcurve (`#22`) is a crude straight 2D `LINE` that does not match the true projection, and the terminal `VERTEX_POINT` (`#13`, `(0.02,0.48,4.98)`) is offset ~0.02 mm from the 3D curve endpoint, forcing a real (non-zero) endpoint residual. OCCT loads the shape (`shape(1)`) after running the sampled projection and adding the sphere's natural bounds (seam + pole degenerate edges), so the single declared edge becomes a 5-edge, 10-vertex healed face.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect that no analytic projection exists, sample the 3D curve, approximate the pcurve, and snap the projected extremities to the vertex parameters within tolerance; or reject the edge if the sampled approximation exceeds the edge tolerance. The residual endpoint gap must be closed by re-projecting the vertices, not left as a `SameParameter` violation.
notes: OCCT `ShapeConstruct_ProjectCurveOnSurface` sampled-fallback + `correctExtremity`. B4 wave-12 repair-code mining. **See also**: Gp005 (apex-projection singularity), Gp008 (oscillating projected pcurve), Gp072 (`FixAddPCurve` planar projection). Distinct from those: this is the **sampled-approximation** path taken when analytic projection is unavailable on a curved surface, plus the endpoint-extremity correction sub-step. Provenance tier: runtime-only — the bytes encode only the trigger geometry (non-analytic 3D B-spline + placeholder pcurve + offset vertex); whether the projector uses the sampled branch and how `correctExtremity` nudges the endpoints manifests only at kernel runtime. category: §12.2a pcurve (sub-class: edge crossing a surface singularity in its interior — `tkshh-edge-crossing-surface-singularity`, subvariant a)
description: A `SPHERICAL_SURFACE` (radius 1) face has one edge (`polar_edge`) whose 3D curve is the great-circle `CIRCLE` lying in the XZ-plane, running from equator vertex `A=(1,0,0)` through the NORTH POLE `(0,0,1)` — strictly the parameter-range MIDPOINT, not an endpoint — down to equator vertex `B=(-1,0,0)`. This is the case Xp013 and Gp048 do not cover: both of those touch the singularity only at an edge ENDPOINT (a vertex sits exactly at the apex/pole). The edge's pcurve is a single straight UV line `v=0` constant from `(u=0,v=0)` to `(u=pi,v=0)` — the naive "apex-adjacent" patch job the work packet calls insufficient: it treats the edge as though it stayed on the equator the whole way, when the true path needs `u` to jump `0->pi` exactly at `v=pi/2` (the pole), which one pcurve cannot represent. A second, healthy edge closes the loop via the equator's *other* semicircle (through the back, negative-Y side, touching neither pole), giving a real 2-edge lune face with non-degenerate area.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect that the 3D curve's interior crosses the surface singularity, split the edge into two sub-edges at the singularity parameter (inserting a degenerate vertex at the pole), and give each sub-edge its own clean pcurve — not patch a single pcurve near the apex.
notes: **See also**: Xp013 (apex touched only at a shared, non-manifold vertex — an endpoint case), Gp048 (apex is an edge endpoint, degenerate pcurve construction), Gp178 (companion subvariant: pole + periodic seam together). **OCC behavior**: heals, but not into a clean 2-sub-edge split — OCCT fragments the single input edge into many small sub-edges with escalating vertex tolerance as they approach the pole (from 1 input edge and 1 input face the healer emits several faces and a double-digit sub-edge count — observed as both 3 faces/18 edges and 6 faces/24 edges on different runs of the SAME build), rather than the idealized single split at the singularity parameter. The exact tally is NOT reproducible run-to-run, so the tier-3 assertion pins only the invariant that matters — fragmentation occurred (`n_faces_total > 1` from one input face) — rather than a brittle exact count. `shape(1)` (root count) on both heal on/off; `brepcheck` reports valid. gmsh triangulates the fragmented result to `shape(38)` (CI-Linux authoritative; macOS-ARM reports `shape(32)` on the same bytes — the fragmentation is a floating-point-sensitive tessellation artifact, so this count is platform-dependent and the CI value is the baseline). Synonyms: "edge interior crosses cone apex or sphere pole", "single pcurve cannot represent a pole-crossing edge", "apex-adjacent pcurve patch insufficient for interior singularity", "edge must be split at singularity parameter not just re-pcurved", "great-circle edge passes through pole at its midpoint".
reproducer: `SPHERICAL_SURFACE` radius 1; `EDGE_CURVE` whose 3D curve is a great-circle `CIRCLE` oriented so its parameter range's midpoint lands exactly on the pole (not an endpoint); its `PCURVE` is a single straight line that does not reflect the pole crossing; a second `EDGE_CURVE` (equatorial semicircle avoiding both poles) closes a 2-edge `EDGE_LOOP`.

category: §12.2a pcurve (sub-class: invalid same-range flag, face-hosted subvariant — `bc-invalid-same-range-flag`)
description: An `EDGE_CURVE` declares `same_range=.T.`, asserting that its 3D-curve parameter range and its pcurve's parameter range are identical, when in fact they genuinely differ: the 3D `LINE` spans `[0,10]` while the paired `PCURVE`'s UV `LINE` spans `[0,5]`. This is Twi082's exact numeric mismatch, but wired into a real `ADVANCED_FACE` on a `PLANE` instead of an orphan `GEOMETRIC_CURVE_SET` — so translation actually binds the pcurve to a face rather than yielding an empty shape.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect the range mismatch and flag the same-range validity status, or reject/repair with a diagnostic rather than silently trusting the flag.
notes: **See also**: Twi082 (identical numeric defect, orphan `GEOMETRIC_CURVE_SET`, `occt=empty`). **Empirical finding (live-verified, OCP/OCCT 7.8.1)**: this fixture DOES reach a live face (`occt=shape(1)`, unlike Twi082) — that portion of the packet's ask is achieved. However, `BRep_Tool::Range(edge, face)` on the translated shape reads back `(0.0, 10.0)`, NOT the authored `(0.0, 5.0)` — OCCT's the edge-translation stage unconditionally rescales the pcurve's parameter domain to match the 3D curve during ordinary edge construction (confirmed under both `occt_heal_on` and `occt_heal_off` Interface_Static profiles; `BRep_Tool::SameRange(edge)` still reads `True` post-translation, but the underlying ranges have already been silently reconciled). Consequently the edge validity checker (Blind and `InContext(face)`) reports a no-error verdict, not the same-range validity status, on the final the loaded shape — the lie is healed away before any checker could observe it. This is consistent with the class's own `detect_only: true` tag in `problems.json`: the defect is a genuine, byte-level Part-21 malformation (useful for a static/structural linter) but appears to be structurally unobservable as a live `BRepCheck` finding via the standard STEP import pipeline, regardless of face-hosting. No fixture (this one included) has yet demonstrated a translated shape whose the edge validity checker actually flags `InvalidSameRangeFlag` via the standard reader path; see runtime-scaffold finding below for a direct-construction demonstration. **Runtime-scaffold verification (2026-07-16)**: bypassing the reader/translator entirely — constructing the identical byte-level defect (3D range `[0,10]`, pcurve range `[0,5]`, `SameRange` asserted `True`) directly via `BRep_Builder` — reproduces the lie undisturbed, and `BRepCheck_Edge`/`BRepCheck_Analyzer` genuinely fire `BRepCheck_InvalidSameRangeFlag` (plus `InvalidSameParameterFlag`) on it, live-confirmed. category: §12.2a pcurve (sub-class: curve continuity below required criterion — `seq-split-continuity`, curve subvariant)
description: The bottom edge of a rectangular `PLANE` face uses a degree-2 `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS`, 5 control points, knot vector `(0,0,0,0.5,0.5,1,1,1)` (multiplicities `(3,2,3)`): interior multiplicity equals the degree, giving genuine C0 continuity — position-continuous, tangent-discontinuous — at `u=0.5`. The control point exactly at the shared knot sits on the straight line between the edge's endpoints (so 3D position stays continuous), but the neighbouring poles are offset in different axes (`+Y` before the knot, `+Z` after), so the incoming and outgoing tangent directions genuinely differ. The edge is wired through a live `EDGE_CURVE`/`PCURVE` into a reachable, 4-edge `ADVANCED_FACE` — unlike Gp033 (`occt=empty`, `shape_null=True`) or Gn172 (orphan pattern, defect curve unreferenced by any live `EDGE_CURVE`/`PCURVE`).
expected_kernel_behavior: detect the sub-C1 interior knot and split the curve at the discontinuity (the continuity-splitting stage) so downstream consumers requiring C1 receive two valid pieces instead of one curve with a hidden kink.
notes: **See also**: Gp033 (curve subvariant's original attempt, `shape_null=True`), Gn172 (orphan pattern), Gp120 (pcurve subvariant, survives), Gs049/Gs070 (surface subvariant, survives). **Empirical finding (live-verified)**: the packet spec (mirroring Gp033's own recipe) asked for interior multiplicity `= degree+1` (3, for a degree-2 curve). Tested directly against `Geom_BSplineCurve`'s constructor: multiplicity 3 at an INTERIOR knot is rejected outright ("`BSpline curve: # Poles and degree mismatch`") — OCCT only permits `degree+1` multiplicity at the first/last knot of a clamped curve, never interior. This is exactly why Gp033 is `shape_null` — the curve entity never constructs, so translation fails before the edge is reachable. This fixture instead uses interior multiplicity `= degree` (2), the textbook C0 case, which OCCT accepts. Live-verified via direct curve evaluation on the translated edge: overall `Continuity() == GeomAbs_C0`, `NbIntervals(GeomAbs_C1) == 2` (exactly one C1-break, located at parameter 0.5), position at the break is `(5,0,0)` on both sides (continuous), but the unit tangent evaluated at `0.5 - 1e-5` is `(0.972, -0.233, 0.0)` while at `0.5 + 1e-5` it is `(0.972, 0.0, 0.233)` — genuinely different directions, confirming a real tangent-discontinuous kink (not an accidental smooth pass-through). An earlier symmetric pole choice (bump `+Z` before, `-Z` after, both offset equally) was tested first and turned out to produce IDENTICAL tangents on both sides (an accidental C1 pass-through despite the double knot) — discarded once live-verified; the asymmetric-axis bump shipped here is the one that live-confirmed a genuine kink.

category: §12.2a pcurve (sub-class: SameParameter repair, ill-conditioned knot-ratio subvariant — `sew-pcurve-parameter-desync-repair`)
description: A `PLANE`-hosted edge's 3D curve is a plain `LINE` from `(0,0,0)` to `(1,0,0)`, uniformly parametrized over `[0,1]`. expected_kernel_behavior: `BRepLib::SameParameter` detects the ill-conditioned knot ratio and reparametrizes by arc length rather than attempting a direct polynomial-domain approximation that would be numerically unstable at that scale.
notes: **See also**: Gp040 (this class's prior witness — a plain positional pcurve/3D-curve displacement, a different input shape from this fixture's knot-ratio ill-conditioning). This fixture covers the "ill-conditioned knot-ratio arc-length reparametrization" subvariant. **Scope note (evidence-based, honest deferral)**: the class is missing 3 of 4 subvariants; the packet asked for 2 of them. The OTHER missing subvariant ("a pcurve needing the relaxed second smoothing attempt after the first C0→C1 upgrade doesn't fully resolve, with a deliberate regression so the revert-on-regression path fires") requires distinguishing, from outside, WHICH internal retry branch `BRepLib::SameParameter` takes — no counter or diagnostic enum for "first pass" vs. "second, more relaxed pass" is exposed through OCCT's public API, so a STEP-input-only fixture cannot be verified (rather than merely asserted) to hit that specific branch instead of the ordinary single-pass smoothing Gp040 already demonstrates. category: §12.2a pcurve (sub-class: missing/failed pcurve deferred to projection, "listed pcurve fails to translate" subvariant — `stp-missing-pcurve-projection`)
description: A half-cylinder face (u in `[0,pi]`, v in `[0,1]`), the same 4-edge idiom as Gp035. The left seam edge's `SURFACE_CURVE` carries a correct 3D `LINE` plus a real, non-null `PCURVE` in `associated_geometry` — but that `PCURVE`'s `DEFINITIONAL_REPRESENTATION` `items` list references a `LINE` built from 3-coordinate (3D) `CARTESIAN_POINT`/`DIRECTION` entities instead of the 2-coordinate ones a pcurve's UV-space `LINE` requires — a wrong-dimensionality item, the kind of bug a producer's export code genuinely commits when it accidentally wires a 3D curve builder into a 2D pcurve slot. The other three edges (bottom arc, right seam, top arc) are correct `SURFACE_CURVE`s.
expected_kernel_behavior: the malformed pcurve item fails its per-item conversion; the edge-loop translation stage defers the edge and computes a correct pcurve by projecting the already-built 3D edge onto the face's surface.
notes: **See also**: Gp001, Gp035, Gp042 (the "no pcurve entity at all" trigger mode — already solid). Gp012 (struck as a bogus citation for this class per prior audit: its `SEAM_CURVE associated_geometry` contains `(#pc,$)`, a null `$` slot, which is the SAME "absent pcurve" mode as Gp001/Gp035/Gp042, not "a real pcurve reference that fails to translate"). This fixture is the first to encode the latter. **Empirical finding (live-verified, decisive; includes a discarded unsafe attempt)**: the obvious first construction — a `DEFINITIONAL_REPRESENTATION` item that is a totally wrong entity TYPE (a bare `CARTESIAN_POINT` standing in for a curve) — was built and tested first. A segfault is not a Python-catchable outcome — it kills the interpreter — so that construction was DISCARDED as unsafe for this corpus's live harness/CI and never shipped. The wrong-dimensionality `LINE` shipped here was verified safe (no crash under either healing profile) and, via `BRep_Tool::CurveOnSurface` on the translated shape, decisively confirmed to demonstrate the intended mechanism: the left seam edge's malformed pcurve item is silently dropped, and OCCT supplies a freshly-computed pcurve instead — sampled at `t=0.0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1.0`, the recovered pcurve is `u=0.0` constant with `v` running `0.0→1.0`, exactly the correct projected result for that physical edge (matching the healthy right-seam edge's own pcurve shape in Gp035).

description: An `EDGE_CURVE` bounding a real `ADVANCED_FACE` on a planar surface (P(u,v)=(u,v,0)) carries a `SURFACE_CURVE` whose sole `PCURVE` is a 2D `LINE` seeded at `(0.0, 0.5)` — v=0.5 — while the edge's 3D `LINE` genuinely lies at v=0.0 on the plane. The declared 2D parameter curve thus disagrees with the 3D geometry by 0.5 in the surface's V direction, far beyond the file's 1e-7 uncertainty. A strict "curve on surface" validator would reject this as an invalid pcurve.
expected_kernel_behavior: OCC's `STEPControl_Reader` discards the grossly-disagreeing declared pcurve and recomputes it from the 3D curve during transfer; the face builds cleanly with a pcurve at v=0. A strict validator instead rejects "invalid curve on surface".
notes: **Live-verified (2026-07-18, OCP/OCCT 7.8.1)** by reading the built edge's stored curve-on-surface: the recomputed pcurve is `(0,0)→(1,0)` (v=0, matching the 3D curve — NOT the declared v=0.5), with edge tolerance unchanged at 1e-7 (no tolerance inflation). Swept declared drift v=0.5/5/50/500 — **all** recompute to v=0 with `face:1`; there is **no tolerance boundary**, and the behaviour is identical under `heal_on` (`read.surfacecurve.mode=3`) and `heal_off` (`mode=0`). So OCC's STEP reader does not trust declared pcurves at all — it recomputes every one from the 3D curve, silently correcting producer-side pcurve errors on read. **Honest scope caveat:** because OCC absorbs the drift by recompute, this file builds `face:1` *identically to a clean face* — the heal is genuine and directly verifiable (by reading the built pcurve) but is INVISIBLE to the shape-count oracles; it is not mutation-visible. Retained as a genuine, directly-verified documentation of OCC's pcurve-recompute-on-read robustness for kernel grading (a grader should confirm its kernel builds the face AND recomputes the pcurve to v=0), and as the genuine face-hosted counterpart to P014 (which is byte-level provenance only). **See also**: P014, Gp010, Gp002.
reproducer: `PLANE` at origin (axis +Z, ref +X); 3D `LINE` edge (0,0,0)→(1,0,0); `PCURVE` on the plane whose 2D `LINE` seed is `(0.0, 0.5)` (drifted +0.5 in V); `SURFACE_CURVE` binding the two on one `EDGE_CURVE`; a single `ADVANCED_FACE`/`OPEN_SHELL`/`SHELL_BASED_SURFACE_MODEL`.

title: Pcurve 2D seed drifts in V from the 3D edge geometry; OCC heals by recomputing the pcurve from the 3D curve

category: §12.2a pcurves (sub-class: `tkshh-nonperiodic-bspline-seamlike-edge`, subvariant "non-B-spline base surface requiring approximation before periodicity can be set")
description: The CATIA like-seam idiom (a single `EDGE_CURVE` whose `SURFACE_CURVE` carries TWO `PCURVE`s on one and the same host surface, used twice with opposite orientations in one `EDGE_LOOP`) hosted on a `SURFACE_OF_LINEAR_EXTRUSION` swept 1.0 along +Z from a CLOSED but NON-PERIODIC `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` — 9 control points around a unit circle with the first pole equal to the last, degree 2, clamped knots. An extrusion inherits its periodicity from its basis curve, so this host wraps around in U while declaring no period, and it is not a B-spline surface. That combination is precisely what the subvariant names and what none of the existing fixtures can present: Gp013 and Gp181 are B-spline hosts (so no approximation is needed, and the reader has already periodized them by the time a shape exists), and Gp182's `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` is inherently periodic, so it can never require the approximation either.
expected_kernel_behavior: recognise that the host is closed in U but carries no declared period and cannot be periodized in place because it is not a B-spline; approximate it to a B-spline surface first, declare that surface periodic in U, migrate every pcurve to it, and merge across the like-seam edge — rather than treating the two pcurve banks as an ordinary non-seam duplication.
notes: Live-verified (2026-07-31, this worktree, OCP/OCCT 7.8.1) against this fixture's own bytes: the face reads back on a `Geom_SurfaceOfLinearExtrusion` with `IsUPeriodic() == False`, `IsUClosed() == True`, U bounds [0,1], and the reader does NOT periodize it — the direct contrast with Gp013 (`IsUPeriodic == True` straight out of the reader) and Gp181 (`IsVPeriodic == True`), both live-rechecked here, and with Gp182's cylinder (`IsUPeriodic == True` by construction). **Control**: the byte-identical construction with only the basis curve swapped for a `CIRCLE` reads back on a `Geom_SurfaceOfLinearExtrusion` with `IsUPeriodic() == True`, isolating the closed-but-non-periodic basis curve as the sole cause of the missing period. **HONEST LIMITATION — what this fixture does NOT show**: it supplies the input precondition (and is the only fixture in the class that genuinely does), but it does not independently demonstrate the unify-level repair firing, and no STEP file appears able to. That branch additionally needs `faces.Length() > 1` in one same-domain group plus an `EdgeWith2pcurves` — an edge carrying two pcurves on the reference face while NOT being really-closed in that face (`ShapeUpgrade_UnifySameDomain.cxx:3206-3214`) — and the two ways a STEP file can produce two pcurves are mutually exclusive with that. Route (a), the true-seam route, requires the same edge to appear TWICE in one `EDGE_LOOP` (`StepToTopoDS_GeometricTool.cxx:99-104`), which is what makes the reader call the two-pcurve `BRep_Builder::UpdateEdge` overload (`StepToTopoDS_TranslateEdgeLoop.cxx:611`, `:621`) — but an edge appearing twice in a face IS really-closed there, so `:3206` classifies it as a seam, `:3218` sets `SeamFound`, and `:3221` disables the branch. Route (b), the like-seam route, requires the edge to appear exactly ONCE (`StepToTopoDS_GeometricTool.cxx:136-146`) and stores only the SINGLE-pcurve overload per face (`StepToTopoDS_TranslateEdgeLoop.cxx:615`, `:625`); with both faces on the same surface and identity location the second call replaces the first, so no `BRep_CurveOnClosedSurface` is ever built and `BRep_Tool::IsClosed(edge, face)` stays false. Live-confirmed: a two-face variant of exactly this idiom (two half-faces on one shared host, the like-seam edge used once in each) was built and read in this worktree and came back with ZERO edges carrying two pcurves on their face, and `ShapeUpgrade_UnifySameDomain` with ConcatBSplines on and off produced identical output. **See also**: Gp013 (U-direction B-spline host), Gp181 (V-direction B-spline host), Gp182 (the earlier non-B-spline attempt, whose cylinder is inherently periodic — this fixture is its corrected successor and does not replace it). Synonyms: "extrusion of closed non-periodic curve", "surface wraps but declares no period", "like-seam on non-bspline host", "two pcurve banks non-periodic extrusion", "CATIA seam surface needs approximation". Provenance tier: bytes-sufficient.
reproducer: `SURFACE_OF_LINEAR_EXTRUSION('',#closed_nonperiodic_bspline_curve,#vector)` as the surface of an `ADVANCED_FACE`; one `EDGE_CURVE` whose `SURFACE_CURVE` lists TWO `PCURVE`s, both with `basis_surface` = that extrusion, one a 2D line at u=0 and one at u=1; that `EDGE_CURVE` referenced twice, with opposite `ORIENTED_EDGE` senses, in the face's single `EDGE_LOOP`, closed off by the two wrap-around `CIRCLE` edges at v=0 and v=1.

description: A `COMPOSITE_CURVE` traces the unit square with four `COMPOSITE_CURVE_SEGMENT`s, but lists them A, C, B, D — the top edge sits between the bottom edge and the right edge, so successive entries in the list do not follow on from one another, and the permutation is neither the identity nor a cyclic rotation (which on a closed wire would be a mere choice of starting point). Every segment's parent curve is a genuinely BOUNDED curve — a degree-1 `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` over a finite [0,1] domain — so each yields a real finite edge, unlike the infinite-parameter segments a bare `LINE` produces. The composite curve is the sole element of the shape representation's own curve set, so it is a real translation root, not an orphan.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect that the segment list is not in connected sequence, reorder the collected segments algorithmically before assembling them, log that the disorder was repaired, and emit a single wire — rather than building a disjoint or self-crossing wire in list order.
notes: **See also**: Gp176 (byte-genuine disordered composite curve in the container where the repair cannot be observed — this entry is its observable counterpart, not a duplicate), Twi007, Twi028, Twi038 (`EDGE_LOOP` edge-list scrambles, a different translation path), Ad137, Gp188 (composite-curve siblings). Live-verified (2026-07-31, this worktree, OCP/OCCT 7.8.1): the transfer check list carries exactly one message, the warning "Segments were disordered; fixed" — the literal string emitted when the reorder status comes back set — and the transfer yields ONE wire of 4 edges (8 raw vertices). Perturbation control (byte-level A/B): re-listing the same four unchanged segment entities in their connected order A, B, C, D — a single-token edit to the segment list, nothing else — makes the warning disappear entirely while the resulting topology is identical (1 wire, 4 edges, 8 vertices, zero check messages). The message is therefore caused by the segment ORDER alone, which is exactly what Gp176's own control could not establish, because in Gp176's configuration both orders produced the identical empty signature. Synonyms: "segments were disordered fixed", "composite curve segments out of sequence", "composite curve reorder", "successive segments do not follow on", "wire assembled from scrambled segments". Provenance tier: bytes-sufficient.
reproducer: four `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` of degree 1, knots `(0.0,1.0)`, multiplicities `(2,2)`: `seg_a_bottom` (0,0,0)→(1,0,0), `seg_b_right` (1,0,0)→(1,1,0), `seg_c_top` (1,1,0)→(0,1,0), `seg_d_left` (0,1,0)→(0,0,0); each wrapped in `COMPOSITE_CURVE_SEGMENT(.CONTINUOUS.,.T.,#crv)`; then `COMPOSITE_CURVE('composite_curve_scrambled_order',(#seg_a,#seg_c,#seg_b,#seg_d),.F.)` — note the A, C, B, D order — inside `GEOMETRIC_CURVE_SET('gp195_composite_set',(#composite))` in a `MANIFOLD_SURFACE_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION`.
sources: occt-coverage `exchange/problems.json` `stp-compcurve-reorder` (`StepToTopoDS_TranslateCompositeCurve::Init`, `StepToTopoDS_TranslateCompositeCurve.cxx:265-274` — `sfw->FixReorder()`, and `StatusReorder(ShapeExtend_DONE)` → the warning "Segments were disordered

fixed"). The verdict was held at PARTIAL because Gp176 could not be made to show the repair firing. Root cause identified live: Gp176 hands its composite curve to an `EDGE_CURVE` as `edge_geometry`, which routes through the single-curve conversion path and never constructs the segment-wise wire assembler at all (Gp176 reports " Make Geom_Curve (3D) failed" / "Could not convert a curve", and no reorder message, in either segment order). The assembler — and hence the reorder pass — is only reached when the composite curve is an ELEMENT of a curve set (`StepToTopoDS_Builder::Init(GeometricSet)`, `StepToTopoDS_Builder.cxx:677-698`).

description: A closed-cylinder face is bounded by the canonical four-entry loop — bottom circle, seam forward, top circle reversed, seam reversed — so the seam `EDGE_CURVE` is referenced TWICE inside the one `EDGE_LOOP`, the formal-seam encoding. Its geometry is a `SEAM_CURVE` carrying two DISTINCT `PCURVE`s, one per bank at u=0 and u=2π, but each of those pcurves' definitional representation holds a 2D `CIRCLE` rather than the usual 2D `LINE`. The two banks are then of a 2D curve kind from which no traversal direction can be extracted, so which bank is the forward one for this edge/wire/face orientation is genuinely indeterminate — and the receiver refuses to guess. Every prior fixture in this class (Gs193, Gp013, Gp011, Gs028, Twi022, Gp190) translates successfully; none reaches this branch. The seam edge's start and end vertices are deliberately distinct `VERTEX_POINT`s (z=0 and z=1) because a same-entity start/end (a full-circle seam, Gp011's shape) is swallowed by a separate equal-vertices recovery path and would hide the failure.
expected_kernel_behavior: when the two banks of a seam cannot be ordered, the edge is hard-failed and reported rather than silently assigned an arbitrary bank; the failure then propagates to the wire ("at least one edge failed") and the face is left without an outer bound, so nothing downstream inherits a guessed parametrisation.
notes: **See also**: Gs193, Gp011, Gp013, Gp190 (the formal-seam and pseudo-seam subvariants of this class, all of which succeed). Live-verified (2026-07-31, this worktree, OCP/OCCT 7.8.1): the transfer check list carries " Seam curve not mapped" TWICE — once per traversal of the twice-referenced seam edge — followed by " Edge with equal vertices failed, scipped" (the two full-circle boundary edges), "At least one edge failed : wire not done", " EdgeLoop not mapped to TopoDS" and "No Outer Bound : Face not done": exactly the cascade the cited lines predict. The transferred shape is therefore the cylinder face with no wire at all — `n_edges_total == 0`, `n_vertices_total == 0`, face area 8e+100 (the unbounded natural-surface placeholder). That placeholder IS the claim here, as for Tfa252, so this entry is listed in the tier-3 placeholder lint's intentional-placeholder set. Perturbation control (byte-level A/B): replacing each pcurve's 2D `CIRCLE` with a 2D `LINE` spanning the same two bank endpoints — nothing else changed — makes all six check messages vanish and the face translate normally (1 wire, 4 edges, 8 vertices, zero failures). Synonyms: "seam curve not mapped", "forward pcurve indeterminate", "which bank of the seam is forward", "seam edge hard fail", "two pcurves cannot be ordered", "non-linear seam pcurve rejected". Provenance tier: bytes-sufficient.
reproducer: `CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE` radius 1, axis +Z. Seam 3D geometry `LINE` (1,0,0)→(1,0,1). Each bank: `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_2D` at `(u_bank, 0.5)`, `CIRCLE('seam_bank_u0_circle_pcurve',#plc,0.5)` (and `seam_bank_u2pi_circle_pcurve` at u=2π) — both circles genuinely pass through their bank's two seam endpoints `(u_bank,0)` and `(u_bank,1)` — wrapped in `DEFINITIONAL_REPRESENTATION` + `PCURVE` on the cylinder. `SEAM_CURVE('',#line3d,(#pc_u0,#pc_u2pi),.PCURVE_S1.)`; `EDGE_CURVE('indeterminate_seam_edge',#v_bottom,#v_top,#seam,.T.)`; `EDGE_LOOP('',(#oe_bottom_circle,#oe_seam_T,#oe_top_circle_F,#oe_seam_F))` → `FACE_OUTER_BOUND` → `ADVANCED_FACE` → `OPEN_SHELL` → `SHELL_BASED_SURFACE_MODEL`.

description: A `RATIONAL_B_SPLINE_CURVE` (or surface) has a weights array whose length differs from the control-point list length, breaking reader contracts. OCCT's writer historically also emitted mismatched lengths.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal; pad weights with 1.0 / truncate to match pole count; warn. Do not crash. Writers must always emit len(weights) == len(poles).
notes: Both malformed rational entities (curve: 4 poles / 3 weights; surface: 4×4 net / 4×3 weight grid) are wired as members of a `GEOMETRIC_SET` (`#2`) reachable from the shape representation — they are genuinely part of the loaded model, not orphan definitions. **Live-oracle behaviour (OCCT 7.8.1, deterministic across reruns):** the parser accepts the file but the transfer stage silently DROPS both entities on the weight-count mismatch, so `occt` yields `shape_null` (empty); gmsh likewise yields empty. This is genuinely CAUSED by the defect: a well-formed control (curve 4 weights, surface 4×4 grid) built the same way yields a real edge+face (`occt=shape(1)`, face:1). So the fixture demonstrates the class by the observable empty-vs-nonempty contrast, not merely by byte presence. (An earlier version placed the malformed entities in an *unreferenced* `GEOMETRIC_CURVE_SET` beside a decoy point, which loaded a 1-vertex stub and demonstrated nothing — corrected 2026-07-17 to wire the defect carriers into the loaded model.) **See also**: Ad059. Synonyms: "rational B-spline weights count doesn't match poles", "weights array length differs from control points", "NbWeights ≠ NbControlPoints", "NURBS curve weight vector wrong length", "rational BSpline missing weight or has extra weight".
reproducer: Emit `RATIONAL_B_SPLINE_CURVE(..,(w0,w1,w2))` paired with a 2D/3D pole list of length 4; or surface analogue with rectangular weight grid having a missing row.

description: Long thin parts (e.g. 2.5 m extrusion with sub-mm helical features) export with visibly warped helical `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` because Creo's relative accuracy tessellates surfaces too coarsely on export. Typical signature: a B-spline approximating a tall helix carries only ~16 control points across z=0.2500, the poles zig-zag in x sign and barely move radially; severe under-sampling, far fewer poles per turn than a faithful helix needs. expected_kernel_behavior: reject the surface; refuse to materialize. At minimum, refuse to use it for projection or intersection. Validate magnitudes against bounding-box envelope.
notes: **See also**: Gs036. **OCC behavior**: OCC loads the file and produces no shape (empty). Re-audit (2026-07-18, empty-claim re-audit) shows the empty is not caused by the declared defect (out-of-range (1e100) NURBS control point): the model is one hand-authored ADVANCED_FACE (B-spline surface with per-edge SURFACE_CURVE/PCURVE) in an OPEN_SHELL that OCC's STEP transfer never builds into a TopoDS face. Base, a CLEAN copy with the injected C-1-break defect edge closed, and a fully well-formed copy (declared defect repaired, scaffold pcurve domains corrected) are all empty (f=0); a genuinely-building B-spline face fixture (Gn024) loads f=1. expected_kernel_behavior: reject the curve with a precise diagnostic; emit a warning; continue translating the remainder of the file.
notes: **See also**: Gn001, Gn003. **OCC behavior**: accepts with ERR diagnostic (empty result); outside catalog's allowed set ({reject, warn-and-proceed}). Kernel-bug witnessed: receivers must reject this fixture per the catalog's stated invariant. Synonyms: "B-spline surface single distinct knot", "BSpline knot vector collapses to one unique value", "empty parametric range from collapsed knots", "all knots equal produces empty domain", "BSpline curve with degenerate knot vector throws".
reproducer: `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS('',3,(#20,#21,#22,#23),.UNSPECIFIED.,.F.,.F.,(4,4),(0.0,0.0),.UNSPECIFIED.);`
title: BSpline curve whose knot vector collapses to a single unique value

description: `BOUNDED_PCURVE` is a degenerate subclass whose role is to give a bounded version of an otherwise infinite parametric basis curve. step-g loads the entity into the in-memory model fine, but the LoadONBrep path falls through to the base-class stub which prints `"not implemented for BoundedPCurve"` and returns false. Trims referencing a `BOUNDED_PCURVE` in their `associated_geometry` list lose the parametric curve in the ON_Brep representation, so the trim becomes 3D-only and is later re-projected numerically (introducing drift). Distinct from Gn019 (coincident-control-point degeneracy): this is a *type-dispatch* defect rather than a degeneracy.
expected_kernel_behavior: heal-and-accept; `BoundedPCurve::LoadONBrep` must defer to its underlying definitional basis curve and reparameterise to the bounded subrange; if unhandled, emit `W_BOUNDED_PCURVE_FALLBACK` and project from 3D.
notes: **See also**: Gn019, Twi100, Twi101. Synonyms: "BOUNDED_PCURVE LoadONBrep stub", "step-g BOUNDED_PCURVE drop", "BOUNDED_PCURVE subtype unimplemented".
reproducer: `#41=BOUNDED_PCURVE('bp_on_plane', #14, #40);` referenced from a `SURFACE_CURVE.associated_geometry`. step-g loads the entity; LoadONBrep stub returns false.
sender: Producers that emit a bounded re-parametrisation of an otherwise infinite parametric basis curve.
sources: BRL-CAD `src/conv/step/step-g/Curve.cpp` `LoadONBrep` base stub `"::LoadONBrep(..) not implemented for <entity>"`
`BoundedPCurve` is a non-overriding subclass that inherits the stub
bug-reporter language: "BOUNDED_PCURVE dropped on import", "step-g subtype unsupported", "BOUNDED_PCURVE falls through to base-class stub".
title: `BOUNDED_PCURVE` LoadONBrep stub (BRL-CAD step-g)
