description: A fillet between a planar face and a cylindrical face is emitted as a `B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS` cubic patch instead of an analytical `TOROIDAL_SURFACE`. Receivers (Onshape, Rhino) classify the result as "rounded edge" rather than "fillet feature" because they look for the `TOROIDAL_SURFACE` analytic type to recognize fillets as features for downstream chamfer/blend editing. Fusion 360 and FreeCAD itself recognise the geometry visually but lose the feature category.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: writer prefers the most-specific analytical surface type when geometry permits; receivers should heal feature classification by falling back to feature-recognition heuristics rather than relying on surface-type classification. Warn and accept with W_FEATURE_CLASSIFICATION_LOST when the analytical surface cannot be recovered.
notes: **See also**: P007. Synonyms: "fillet emitted as B-spline instead of torus", "Onshape sees rounded edge not fillet", "feature category lost on STEP export", "STEP fillet is bspline".
reproducer: STEP file where a fillet between a planar face and a cylindrical face is encoded as `B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS` instead of `TOROIDAL_SURFACE`.
sender: FreeCAD PartDesign Fillet on the boolean union of a Box + Cylinder.
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP export gives wrong results for fillets", "fillets are read incorrectly by Onshape, Rhino — rounded edge instead of fillet", "fusion and FreeCAD itself read it correctly".
title: Fillet faces re-import as rounded edge (Onshape/Rhino) but as fillet in producer

description: An imported STEP body whose `STYLED_ITEM` records bind colours to specific `ADVANCED_FACE` entity numbers loads with correct per-face colours, but adding an unrelated Part Cube to the document re-walks the OCAF tree and the per-session sub-shape pointer indices shift by one, leaving every coloured face referencing the wrong sub-shape. The on-disk symptom is a STEP whose `STYLED_ITEM` `item` attribute is `#NN` where `#NN` is the *N*-th `ADVANCED_FACE` in document-order, and the receiver's binding logic relies on order rather than on the entity number.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: receivers must bind styled-items by stable attributes (entity number or `name`), not by document-walk order. Index-based bindings that drift on document edits are a coverage gap; emit W_UNSTABLE_STYLE_BINDING and recover by re-binding to entity identity.
notes: **See also**: A018. Synonyms: "imported step colors scramble after edit", "STYLED_ITEM binding by index breaks on document change", "face colors get random after unrelated Part add", "color corruption non-reversible".
reproducer: STEP solid with 6 faces, each carrying a distinct `STYLED_ITEM` referencing a `COLOUR_RGB` — entity numbering deliberately interleaved so the document-order doesn't match entity-id order.
sender: FreeCAD STEP importer's `STYLED_ITEM` binding pass that uses per-session sub-shape pointers as the binding key.
sources: bug-reporter language: "Material/colors look right after import", "after any operation (even adding an unrelated Part Cube) colors get corrupted", "each face seems to get a random color and is non-reversible".
title: Imported STEP per-face colours scramble after any unrelated edit operation (style binding instability)

description: A LinearPattern of count=4 over an arc-shaped Pad yields a solid where the 4th instance's face normals are inverted relative to the first 3. The on-disk symptom is 4 `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`s where instances 1–3 have consistent `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` direction vectors but the 4th has its `axis` direction `(0.0, 0.0, -1.0)` instead of `(0.0, 0.0, 1.0)`. Pattern counts other than 4 reproduce the issue at counts 8, 12 (multiples of 4); suggesting a sign-bit overflow in the pattern's index-to-transform table.
expected_kernel_behavior: Heal and accept: writer builds the pattern transform table without sign-bit corruption; receivers should validate consistency of repeated-instance transforms within a pattern and emit a warning when an instance's axis flips relative to its siblings. Reject with E_PATTERN_INSTANCE_INCONSISTENT or warn-and-proceed by repairing the orientation; never silently accept inverted instances.
notes: **See also**: P018, A006. Synonyms: "LinearPattern of arc twisted on STEP export", "pattern instance count 4 corrupts orientation", "tessellation issue with arc pattern", "fourth instance is inverted".
reproducer: STEP file with 4 `MAPPED_ITEM`s referencing the same `REPRESENTATION_MAP`, where the 4th's `transformation_operator.axis` is `(0.0, 0.0, -1.0)` while instances 1–3 have `(0.0, 0.0, 1.0)`.
sender: FreeCAD PartDesign LinearPattern feature instantiated 4 times over an arc-shaped Pad.
sources: bug-reporter language: "Arc shape in linear pattern corrupted / twisted", "appears when number of slots = 4 but not other numbers", "tessellation issue, has workaround".
title: Linear pattern of arc-shaped feature emits twisted/corrupted faces in STEP

description: A cylindrical body decorated with a knurl (dense pattern of small triangular pockets) emits a STEP where some of the densely packed `ADVANCED_FACE`s along the knurl ridges are degenerate slivers whose `FACE_OUTER_BOUND` collapses to a near-zero-area loop. The receiver loads, validates each face individually as planar, but the dense cluster leaves several missing faces, producing visible "holes" in the surface when rendered; the kernel's writer-side de-duplication of co-incident vertices prunes faces below an internal area threshold.
expected_kernel_behavior: writer must not prune below-tolerance faces from the emitted shell; receivers should warn but include them.
notes: Synonyms: "knurl produces holes on STEP export", "dense feature cluster has missing faces", "small triangular faces dropped", "STEP non-manifold due to sliver faces".
reproducer: STEP solid with a `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` containing several `ADVANCED_FACE`s whose `FACE_OUTER_BOUND` `EDGE_LOOP` has 3 edges of length < 1e-3 forming a sub-tolerance triangle face that the receiver may prune.
sender: FreeCAD with knurled-cylinder PartDesign feature.
sources: bug-reporter language: "knurl exports fine to stl but step has holes in strange places", "import into a slicer shows holes", "with or without write parametric pcurves option both wrong".
title: Knurled body exports STEP with holes in surface (slicer reports non-manifold)

description: A body comprising a base + 30 thin parallel fins (each fin a 1 mm × 30 mm × 30 mm rectangular Pad) crashes the VRML writer in the tessellator and emits a misshapen STEP where the fins' inter-fin gap faces are paired with normals oriented inwards toward the gap (negative-volume slivers). Although the STEP writer doesn't crash, the fin-pair faces in the on-disk file have `FACE_OUTER_BOUND` orientation flags that don't agree with the surface normal direction.
expected_kernel_behavior: writer's tessellator handles fin arrays without crashing; receivers detect double-flipped orientation pairs and reject or heal.
notes: **See also**: P023. Synonyms: "fin array crashes export tessellator", "heatsink causes vrml crash and step misorientation", "tightly spaced parallel solids cause writer issues".
reproducer: STEP body containing 30 parallel thin `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`s arranged 1 mm apart along Y; some fin-pair faces have `FACE_OUTER_BOUND.orientation` `.F.` while the surface normal is also flipped — double-flip cancels but still produces the wrong sign on volume integral.
sender: FreeCAD heatsink-style PartDesign body with a tight linear array of thin fins.
sources: bug-reporter language: "When I export below simple model of a heatsink to VRML FreeCAD crashes", "Export to STEP or WEBGL goes without issues", "heatsink fins make exporter unhappy".
title: Heatsink-style fin array crashes export pipeline at faceted sub-shape boundary

description: A `TURNING_OPERATION` declares a radial depth-of-cut (e.g. 30 mm) that exceeds the stock cylinder's radius (12.5 mm on a 25 mm bar). The single-pass move passes through the spindle axis and out the far side, parting the workpiece with no support. The controller either crashes the tool against the chuck or severs the bar mid-cut. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 turning cut-through", "STEP-NC depth bigger than radius", "lathe op slices bar in half".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate depth-of-cut against stock geometry; reject as malformed or warn that the operation severs the workpiece.
notes: Synonyms: "AP238 turning cuts through stock", "lathe depth exceeds radius", "STEP-NC parting cut unintended", "turning depth-of-cut > workpiece radius".
reproducer: `TURNING_OPERATION` with a depth-of-cut `MEASURE_WITH_UNIT(POSITIVE_LENGTH_MEASURE(30.0), mm_unit)` on a workpiece whose stock-cylinder radius is 12.5 mm.
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP-NC turning cuts through part", "AP238 depth too deep on bar stock", "turn op parts the workpiece".
title: AP238 turning operation cut depth exceeds workpiece radius

description: A `TURNING_FINISHING_FACE` declares a feed_direction vector pointing OUTWARD (away from the spindle axis) where face-turning requires inward feed (toward the axis). The tool retracts during what should be the finishing pass, leaving uncut stock and a witness mark from the entry point. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 face-turning direction reversed", "STEP-NC feed_direction wrong sign", "turning finish pass goes outward".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate feed_direction against operation semantics for face-turning (must be inward); reject as malformed or warn.
notes: Synonyms: "AP238 face-turn feed reversed", "STEP-NC turning finishing direction wrong", "feed_direction outward on face turn", "lathe finish pass retracts not cuts".
reproducer: `TURNING_FINISHING_FACE` with `feed_direction = DIRECTION('feed_outward_WRONG',(1.0,0.0,0.0))` (outward +X) instead of inward (-X) toward the spindle axis.
sources: bug-reporter language: "STEP-NC face-turn feeds outward", "AP238 finishing pass leaves stock", "lathe retracts during finish cut".
title: AP238 turning_finishing_face with feed direction inverted

description: A `TURNING_ROUGHING` op declares a radial stepover (e.g. 4.0 mm) larger than the cutting tool's nose radius (0.8 mm). Each successive pass leaves an unsupported scallop the nose can't reach, producing a stair-stepped surface that the next pass either gouges or leaves visible. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 turning stepover > nose r", "STEP-NC roughing scallops", "lathe rough pass leaves steps".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate stepover against tool nose radius; warn or reject when the ratio leaves un-machinable scallops.
notes: Synonyms: "AP238 stepover gouge", "STEP-NC turning rough pass scallops", "stepover larger than nose radius", "lathe stair-step finish".
reproducer: a `TURNING_MACHINING_TOOL` with `nose_radius = 0.8` mm; a `TURNING_ROUGHING` op with `stepover = 4.0` mm.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP238 lathe stepover too big", "STEP-NC scallops between turn passes", "turning leaves stair-step".
title: AP238 turning_roughing stepover exceeds tool nose radius

description: A `TURNING_OPERATION` carries two contradictory feed-direction attributes: one says radial (X-axis), the other says axial (Z-axis). The controller has no way to decide whether to perform a face-turning or longitudinal-turning move; some implementations pick the first, some the second, some refuse. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 turning feed direction ambiguous", "STEP-NC radial-vs-axial feed conflict", "turning op declares two feed axes".
expected_kernel_behavior: detect contradictory feed-direction attributes; reject as malformed or pick a documented default and warn.
notes: Synonyms: "AP238 feed direction conflict", "STEP-NC turning has two feeds", "radial vs axial ambiguity", "turning operation feed axis undecidable".
reproducer: a `TURNING_OPERATION` populated with both `radial_feed = DIRECTION((1.0,0.0,0.0))` and `axial_feed = DIRECTION((0.0,0.0,1.0))` as separate non-null feed_direction-class attributes.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP238 turn op has two feed directions", "STEP-NC radial AND axial feed", "turning operation contradicts itself".
title: AP238 turning feed-direction ambiguous (radial vs axial conflict)

description: A `THREAD_TURNING` op declares a lead/pitch of 1.5 mm while the referenced thread feature's spec is M10x1.0 (pitch 1.0 mm). The controller cuts a thread whose pitch doesn't match the design intent; the mating fastener won't thread in. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 thread pitch mismatch", "STEP-NC thread-turn wrong lead", "M10x1 cut as M10x1.5".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate that thread-turning pitch matches the referenced thread feature's spec; reject as malformed or warn loudly.
notes: Synonyms: "AP238 thread pitch disagrees with spec", "STEP-NC thread-turn lead wrong", "thread feature vs op pitch mismatch", "lathe cuts wrong thread pitch".
reproducer: a `THREAD` feature with spec pitch 1.0 mm and a `THREAD_TURNING` op whose declared pitch is 1.5 mm; the two attributes refer to the same feature.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP238 thread pitch wrong", "STEP-NC cuts wrong thread", "thread won't engage mating part".
title: AP238 thread_turning pitch differs from thread-spec pitch

description: A `TURNING_OPERATION` targets a `WORKPIECE` that has no rotational-axis declaration (no spindle_axis, no axis_of_revolution placement). The controller has no axis to spin the stock around; turning is meaningless on a non-rotating workpiece. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 turn op on prismatic block", "STEP-NC missing rotation axis", "lathe op without spindle axis".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate that the workpiece declares a rotational axis when targeted by a turning operation; reject or warn.
notes: Synonyms: "AP238 turning prismatic part", "STEP-NC missing rotation axis on lathe op", "block targeted by turning operation", "turn op without spindle axis".
reproducer: a `WORKPIECE` declared with no axis_of_revolution; a `TURNING_OPERATION` whose workingstep mounts that workpiece.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP238 turning a block", "STEP-NC lathe op on non-rotating part", "turning workpiece has no spindle axis".
title: AP238 turning_operation on workpiece without rotation axis

description: A `MILLING_TOOLPATH` lists consecutive points spaced 12 mm apart while the tool diameter is 6 mm. Linear interpolation between samples leaves stock between passes; the toolpath has no implicit guarantee of contiguous engagement. Controllers either over-feed (gouging) or leave uncut islands. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 milling sample distance > tool dia", "STEP-NC toolpath skips", "uncut stock between samples".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate sample-density against tool diameter; warn or refine the path before emission.
notes: Synonyms: "AP238 toolpath sample gap > tool diameter", "STEP-NC sparse milling samples", "milling path discontinuity", "toolpath leaves uncut between points".
reproducer: a `MILLING_CUTTING_TOOL` with diameter 6 mm; a `MILLING_TOOLPATH` whose underlying `POLYLINE` has points 12 mm apart.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP238 toolpath samples too sparse", "STEP-NC milling skips between points", "uncut islands between toolpath samples".
title: AP238 milling_toolpath consecutive points spaced beyond tool diameter

description: A milling toolpath references two `MILLING_FEED_RATE` entities with different magnitudes (300 mm/min and 1200 mm/min) on consecutive segments, but no F-code transition / acceleration profile is declared. Controllers either snap discontinuously (over-shooting the corner) or silently use one rate for the entire path. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 feedrate step change", "STEP-NC missing acceleration profile", "milling F-code transition absent".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate that feedrate changes carry an explicit transition; warn or insert a default ramp.
notes: Synonyms: "AP238 feedrate jump no F-code", "STEP-NC milling no acceleration profile", "feed-rate change without transition", "milling F-word missing between segments".
reproducer: two `MILLING_OPERATION` entries in workplan order, the first with feed_rate 300 mm/min and the second with feed_rate 1200 mm/min, with no transition operation between them.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP238 feedrate jumps with no transition", "STEP-NC F-code missing", "milling feedrate snap from 300 to 1200".
title: AP238 milling_feed_rate varies along path with no F-code transition

description: A `DRILLING_OPERATION` declares a tool_axis vector tilted 30 degrees from the feature's hole-axis. The controller either drills a slanted hole (mismatching the design intent) or refuses the operation because the tool axis isn't normal to the feature face. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 drill operation tilted", "STEP-NC drill axis off normal", "drilling tool not perpendicular".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate tool_axis against the targeted feature's hole-axis; reject or warn.
notes: Synonyms: "AP238 drilling tilted axis", "STEP-NC drill not normal to face", "drilling op axis mismatch with feature", "drill operation skewed".
reproducer: a `ROUND_HOLE` whose locator's axis is `(0,0,1)`; a `DRILLING_OPERATION` whose `tool_axis` is `(0.5, 0.0, 0.866)` (30 deg tilt).
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP238 drill axis tilted", "STEP-NC drilling skewed hole", "drill not perpendicular to face".
title: AP238 drilling_operation tool axis not normal to feature face

description: A `BORING_OPERATION` declares a boring-bar tool diameter (15 mm) larger than the pre-drilled start-hole diameter (10 mm). The boring bar physically cannot enter the hole - the operation is impossible. The controller either crashes the tool against the workpiece face or refuses to plunge. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 bore tool too big for hole", "STEP-NC boring insertion impossible", "boring bar exceeds start-hole dia".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate that boring tool diameter is less than start-hole diameter; reject as infeasible.
notes: Synonyms: "AP238 boring tool larger than hole", "STEP-NC bore-bar won't fit", "boring insertion impossible", "tool diameter exceeds start-hole".
reproducer: a `ROUND_HOLE` of diameter 10 mm; a `BORING_TOOL` of diameter 15 mm referenced by a `BORING_OPERATION` targeting that hole.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP238 boring bar bigger than hole", "STEP-NC bore tool can't enter hole", "boring impossible".
title: AP238 boring tool diameter exceeds start-hole diameter

description: A `COOLANT_OPERATION` specifies through-spindle / through-tool coolant delivery, but the referenced milling tool has no internal-cooling channel attribute. Activating through-tool flood on a solid-shank tool either floods the spindle bearings or stalls the coolant pump. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 through-tool on solid endmill", "STEP-NC coolant capability mismatch", "coolant through tool with no channel".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate coolant-mode capability against tool attributes; reject incompatible combinations.
notes: Synonyms: "AP238 through-tool coolant on non-coolant tool", "STEP-NC coolant capability mismatch", "internal cooling not declared", "coolant through-tool stalls pump".
reproducer: a `MILLING_CUTTING_TOOL` declared without an `internal_cooling` attribute; a `COOLANT_OPERATION` with mode `.THROUGH_TOOL.` targeting that tool.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP238 through-tool coolant on solid shank", "STEP-NC coolant floods spindle", "tool has no internal channel".
title: AP238 coolant_operation requests through-tool flow on tool with no internal cooling

description: An `INSPECTION_PROBING` op's approach segment runs from the probe-storage position straight through the workpiece body to reach the touch point. The probe stylus shears or breaks. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 probe path through part", "STEP-NC inspection collision", "stylus crashes against workpiece".
expected_kernel_behavior: collision-check probe paths against workpiece envelope; reject the op or warn loudly.
notes: Synonyms: "AP238 probe collision", "STEP-NC inspection path crashes", "probe stylus shears", "inspection trajectory through workpiece".
reproducer: an `INSPECTION_PROBING` op whose probe path `POLYLINE` runs from `(50,50,200)` to `(50,50,-5)` while the workpiece body occupies the box `(0.100, 0.100, 0.50)`.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP238 probe crashes into part", "STEP-NC inspection path collides", "stylus shears off".
title: AP238 inspection_probing path passes through workpiece body

description: A `TOUCH_PROBING` op declares a measurement tolerance of 0.005 mm while the touch probe's stylus tip ball diameter is 4.0 mm (radius 2.0 mm). The stylus radius compensation cannot resolve features below the tip radius - the declared tolerance is fundamentally unattainable with this probe. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 probe tolerance < stylus radius", "STEP-NC inspection resolution impossible", "touch probe tip too big".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate measurement tolerance against probe stylus radius; reject as unattainable or warn.
notes: Synonyms: "AP238 probe tolerance below stylus", "STEP-NC touch probe over-spec'd", "inspection resolution exceeds probe capability", "stylus diameter exceeds tolerance".
reproducer: a `TOUCH_PROBE` with stylus diameter 4.0 mm; a `TOUCH_PROBING` op with tolerance 0.005 mm referencing that probe.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP238 probe tolerance below stylus", "STEP-NC inspection unattainable resolution", "touch probe can't resolve sub-radius features".
title: AP238 touch_probing tolerance smaller than probe stylus radius

description: An `INSPECTION_RESULT` records a `measurement_uncertainty` of 0.05 mm against a feature whose design tolerance is +/-0.02 mm. The measurement is statistically incapable of confirming or denying conformance - it tells you nothing. Reporting it as "in spec" or "out of spec" is misleading. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 inspection uncertainty > tolerance", "STEP-NC gauge R&R insufficient", "measurement uncertainty exceeds feature tol".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate that measurement uncertainty is below feature tolerance; reject as gauge-incapable or warn.
notes: Synonyms: "AP238 gauge R&R insufficient", "STEP-NC inspection uncertainty exceeds tol", "measurement uncertainty too large", "gauge can't resolve feature tolerance".
reproducer: a `PLUS_MINUS_TOLERANCE` of +/-0.02 mm on a feature; an `INSPECTION_RESULT` with `measurement_uncertainty = 0.05` mm against the same feature.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP238 measurement uncertainty exceeds tol", "STEP-NC inspection meaningless", "gauge can't resolve tolerance".
title: AP238 inspection_result measurement uncertainty exceeds feature tolerance

description: A `WORKPIECE_COMPLETE_FOR_NC` entity is declared with an empty clamping_position list. AP238 requires that workpieces be tied to their fixturing for collision-checking; an unfixed workpiece cannot be safely machined. The controller has nothing to enforce keep-out zones against. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 workpiece-complete missing clamps", "STEP-NC no fixturing references", "workpiece floats with no clamping".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate that workpiece-complete entries declare at least one clamping reference; reject as malformed.
notes: Synonyms: "AP238 fixturing absent", "STEP-NC clamps missing on workpiece", "workpiece-complete with empty clamping list", "no keep-out zones declared".
reproducer: `WORKPIECE_COMPLETE_FOR_NC('finished_part',$,$,$,$,$,$,(),$)` - empty parenthesised clamping list.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP238 workpiece has no clamps", "STEP-NC fixturing missing", "no keep-out zones for collision check".
title: AP238 workpiece_complete_for_nc missing required clamping references

description: A sequence of `SETUP_INSTRUCTION` entities (mount fixture, locate workpiece, tighten clamps) carries time_stamps in non-monotonic order: instruction A at 09:00, B at 08:30, C at 09:15. Either the publisher copied stamps from a different job or the operator instructions were re-ordered without updating times. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 setup-instruction order wrong", "STEP-NC setup timestamps backwards", "operator step time goes back".
expected_kernel_behavior: warn-and-accept; validate timestamp monotonicity along setup-instruction sequence and emit a diagnostic on inversions.
notes: Synonyms: "AP238 setup-instruction time inversion", "STEP-NC operator steps non-monotonic", "setup chronology wrong", "instruction timestamps decreasing".
reproducer: three `SETUP_INSTRUCTION` entities with timestamps `2026-05-02T09:00:00`, `2026-05-02T08:30:00`, `2026-05-02T09:15:00` (non-monotonic).
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP238 setup steps out of order", "STEP-NC setup timestamps wrong", "operator instructions go backward in time".
title: AP238 setup_instruction sequence with non-monotonic time stamps

description: A `WORKPIECE_SETUP`'s placement axes are rotated 17.3 degrees about the machine Z-axis with no rotational fixturing declared. The machine cannot drive its X/Y stages along the workpiece's local axes; every toolpath issues compound moves that exceed acceleration limits. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 workpiece-setup rotation without rotary axis", "STEP-NC setup not aligned to machine", "workpiece coords skewed".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate workpiece-setup orientation against machine axes when no rotary stage is declared; warn or reject.

reproducer: `WORKPIECE_SETUP` whose `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` x-axis is `DIRECTION((0.9550, 0.2974, 0.0))` (17.3 deg rotation), with no rotary fixturing referenced.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP238 workpiece setup rotated", "STEP-NC setup not square to machine", "fixture skew without rotary axis".
title: AP238 workpiece_setup coordinate system not aligned with machine axes

The workplan has no valid topological order; consumers either deadlock during scheduling or pick an arbitrary order that breaks the dependency. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 executable_relationship cycle", "STEP-NC dependency graph cyclic", "workplan deadlock from circular precedes".

Tool manufacturer's rated chip-load for a 6 mm carbide cutter at this RPM is closer to 0.04 mm per tooth; the tool will fracture. Bug-reporter language: "AP238 feedrate × rpm too high", "STEP-NC chipload exceeds tool max", "feed-per-tooth × spindle exceeds envelope".
expected_kernel_behavior: validate feedspeed product against tool-family envelope; warn loudly or reject.

reproducer: `MACHINING_TOOL_FEEDSPEED` with spindle_speed 12000 rpm, feed_per_tooth 0.10 mm, on a 4-flute carbide end-mill rated for 0.04 mm/tooth at that RPM.
sources: bug-reporter language: "AP238 chipload too aggressive", "STEP-NC feed-per-tooth above max", "tool will fracture from rpm × ipt".
title: AP238 machining_tool_feedspeed product exceeds tool envelope

Bug-reporter language: "AP238 knurl finer than tool", "STEP-NC knurling pitch impossible", "knurl spec below tool resolution".

description: The transferred shape is a `GEOMETRIC_CURVE_SET` whose items are twelve valid `LINE` curves tracing the outline of a 10 mm cube. There is no topological superstructure of any kind — no `VERTEX_POINT`, `EDGE_CURVE`, `EDGE_LOOP`, `ADVANCED_FACE`, `CLOSED_SHELL`, or `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`. Every item is a legal `geometric_select` curve and the file is well-formed, so OCC transfers the set cleanly to a single `COMPOUND` holding 12 free edges — there is no solid, face, or wire. A consumer that reports "import OK" without noticing the empty solid set hands a boolean / meshing / mass-property pipeline nothing to operate on. This is a completeness defect (wireframe delivered where a solid was expected), *not* corruption — distinct from M051 (`GEOMETRIC_CURVE_SET` aggregating schema-illegal non-geometric children, which crashes OCC with signal 11) and M058 (curve set carried inside an AP203-tag/AP214-entity schema-mismatch file).
expected_kernel_behavior: accept, but surface the wireframe-only nature (warn / expose a subshape inventory showing zero solids and zero faces); LOTAR/downstream solid-expecting pipelines must not treat a curve-only import as a successful solid import.
notes: Synonyms: "wireframe-only STEP has no solid", "curve set imports as loose edges not a solid", "GEOMETRIC_CURVE_SET with no topology", "geometry present but no faces or shells", "cube delivered as wireframe". **See also**: M051, M058, M190, M192.
reproducer: a `GEOMETRIC_CURVE_SET` listing 12 `LINE` entities (the edges of a cube), wrapped in a `MANIFOLD_SURFACE_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION` under the canonical PRODUCT chain; emit no topological entities at all.
sources: SASIG PDQ non-geometric enumeration (geometry-completeness / "wireframe-only export" class)

title: Isolated wireframe: `GEOMETRIC_CURVE_SET` of a cube's 12 edges with no topology (no solid root)

description: The transferred shape is a `GEOMETRIC_SET` whose items are eight bare `CARTESIAN_POINT`s (the corners of a 10 mm cube). There are no curves, no surfaces, and no topological entities — the model is a pure zero-dimensional point cloud. Every item is a legal `geometric_select` point and the file is well-formed, so OCC transfers the set to a single `COMPOUND` holding 8 free vertices: vertices exist but edge, face, and solid counts are all zero. A consumer expecting bounded geometry receives nothing to bound. Distinct from the wireframe class (M191, curves → edges) and from the curve-set crash/mismatch fixtures (M051 non-geometric children → signal 11; M058 schema mismatch): the input here is legal and point-only.
expected_kernel_behavior: accept, but surface the point-only nature (warn / expose a subshape inventory showing only vertices); a point-cloud import must not be reported as a solid/surface import to solid-expecting consumers.
notes: Synonyms: "point cloud STEP has no geometry to bound", "GEOMETRIC_SET of points imports as loose vertices", "reference points only no solid", "scan points delivered as model", "part delivered as point cloud". **See also**: M051, M190, M191.

description: A tessellated face declares a link to its exact-geometry counterpart, but that counterpart, while a real and well-formed face entity present in the file, is never itself built as part of the model because nothing else in the model's shell/solid structure reaches it. The declared link therefore resolves to nothing at read time, and the reader quietly substitutes an empty face carrying only the mesh data in its place — a face with triangle geometry attached but no underlying continuous surface at all.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject a tessellated face whose declared exact-geometry link cannot be resolved, or heal by substituting a diagnosed placeholder surface; never silently emit a mesh-bearing face with no surface behind it and no diagnostic distinguishing it from a legitimately surfaceless mesh.
notes: Synonyms: "tessellated face dangling geometric link", "unresolved exact-geometry counterpart falls back to empty face", "mesh face with no B-rep surface behind it", "surfaceless face from unbound tessellation link". Live-verified: loads cleanly as a single face whose surface kind reports as unrecognized and whose validity check reports invalid for lacking a surface, confirming the fallback path fires exactly as described. A minimal control with the identical layout but an entirely absent link (rather than a populated-but-unresolvable one) reaches the identical unrecognized-surface, invalid-check outcome — since any tessellated face with no attached exact-geometry counterpart takes this same empty-face path, the unresolvable-versus-absent distinction only shows up in the file bytes, never downstream. The independent mesh-processing oracle used alongside the primary kernel crashes on this fixture and on the absent-link control identically — that crash is a property of any surfaceless mesh-only face reaching that oracle at all, not of the unresolvable-link mechanism this entry targets (isolated by testing both variants). See also: M022 (absent link, not unresolvable; also shares one coordinate list across six faces, which independently crashes this build regardless of link content).
reproducer: `TRIANGULATED_FACE` whose `geometric_link` attribute is populated with a reference to a syntactically valid `ADVANCED_FACE` entity that is fully defined in the file (its own `PLANE`/`EDGE_LOOP` boundary) but never appears inside any `CLOSED_SHELL`/`OPEN_SHELL`/`MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` reachable from the model's shape representation; own `COORDINATES_LIST` for the tessellated item (not shared with any other tessellated item); wired directly as the sole item of a `MANIFOLD_SURFACE_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION` rather than nested inside a `GEOMETRIC_SET`/`GEOMETRIC_CURVE_SET` wrapper, which independently destabilizes this reader build for any tessellated content regardless of link resolution (live-verified on a minimal control).
sources: StepToTopoDS_TranslateFace.cxx:718-738 (unresolved geometric_link falls back to a fresh empty face with the has-geometry flag cleared, via a lookup against the transient-process binder map rather than a recursive translate of the linked entity)
title: Tessellated face's declared exact-geometry link points at a real but never-built face, reader substitutes a surfaceless mesh face

The declared link resolves to nothing at read time, and the reader quietly builds a brand-new shell from the tessellated shell's own mesh items instead of substituting the intended precise topology.
expected_kernel_behavior: reject a tessellated shell whose declared topological link cannot be resolved, or heal by substituting a diagnosed placeholder shell; never silently rebuild an unrelated fresh shell from mesh data alone without flagging that the intended precise topology was never actually used.
notes: **See also**: M195. description: A bare geometric set aggregates items beyond curve/surface/point — here a placement entity alongside an ordinary curve. Per-item type dispatch inside the reader recognizes the curve and builds a live edge from it; the placement entity matches none of the directly-supported kinds, falls through to a last-resort general path that has no way to turn a bare placement into geometry, and is silently dropped with nothing surfaced to the consumer about the item that went missing.
expected_kernel_behavior: accept the supported item, but surface a diagnostic naming which item(s) in the set could not be interpreted as geometry rather than dropping them without a trace; never report a partial result as a complete transfer.
notes: Synonyms: "geometric set mixed item silently skipped", "unsupported representation item dropped from geometric set", "placement entity in geometric curve set produces no shape", "bare geometric set partial transfer no diagnostic". Live-verified: the result is exactly the circle's one edge and nothing attributable to the placement — the mixed-dispatch mechanism fires cleanly. Mirrors M051, whose supported item was an unbounded line: an unbounded line placed bare inside this kind of set crashes this reader build on its own, with or without a second mixed-in item (isolated by testing an unbounded-line-only set against this same wrapper, independently of any placement entity) — an unrelated instability in how the reader turns an untrimmed infinite line into an edge inside this context, not a symptom of the mixed-item dispatch this entry targets. Swapping in a bounded curve isolates the dispatch-skip behavior cleanly.
reproducer: `GEOMETRIC_CURVE_SET` whose items list mixes one `CIRCLE` (a supported curve, bounded/periodic so it survives the reader's curve path without incident) and one `AXIS2_PLACEMENT_3D` (a placement entity, not a geometric_select member); wired directly as the sole item of a `MANIFOLD_SURFACE_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION`.
sources: StepToTopoDS_Builder.cxx:636-775 (per-item type dispatch inside the geometric-set builder: curve/point/surface each get a dedicated path

anything else that is still a generic geometry-representation item is routed through a last-resort general-purpose transfer, and a bare placement entity produces no shape there, so it is silently omitted from the result with only a warning).
title: Bare geometric set mixing a supported curve with an unsupported placement entity: the placement is silently skipped, the curve translates normally

description: A faceted polygon boundary lists its points as a flat, closable loop. When the very same point entity appears twice in a row, building an edge between that pair would produce a zero-length edge with no useful geometry. Instead of doing that, the reader recognizes the immediate repeat and simply omits that one segment, so the resulting boundary is the honest polygon with the redundant vertex silently absorbed rather than a polygon with a degenerate stub edge in it.
expected_kernel_behavior: recognize and skip the degenerate repeated-point segment, closing the loop across the gap; or reject the boundary as malformed if zero-length segments are not tolerated at all — either way, never silently build a zero-length edge into the result.
notes: Synonyms: "faceted polygon repeats a point twice in a row", "degenerate polygon segment silently skipped", "same point entity referenced consecutively in a poly loop", "faceted brep avoids a zero-length edge from a duplicate vertex reference". Live-verified: the resulting boundary has exactly four edges (not five), area exactly matching the intended unit square, and the validity check reports the face as fully valid — confirming the redundant reference was cleanly absorbed rather than producing a corrupt loop. Mirrors M055, which uses four distinct points on a deliberately non-planar surface to test a different problem (the schema-illegal non-planar-face path); this entry keeps the surface planar and duplicates one point reference instead, isolating the degenerate-segment skip from the non-planar check.
reproducer: `FACETED_BREP` referencing a `CLOSED_SHELL` containing one `ADVANCED_FACE` on a `PLANE` whose `FACE_OUTER_BOUND` is a `POLY_LOOP` listing five point references for a four-corner unit square, where the second corner's point entity is listed twice in immediate succession (positions 2 and 3 of the flat point list both cite the same `CARTESIAN_POINT`).
sources: StepToTopoDS_TranslatePolyLoop.cxx:117-119 (consecutive-point comparison is by entity identity, not coordinate equality
a repeat is skipped with a bare loop continue, leaving the running "previous point" unmoved so the next distinct point closes the gap cleanly).
title: Faceted polygon boundary repeats the same point reference twice in a row; the reader skips the resulting zero-length segment instead of building a degenerate edge

description: Tessellated triangle geometry can be packed as a strip — a running list of vertex indices where each new index combines with the previous two to form one triangle — rather than as a flat list of independent triangles. When a strip's running window repeats a vertex, the candidate triangle it would form has zero area. The reader detects this collapse and leaves that one triangle out of the built mesh entirely, while the rest of the strip continues to build normally.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect and exclude the collapsed triangle from the built mesh, leaving the rest of the strip intact; never emit a zero-area triangle or leave an uninitialized triangle slot in its place.
notes: Synonyms: "triangle strip repeats a vertex index", "collapsed strip triangle silently excluded", "degenerate triangle omitted from packed strip mesh", "tessellated strip skip guard". Live-verified by inspecting the built mesh directly: it carries exactly one triangle, the well-formed one from the strip's first three indices, with the collapsed second candidate cleanly absent rather than present with garbage data. Mirrors M005, a plain flat-list tessellated face (the wrong packing mode entirely) whose repeated-index triple reaches no such guard at all and instead crashes downstream from an undefined per-vertex normal; rebuilt here in the packed strip form so the skip guard genuinely has something to fire on. A triangle-fan encoding of the same idea was tried and rejected: the fan variant's array-sizing pass does not reapply the same skip check the fill pass uses, so a collapsed fan triangle leaves an uninitialized triangle slot behind rather than being cleanly excluded — the strip encoding avoids that confound.
reproducer: `COMPLEX_TRIANGULATED_FACE` (the strip/fan-capable tessellated-face variant, not the plain-list variant) over a four-node unit-square `COORDINATES_LIST`, with one `triangle_strips` entry `(1,2,3,3)` — a strip whose last two positions repeat vertex index 3.
sources: StepToTopoDS_TranslateFace.cxx:181-198,341-356 (strip processing walks the index array pairwise, checking each new vertex against both of its immediate predecessors in the strip before emitting a triangle
the array-sizing pass that runs first reapplies the identical check, so the allocated triangle count matches what actually gets filled, leaving no uninitialized slot).
title: Triangle-strip index list repeats a vertex within one triple; the reader silently excludes the collapsed triangle instead of misreading or crashing on it

description: A tessellated face can declare a single per-face normal (one row, applied to every node) instead of one normal per node. When that one row does not have exactly the three components an XYZ vector needs, the reader does not try to interpret whatever values are present, nor does it reject the face — it simply leaves the mesh's per-node normal storage allocated but never actually filled with the row's values, so every node keeps its zero-initialized default rather than the malformed vector.
expected_kernel_behavior: detect the malformed row width and either reject the face or clearly diagnose that normals were dropped; never silently allocate normal storage that is never actually populated, since a consumer that checks "has normals" without checking the values gets a false positive.
notes: Synonyms: "tessellated normals row wrong component count", "malformed normal row silently ignored", "per-node normal storage allocated but never filled", "four-component normal row dropped without diagnostic". Live-verified by inspecting the built mesh directly: it reports normals as present, but reading any individual node's normal value raises a construction error because the stored vector is still all zeros — direct confirmation that the malformed row was never actually copied in, only its presence flag survived. Mirrors Bo027, whose per-vertex normal rows are well-formed three-component rows that merely disagree in value across a shared edge — a different defect (value disagreement, not row width) — by malforming the row's component count instead of its value.
reproducer: `TRIANGULATED_FACE` whose normals table is a single row of four components `(0.,0.,1.,0.)` instead of three, over a three-point `COORDINATES_LIST` triangle; wired directly as the sole item of a `MANIFOLD_SURFACE_SHAPE_REPRESENTATION`.
sources: StepToTopoDS_TranslateFace.cxx:123-131 (the normals table's row width is checked once, up front, against the required three components
any other width returns immediately, before the per-node assignment loop that would otherwise copy the row's values into the mesh ever runs).
title: Tessellated face's per-face normal row has the wrong number of components; the reader silently leaves every node's normal unset rather than misreading the row

Bug-reporter language: "contiguous edges mismatched length", "free edge pair length differ", "non-unit DIRECTION breaks parameterization".

reproducer: Two LINE/VECTOR pairs both running between the same two 3D points, one along a unit DIRECTION and one along a non-unit DIRECTION — so parameterized lengths differ even though 3D extents match.
sender: deduced — OCCT uncovered-class sweep
title: FindContigousEdges: paired LINEs/VECTORs from sewing have unequal parameter lengths (unit vs non-unit DIRECTION) for the same 3D extent
